compendium.big_tower.title: Cooling towers
compendium.blast_furnace.text:
The **blast furnace** (**5×4×5**) is a tilting melting furnace on two bearing stands. While it works it tilts and pours the melt into the ladle. The signal tower on the control cabinet shows **green** when idle, **yellow** while working and **red** when the output is full.
## Recipes
**Steel**: 8 iron ingots + 8 coal or coke (second input) make 8 steel ingots (10 s, 3,600 FE/t). Same cost as in the Small Parts Assembler, only much faster
**Raw ore and dust**: 8 raw iron, raw copper or raw gold or 8 iron, copper or gold dust make 8 ingots (10 s, 3,600 FE/t). Same yield as a furnace
**Lead block**: 34 lead ingots make 1 block (8 s, 3,000 FE/t)
**Atomic hull plate**: 4 netherite or atomic alloy + 4 lead shielding (second input) make 1 plate (12 s, 4,500 FE/t)
**Refined glowstone ingot**: 4 glowstone dust + 1 osmium (second input) make 1 ingot (10 s, 3,600 FE/t)
**Experience**: taking ingots from the ladle gives experience like a furnace for the same ingot, otherwise 0.5 per item. Items taken out by pipes give none
## Setup
Kit from the **Heavy Assembler**, placed like any machine. Material into the scrap bin in the back, ingots from the ladle in front, power and data cables at the control cabinet.
compendium.blast_furnace.tip: The blast furnace works in batches: steel, ore and dust always need 8 pieces at once. For single ingots the Small Parts Assembler remains.
compendium.blast_furnace.title: Blast Furnace
compendium.brief.title: FACT SHEET
compendium.build.hint: Drag: rotate · Right-drag: move · Wheel: zoom
compendium.build.hint.data: Connect a data cable between the data ports, or place the device right next to the rack.
compendium.build.portshint: Hover a port to see what it is for
compendium.build.tip.pipe: Connect a pipe to both ports.
compendium.catalog_all.text: All items by the place where they are made first. Gray = never had it yet, click opens the page.
compendium.catalog_all.title: All Items
compendium.chem_electrolysis.text:
## Electrolyzer (3×3×3)
Electrolysis cell with two gas columns: 1 mB **water** → 1 mB **hydrogen** and 0.5 mB **oxygen**
**2 mB/t** hydrogen and 1 mB/t oxygen at **2,400 FE/t**
**Water in**, hydrogen and oxygen **out** at the two gas ports (names in the hologram), power as there
Without water, power or room in one of the gas tanks the cell stands still
Hydrogen and oxygen are the gases of the oxyhydrogen chain
compendium.chem_electrolysis.tip: The gases move on by pipe. The deuterium separator makes a different gas from water.
compendium.chem_electrolysis.title: Electrolyzer
compendium.chem_fuel_cell.text:
## Fuel cell (3×3×3)
Cell block with two gas columns, the counterpart of the electrolyzer: **hydrogen** and **oxygen** (2 : 1) → **power**
**15 mB/t** hydrogen and 7 mB/t oxygen give **15,000 FE/t** (the electrolyzer needs 18,000 FE/t for that)
**Hydrogen in** (right, bottom, seen from the front) and **oxygen in** (left, top) at the two gas ports, **power out** at the back right (names in the hologram)
No storage: what the consumer does not take in the same tick is lost. Without gas the cell stands still
compendium.chem_fuel_cell.tip: Useful as emergency power: fill the gas tanks while power is spare, burn it when the grid fails.
compendium.chem_fuel_cell.title: Fuel cell
compendium.chips_chain.text:
Chips are the heart of every later machine. They are made from **silicon**, which you get in three steps, and come in three tiers.
## The chain
1. **Foundry**: 4 sand and 1 coal make 2 **raw silicon** (10 s, 3,000 FE/t)
2. **Chemical lab**: 3 raw silicon and 300 mB sulfuric acid make 2 **pure silicon** (12 s, 2,700 FE/t)
3. **Foundry**: 2 pure silicon make 4 **wafers** (10 s, 3,300 FE/t)
## The three chips
**Chip I**: wafer, copper ingot and 2 redstone, made in the **micro assembler** (4.6 s)
**Chip II**: chip I, pure silicon, rubber, 2 **photoresist** and 2 gold, made in the **Soldering Machine** (8 s)
**Chip III**: chip II, 3 pure silicon, ender pearl, diamond, 2 gold and **HDPE sheet**, made in the **clean room** with a robot arm (14 s)
Photoresist and HDPE sheet come from the **polymer plant**, made from naphtha and ethylene of the oil chain
## What for
The **controller** of later machines needs a chip matching the tier of its control board: repository chip I; component, compute and particle assembler, clean room, deuterium separator, electrolyzer, fuel cell and decon dock chip II; fast breeder, fusion reactor, quantum computer and weapons material plant chip III
**RAM modules**, **CPU modules**, **Exo Cores** and **Exo Modules** need chips too: the higher the tier, the better the chip
All machines up to the chemical lab, including the reactor assembler, need **no** chip, because there is no silicon before it
compendium.chips_chain.tip: Without chip II or III you get stuck: build the foundry and the chemical lab early and let the silicon run automatically.
compendium.chips_chain.title: Silicon and Chips
compendium.clean_room.text:
The **clean room** is a dust-free precision chamber (**3×3×3**). It makes **chip III** and the highest RAM and CPU tiers. It **only runs with a docked robot arm**, so nobody touches the parts. How to do it is explained under **Robot Arm Docking**.
## What it makes
**Chip III**
**CPU modules** with 32, 64 and 128 cores
**RAM modules** with 32, 64 and 128 GB
## Setting up
1. Make the **kit** in the **Heavy Assembler** (among others control board III, RAM and CPU module, casing and ports; 5,760 FE/t)
2. The **controller** comes from the Reactor Assembler and needs a **chip II**
3. Place it like any kit (hologram, right click)
## Operation
**1,920 FE/t** while crafting, one part takes **10 seconds** (a recipe may have its own values), energy storage **1,200,000 FE**
**Power** on the right (west, seen from the front), **items in** on top, **result out** on the left (east), right click on the controller opens the 3×3 grid
A **robot arm** must be docked: its target is inside the chamber and it stands at most 7 blocks away. It brings chip II, pure silicon and the other parts from the previous machine
There is no computer bonus
compendium.clean_room.tip: Plan a chest or machine in front of the clean room for the arm to take parts from. Without an arm nothing happens.
compendium.clean_room.title: Clean Room
compendium.cnc_mill.text:
The **CNC mill** (**2×2×3**) is a gantry mill: the table moves back and forth, the spindle head moves over the workpiece and the spindle turns while it works. It uses a **3×3 grid** like the micro assembler; the position in the grid does not matter, only the amounts count.
## Only here
**HDPE seal**: 8 HDPE sheets + 4 glass seals
**Osmium heat plate**: 30 osmium + 8 steel sheets
**Obsidian composite plate**: 4 refined obsidian + 8 steel sheets
**Lead shielding**: 61 lead + 4 steel sheets
**Advanced reactor casing**: 4 reactor casings + 2 osmium heat plates + 1 lead shielding make 4
## Also in the Small Parts Assembler
**Steel sheet**, **reactor plate** and **reactor casing** work in both machines with the same recipe.
## Setup
1. Make the **kit** in the **Small Parts Assembler**: 2 control boards I, 8 reactor casings, one power and one data port, 2 item ports, 8 steel sheets, 4 copper coils and 4 diamonds
2. Place it like any kit (hologram, right-click)
## Operation
**480 FE/t** while milling, one part takes **2.5 seconds**, energy buffer **120,000 FE**
**Power** low on the back of the supply block, **parts in** on top of the supply block, **result out** on the left of the supply block, data cable high on the back of the supply block.
compendium.cnc_mill.tip: The CNC mill comes right after the plate mill. Without it there is no HDPE seal, and the acid plant and the chemistry lab need those.
compendium.cnc_mill.title: CNC Mill
compendium.component_assembler.text:
The Component Assembler (**5×4×5**) builds for the digital storage: you order at the **Storage Terminal**, it takes the ingredients from the racks and puts the result back.
## Setup
Kit from the Heavy Assembler, controller from the Reactor Assembler
Power on the right (west, seen from the front), **1,440 FE/t** per working core
**Data cable** to the controller or a port, on the same network as racks and terminal
The item input on top accepts items and stores them right away; on the left only comes out what found no room in the racks
## Pattern cards
The Small Parts Assembler makes blank cards
In the menu, lay out the recipe as a **template** on the left (ghost items, right-click adds one)
Crafting table, Small Parts Assembler and Reactor Assembler recipes are recognised
Put in a blank card, **Write**, then put the card into one of the **8 slots**
## Ordering
Craftable items show in the terminal with **+** (none stored) or a cyan dot
Click (none stored) or **Ctrl+click** opens the order with an amount
If an intermediate product is missing and a card exists for it, it is built first
If raw materials are missing, the terminal names them and nothing is built
Each run (2 s) makes up to 4 items
## Tempo Modules
Up to **8 Tempo Modules** go into the module slot in the menu (from the Small Parts Assembler)
Level 8 makes every run **5 times faster** (8 ticks instead of 40) while power rises to **25 times**
## Computing power
**1 core** always runs, each free **CPU core** on the data network adds one (up to 8): that many runs go at once, also for different orders
An order counts as many units as it has runs; **64** fit without RAM, each free **GB of RAM** allows **16** more
The terminal rejects orders that are too big
{drop=Cluster}
Several Component Assemblers on the same data network **share orders**: free cores of the others help out
Free computing power is split evenly; each assembler saves its own orders
{/drop}
{drop=Safety}
Ingredients are taken only at the moment a run finishes, and the result sits in the rack in the same tick
Orders, progress and buffer are stored in the **same world file as the hard drives** and saved in one step. Every finished run is a numbered booking: a half-done booking is rolled back or completed on loading
Ordering **reserves** the raw materials in the drives (gray in the terminal): other orders and withdrawals cannot touch them, finishing or cancelling frees them
If you take out a **pattern card**, all orders that need it are cancelled (if the same card exists elsewhere on the network they keep running). The buffer goes back into the racks
If a rack or part of the plant is in an unloaded chunk, the assembler **pauses** (status “Chunk not loaded”) and uses nothing up
If neither the racks nor the buffer have room, **nothing is used up** (status “Output full”)
When broken down, the buffer goes back into the racks, nothing drops twice
{/drop}
{drop=Keeping chunks loaded}
Default: the assembler only works while its whole network is loaded
Server config **assembler.keepLoaded**: chunk tickets keep plant, racks and cables loaded permanently. Upside: orders run without a player nearby. Downside: those chunks always tick and cost server performance (at most **assembler.maxChunks**, default 9)
{/drop}
compendium.component_assembler.tip: Several Component Assemblers on one network share cards, orders and computing power: planning uses all cards, and all free cores do the building.
compendium.component_assembler.title: Component Assembler
compendium.compute_assembler.text:
The **compute assembler** (**3×3×3**) is a reactor assembler with a compute turbo: same recipes, same grid, but its speed depends on how much **free computing power** (CPU and RAM) is left for it in the data network.
## Setup
Kit from the heavy assembler, controller from the reactor assembler
**Data cable** to the data port or the controller, on the same network as racks with CPU and RAM modules or a computing cluster
Power on the right (west, seen from the front), items into the grid on top, result at the lower left
## Speed by computing power
**0** (no computer): x1 (400 ticks) | x0.91 (440 ticks)
**1** (4 CPU / 64 GB): x4 | x1.0
**2** (8 / 128): x12 | x1.1
**3** (16 / 256): x32 | x1.15
**4** (32 / 512, one computing cluster): x64 | x1.2
**5** (64 / 1024): x100 | x1.2
**6** (128 / 2048): x128 | x1.2
## Power
Power per part gets cheaper at high levels: it only grows with speed to the power of 0.65
Level 6: a good 23 times (1,350 FE/t base, reactor parts 3,840 FE/t)
## Sharing
All assemblers on the network (component, reactor, small parts and compute assembler) share the free computing power evenly
Consoles and terminals take their share first
compendium.compute_assembler.tip: Several assemblers on the same data network share the free computing power evenly. One computing cluster (32 CPU / 512 GB) for a single compute assembler gives level 4 (x64).
compendium.compute_assembler.title: Compute Assembler
compendium.cool_big.text:
Large machines extend the loop. Each comes as a **machine kit** (chapter Machine basics) and has a **controller**. Right-click the **monitor** in the model (or the controller) to open the terminal, right-click a port for its purpose. Sizes and the position of every port: page **Sizes and ports**.
Each machine has **its own page** in this chapter.
## Water
**Cooling tower**: hot coolant → coolant, 960 mB/t, a little evaporates (no monitor, state in chat)
**Cooling tower XL** (63×120×63, water basin at the bottom): 3,840 mB/t, four times the cooling tower
The hot coolant comes out of the top of the **condenser**. One cooling tower serves six small or one and a half large condensers, the XL 24 small or six large
**Relief tank**: catches the relief of the pressurizer, cools it into primary water with coolant, reserve for the high-pressure injection
## Steam
**Steam generator**: hot primary water from the **fuel rod drive** turns feedwater into **wet steam**, 640 mB/t of primary water (nine full tier 1 rods) make 320 mB/t, one steam generator handles up to 1,280 mB/t
**Steam separator** (40 → 36 steam + 4 water), then **steam dryer** (40 → 39 + 1)
**Fuel rod drive**: the heart of the reactor, moves up to nine fuel rods into its reactor pressure vessel, which heats the primary water (chapter Reactor)
**Steam purifier**, **condenser**, **water treatment** and **feedwater pump** as large machines (page Loop as Large Machines)
## Primary loop
**Main coolant pump** and its **high-pressure tier**: drive the primary water from the steam generator back into the nearest fuel rod drive (pages Main coolant pump)
**Pressurizer** (3×8×3): holds the primary loop at 155 bar, vents into the relief tank above 90 %
## Safety
**Emergency cooling**: with a redstone signal or in manual mode, water → primary water, 320 mB/t, fills the primary loop, starts by itself below 20 % pressure
**High-pressure injection** (3×2×4): below 20 % pressure feeds up to 320 mB/t of primary water from the relief tank
**Containment** (31×32×31) around the fuel rod drive: feedwater and wet steam pass through penetration ports, airlock with 27 slots
## Workshop
**Heavy assembler** (chapter Machine basics) and **reprocessing plant** (chapter Reprocessing)
**Batteries** in three sizes (chapter Conduits, page Batteries)
**Ore mill** and **enrichment centrifuge** (chapter Ore and Metal, page Ore mill, and chapter Uranium Processing, page Enrichment centrifuge)
compendium.cool_big.tip: The fuel rod drive only writes on a change, so SCRAM in the terminal stays in effect until the signal changes.
compendium.cool_big.title: Plant Machines
compendium.cool_bigpumps.keywords: MCP, RCP, HKMP, main coolant pump, reactor coolant pump, primary pump
compendium.cool_bigpumps.text:
The **main coolant pump** drives the primary loop: it pumps cold primary water from the **steam generator** back into the vessel of the **nearest fuel rod drive**. Only as much flows through the vessel as the pumps report there. If the pump stops, the flow stops and the core heats up.
## Main coolant pump (3×3×3)
Pumps **2,560 mB/t** of primary water: one pump carries a drive with nine full tier 1 rods (640 mB/t) with reserve. Higher claddings and moderators need a multiple, the vessel only takes what the pumps deliver
Uses **3,600 FE/t**, power buffer 480,000 FE
Tanks 64,000 mB each
## Good to know
One pump is enough. Several pumps at the same drive add up
Without a reactor in range the terminal shows **NO REACTOR**
Primary water in on the right, out at the back, power on the left (seen from the front)
compendium.cool_bigpumps.tip: The high-pressure tier pumps twice as much but needs almost three times the power.
compendium.cool_bigpumps.title: Main Coolant Pump
compendium.cool_fluids.text:
## Primary water
**Primary water** circulates between the fuel rod drive, the steam generator and the main coolant pump, hot after the vessel, cold after the steam generator. It has no bucket, the emergency cooling fills the loop
## Coolant
**Coolant** circulates between the condenser and the cooling tower
**Sodium** and **cryo coolant** cool twice or four times as strongly in the condenser and relief tank, but turn into hot coolant
## Loop (see Coolant Loop)
Feedwater → steam generator → wet steam → separator and dryer → steam → turbine → exhaust steam → condenser → water → water treatment → feedwater
Cooling water: coolant → condenser → hot coolant → cooling tower → coolant (a little evaporates)
All are normal NeoForge fluids, pipes and tanks move them. Only the liquids have buckets, steam and the other gases live only in tanks and pipes.
compendium.cool_fluids.tip: Stronger coolant uses the same mB but cools more.
compendium.cool_fluids.title: Fluids
compendium.cool_heat.text:
The rods in the fuel rod drive create heat, the deeper and fuller, the more. The core cools a little on its own, the **primary water** flowing through the vessel takes most of it. How much flows is set by the **main coolant pump**.
## Red zone and overheating
From **80 %** heat (red): alarm, steam escapes at the sides, radiation
At **100 %** the core is overheated and the alarm runs: **12.5 seconds** until the explosion
When the countdown runs out, the **big explosion** follows, the same as the detonator's
If heat drops below **90 %** (SCRAM, more flow) the countdown is canceled
Only below **60 %** does the core give power again
See heat and cooling in the drive's terminal and via ComputerCraft (getHeat, isOverheated, getCooling).
compendium.cool_heat.tip: When the warning shows in the action bar, hit SCRAM in the terminal at once and get the primary loop running again.
compendium.cool_heat.title: Heat and Cooling
compendium.cool_hppump.keywords: HP MCP, MCP, RCP, HKMP, high pressure pump
compendium.cool_hppump.text:
The strong tier of the **main coolant pump**. It pumps cold primary water from the **steam generator** back into the vessel of the **nearest fuel rod drive**.
## High-pressure main coolant pump (3×4×5)
Pumps **5,120 mB/t** of primary water, twice as much as the normal pump
Uses **9,600 FE/t**, power buffer 1,200,000 FE
Tanks 128,000 mB each
## Good to know
A drive takes at most 2,560 mB/t, so the normal pump is already enough. The high-pressure tier is reserve (for plants with more than one drive on one pump)
Without a reactor in range the terminal shows **NO REACTOR**
Primary water in on the right, out at the back, power on the left (seen from the front)
compendium.cool_hppump.tip: One pump of this tier serves a fully loaded drive with double reserve.
compendium.cool_hppump.title: High-Pressure Main Coolant Pump
compendium.cool_loop.text:
The **steam generator** uses the hot primary water from the fuel rod drive to turn **feedwater into wet steam**. The loop brings the water back. Every station is a **large machine** from the heavy assembler, their ports are listed on the page **Loop as Large Machines**:
1. **Wet steam** of the steam generator → **Steam Separator** → **Steam Dryer**: dry steam
2. **Steam Dryer** → **Turbine**
3. Turbine **condensate port** → **Condenser**: exhaust steam becomes water. **Coolant** takes the heat, goes to the **cooling tower** as **hot coolant** and comes back cooled
4. **Condenser** → **Water Treatment**: water becomes feedwater
5. **Feedwater Pump** → **feedwater in** at the steam generator
## Good to know
One line is enough: with one steam generator (1,280 mB/t wet steam) one separator, dryer, reheater and purifier (all 1,280 mB/t), one turbine with a shaft generator, two feedwater heaters (640 mB/t each) and two condensers will do
The condenser handles **640 mB/t**, the water treatment **1,280 mB/t**, the feedwater pump **960 mB/t**: enough for a fuel rod drive with nine tier 1 rods (320 mB/t of steam) and for big plants with several stations
**Without coolant** the condenser only condenses air-cooled at **40 mB/t**
One **cooling tower** (960 mB/t) serves **one and a half condensers**, the **cooling tower XL** six. Top up what evaporates there with coolant
Make up losses (evaporation, full tank) with fresh water in the treatment
**Without feedwater** the steam generator gives off no heat, the flow at the drive stops and the core **heats up**, up to the explosion
## Steam purifier
The secondary steam is clean. You only need the **steam purifier** for contaminated steam
The purifier radiates while running, stored residue adds to it. At **16 residue** it stops
The **reprocessing plant** takes the residue: **8 residue** → **4 ash** and a 50 % chance of **1 uranium core**
## Radiation
Hot primary water is slightly radioactive, in pipes too. The turbine radiates slightly, the hot core from 80 % more
compendium.cool_loop.tip: Keep the primary and secondary loops apart: primary water only goes between the drive and the steam generator.
compendium.cool_loop.title: Coolant Loop
compendium.cool_parts.text:
Vent grille, heat exchanger, active cooler, cryo core: cooling
Water inlet supplies the loop
Sodium heat exchanger: for the higher tiers
## Moderator (control rod drive)
Hold the part and **right-click the controller** of the control rod drive. Shift + right-click with an empty hand takes it out again. Without a moderator the drive runs at its base values
It raises the **power** (more primary water is heated) and in the same ratio the **burn-up**: the energy per fuel stays the same, the rods last shorter
Tiers: **coal ×1.25**, **carbon ×1.5**, **obsidian ×2**, **fluorite ×3**, **heavy water ×4**
More power means more heat (coal 120 %, carbon 140 %, obsidian 220 %, fluorite 360 %, heavy water 420 %)
## Cooler (control rod drive)
Installed the same way. Extra cooling per tick: **heat exchanger +0.3**, **active cooler +0.6**, **cryo core +1.0**
Coal and carbon get by with the base cooling. **Obsidian** needs at least the heat exchanger, **fluorite** the active cooler (the cryo core adds reserve). Otherwise the drive overheats: alarm, shutdown and in the worst case a meltdown
## Numbers
All factors are in `cooling_values.json` (section `parts`) and can be changed with a data pack
The terminal shows moderator and cooler tier, the part tooltips show the factors
compendium.cool_parts.tip: Sodium heat exchanger and vent grille are plain components and have no effect of their own yet.
compendium.cool_parts.title: Cooling Parts and Moderators
compendium.cool_plant.text:
Steam purifier, condenser, water treatment and feedwater pump are **large machines** with a terminal. A fuel rod drive with nine tier 1 rods (320 mB/t of steam) needs one of each, bigger plants several. Build them with a **machine kit** from the heavy assembler, right-click the CRT monitor to open the terminal (state, power, tanks, operation off/on). All positions **seen from the front**, level 1 is the bottom.
Each of the four machines has **its own page** right after this one.
## Good to know
Without power or with a full output they stand still and use nothing
Outputs go to all pipes and tanks at the port, not straight into other machine ports
compendium.cool_plant.tip: Coolant and steam each have their own ports. Pipes on the right side and nothing mixes.
compendium.cool_plant.title: Loop as Large Machines
compendium.cool_ports.tip: Right-click a port with an empty hand to see its name and purpose; in the terminal the tooltip explains every port row.
compendium.cool_ports.title: Sizes and ports
compendium.cool_pumps.text:
The **main coolant pump** drives the primary loop (normal and as the high-pressure tier, see their pages).
## Pump components
The four pump tiers are **components** and cannot be placed:
**Basic** and **Electric pump**: for emergency cooling and the feedwater pump
**High pressure pump**: for the main coolant pump
**Sodium pump**: for the high-pressure main coolant pump
Each tier is made in the reactor assembler from the one before.
compendium.cool_pumps.tip: Which fluid goes where is listed on the page Fluids.
compendium.cool_pumps.title: Pumps
compendium.cracker.text:
The **cracker** (**3×3×3**) is a reactor vessel with a heating jacket and a stirrer that turns while it works. Seen from the front, **naphtha** enters on the right and the **ethylene** (gas) leaves the vessel at the upper left.
## Operation
Cracks **20 mB/t** naphtha at **1,800 FE/t**. 1000 mB of naphtha make **400 mB ethylene**.
## Setup
Kit from the Heavy Assembler.
compendium.cracker.tip: Ethylene is a gas: it needs a gas port, the pipe is the same as for fluids.
compendium.cracker.title: Cracker
compendium.data_cc.text:
With **CC:Tweaked** every data terminal, console and the control desk becomes the peripheral **sqc_network**.
## Read
**list()**, **count()**: plants on the network
**getInfo(n)**: every value with unit and maximum
**getStatus(n)**, **getTanks(n)**, **getValue(n, key)**
## Write (values are checked)
**setEnabled(n, on)**, **setThrottle(n, %)**, **setDepth(n, %)**
**setRodTarget(n, 0-15)**, **setRodMode(n, on)**, **setChannel(n, k)**, **lockRod(n, shaft, on)**
**setManual(n, on)**, **dumpTank(n, port)**, **scram(n)**
General: **set(n, key, value)**: errors come back as Lua errors
## Right at the machine: sqc_machine
Every machine and every port of a large machine is the peripheral **sqc_machine** (computer next to it or via modem)
**getInfo()**, **getStatus()**, **getValues()**, **getValue(key)**, **getTanks()**, **getSettable()**
**setEnabled(on)**, **isEnabled()**, **set(key, value)**, **dumpTank(tank)**
The fuel rod drive stays **sqc_reactor**, the control desk stays **sqc_network**
Spot and area radiation sensor: **getValue("dose_rate")** returns the dose rate in Sv/h, **set("threshold", 1e-5)** sets the alarm threshold, **set("reset_peak", 1)** clears the peak, on the area sensor **set("radius", 12)** sets the radius
{drop=Storage Terminal: sqc_storage}
• At the storage terminal the computer sees the peripheral **sqc_storage** (right next to it or via modem), read only
• **getInfo()**: racks, racks with power, drives, used, capacity, types, whether the network is fully loaded
• **getRacks()**: every rack with power, priority, drives, used and capacity
• **getItemCount()**, **list(offset, limit)**, **find(text, limit)**: items with key, name, label, count, reserved, available (up to 500 per call)
• **getItem(key)**: one item by item ID, with a number after # for items with special data
{/drop}
{drop=SQ-OS: Window Operating System}
• Built in as a ROM program: on an **Advanced Computer** (colour) the command **sqos** starts the desktop.
• **sqos** runs on the computer's terminal, **sqos -m** on the first image monitor or CC monitor, **sqos -m name** on a specific one (e.g. monitor_0). **sqos -s 0.5** sets the text size, **sqos -d 128** the pixels per block on the image monitor.
• Modern interface: dark, flat design with an accent colour, a **dock** at the bottom (pinned apps and open windows, right-click pins or unpins, Alt+1 to Alt+9 opens the dock slot), start menu with tiles and search (just start typing), clock, bell and alarms at the top right. The bell opens the **notification center** with the latest messages, the clock the **quick settings** (theme, accent, sound, animations, lock, reboot). On the **image monitor** you get rounded windows with shadows, selectable wallpapers (gradient, glow, grid, plain) and drawn icons, on the terminal and normal monitors the same interface in text form. After an adjustable idle time a **screen saver** shows the clock.
• Windows: buttons at the right of the title bar (minimise, maximise, close), drag the title to move, the bottom right corner resizes, double tap the title to maximise, right-click opens the window menu. Drag a window to the left or right edge to snap it to half the screen, to the top edge to maximise. Monitor and touch: tap the title, then tap the target. The keyboard goes to the active window: Alt+Tab switches (hold Alt, press Tab repeatedly), Alt+F4 closes, Alt+Left/Right snaps, Alt+Up maximises, Alt+Down minimises.
• Programs: **Power plant** (all machines with live values, switches, controls and alarms; search field, favourites with a star at the top of the list, tapping a value shows its history curve), **Storage** (searches the digital storage via sqc_storage), **Chat** (public room and private chats with time stamps and day separators, chat list on the left, history on the right; a mention of your own name notifies you; the sender is the player logged in at the bank terminal, the server stores the messages, **/clear** empties the view. Computer next to a Bank Terminal or a modem at the terminal, plus bank server and Bank Modem as for the bank, no CC modem needed; peripheral functions **chatSend(to, text)** and **chatFetch(after)**), **Files**, **Editor** (with line numbers), **Console** (a normal CraftOS shell in a window), **Notes** (short text notes, the first line is the title), **Calculator**, **System** (ID, computer name, uptime, disk space, attached devices), **Help** (gestures, keys, apps; opens on the first start) and **Settings** (colour scheme Dark, Midnight, Ocean or Light, six accent colours, wallpaper, animations, screen saver, language, clock, sound, dock).
• Bank, auctions and exchange in SQ-OS: the **Bank** keeps a **statement** (every balance change the app sees, with an incoming/outgoing filter) and **standing orders** (player, amount, every how many days; due orders notify you, the transfer is made with a button and a right-click on the terminal). The **Auctions** have a **watch list** (watched offers notify you when they are sold or withdrawn) and notify you when someone undercuts one of your offers. The **Exchange** has **price alerts** (a notification as soon as a good rises above or falls below a price, while the exchange is open). These data live on the computer, not on the server.
• Power plant and Storage show what the computer sees: a data terminal or console on the network (sqc_network) or machines right next to it (sqc_machine).
• Start on boot: a startup.lua file with the line **shell.run("sqos -m")**.
{/drop}
compendium.data_cc.tip: Whole network: computer at the terminal (sqc_network). One machine: computer right next to it (sqc_machine).
compendium.data_cc.title: ComputerCraft
compendium.data_console.text:
The **console** is a command line for every plant on the network.
## Commands
**list**: all plants with number and state
**info 1**: every value and what you can set
**get 1 heat**: one value
**set 2 throttle 80**: change a setting; **on/off** works too
**watch 1 heat**: refresh a value every second, **stop** or Ctrl+C ends it
**open 1**: the plant's terminal
**clear**: clear the screen
## Shortcuts
Instead of the number you can give part of the name: **set turbine run on**
↑ and ↓ recall earlier commands
compendium.data_console.tip: Use 'watch' to keep an eye on heat while starting up, without walking to the reactor.
compendium.data_console.title: Command Console
compendium.data_desk.text:
The **control desk** (3×2×2) is a control room desk as a machine.
1. Kit from the **heavy assembler**: 2 digital displays, command console, control desk controller, 4 steel sheets, 4 redstone blocks, 2 reactor casings, terminal and power port
2. Place it like any kit
3. Data cable to the **data port** at the back right (or the controller), power at the back left (**24 FE/t**, seen from the front)
## Monitors
**Center**: right-click opens the **command line**; shows the selected plant with its state (including faults such as no power or output full) and its six most important values
**Left**: all plants; right-click selects the next one
**Right**: alarms; right-click jumps to the next fault
## Which values
Every plant shows what fits it: first power, output or speed, then heat, fuel, progress or throughput, then storage and fill levels
Fuel rod drive: power, heat, fuel, rod position, cold primary water, flow
Switches such as on/off are part of the state, the command line shows every value with **info**
## Desk
Four **needle gauges** and the **digital display** show the selected plant
Lamps: power, running, notice (yellow), fault (red, blinking)
**Emergency stop** (red mushroom button): right-click pulls the rods of **every fuel rod drive on the network** (SCRAM)
Without power the screens stay dark
compendium.data_desk.tip: Control room wall and desk on the same network: overview on the wall, control at the desk.
compendium.data_desk.title: Control Desk
compendium.data_instruments.text:
Instruments hang on the wall and show **one value** of a plant on the network.
## Kinds
**Needle gauge**: needle with red zone
**Bar display**: bar with percent
**Digital display**: large value
**Multi display**: four values of one plant as a list, right-click opens the selection
## Use
**Right-click**: next value
**Sneak + right-click**: next plant
A **comparator** reads the value as signal 0-15
Without a connection it shows NO SIGNAL
## Controls
**Data button**: trigger an action (emergency stop, empty a tank, reset the peak) or toggle on/off
**Data lever**: switch an on/off value, e.g. a pump or the turbine running
**Data slider**: set a value in 16 steps, e.g. the rod target of the fuel rod drive or the turbine throttle
**Sneak + right-click**: pick plant and value, **right-click**: operate (on the slider, at the spot on the track)
Lever and slider follow the real value, even when a terminal or computer changes it
All three also give redstone: button briefly 15, lever up 15, slider its step
compendium.data_instruments.tip: Comparator on a heat gauge + redstone = your own warning light.
compendium.data_instruments.title: Instruments
compendium.data_logbook.text:
The **Logbook Terminal** writes down what happens in the plants, even when you are not looking.
## Connection
Place it on a wall at the **data cable** (or right next to a plant), like the storage monitor
The monitor shows the **latest entries right in the world**, the newest at the bottom; several blocks side by side (up to 4 x 4) make a big screen
It reads the **state** of every plant on the network each second and records every change
## Entries
**Alarm** (red): fault, shutdown, power loss, explosion countdown
**Warning** (yellow): a plant reports a problem
**All clear** (green): the state is fine again
**Info** (gray): plant on or off, linked or lost
Every entry carries **game time** (day and clock) and **real time**
## Use
**Right-click** opens the full book, the newest entry is at the **bottom**
**Sneak + right-click** switches the monitor **text size** (5 steps)
New entries arrive live; if you scroll up, the view stays where it is
**Mouse wheel**, arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End scroll; **Latest** jumps to the end
Filters: **All**, **Warnings** (warning and above) and **Alarms**
The last **500 entries** stay in the block, also after a restart
If a state flickers, the book writes at most one entry per plant every 3 seconds
## ComputerCraft
Peripheral **sqc_logbook**: **count()**, **get(n)** and **getLast(n)** with number, day, clock, real time, severity and text
compendium.data_logbook.tip: A logbook on the control room cable network shows what happened first after a fault.
compendium.data_logbook.title: Logbook Monitor
compendium.data_monitor.text:
The **image monitor** is a flat screen for **pixel images**. A ComputerCraft computer draws on it, without CC:Tweaked it stays dark.
## Setup
Monitors side by side and on top of each other with the **same direction** as a full rectangle (up to **8×8**) are **one** screen
On a **wall** it hangs flat, on the **ceiling** it lies flat with the picture facing down, on the **floor** it stands upright
**Sneak** while placing: flat on the floor, or hanging upright from the ceiling
Building against a monitor takes over its position and direction
Put a **computer** right next to any monitor of the screen (or use a modem)
## Resolution
Default **64×64 pixels per block**, at most **512** per side (server setting)
**Ctrl + right-click** (empty hand) switches the pixels per block: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256
A new resolution turns the picture black, the computer gets the event **sqc_resize** (name, width, height)
## Touch
**Right-click** sends the computer the event **sqc_touch** (name, x, y, player)
x and y count in pixels of the whole screen from 1, top left
**Sneak + right-click** (empty hand) opens the screen full size: mouse and keyboard belong to the computer, sneak + right-click or Esc leaves it
Events in the full screen: **sqc_touch** (name, x, y, player, button), **sqc_up** (name, x, y, button), **sqc_drag** (name, x, y, button), **sqc_move** (name, x, y), **sqc_scroll** (name, x, y, direction), **sqc_key** (name, key, held), **sqc_key_up** (name, key), **sqc_char** (name, character)
Buttons: 1 left, 2 right, 3 middle; key codes as in ComputerCraft (keys.*)
## ComputerCraft: sqc_image_monitor
All functions act on the whole screen, coordinates start at 1
**getSize()**, **getResolution()**, **setResolution(w, h)**
**clear(color)**, **setPixel(x, y, color)**, **getPixel(x, y)**, **fill(x, y, w, h, color)**, **drawPixels(x, y, rows)**
**drawImage(data)** for PNG, JPG, GIF or BMP: without a place it fills the screen, with **"fit"** it fits in, with x, y, w, h it sits there
**drawText(x, y, text, color, size)** and **measureText(text, size)**
Colors: a number like 0xFF0000, a name like "red" or "#FF0000"
## Drawing fast
Every single call waits one server tick, so send many commands in **one** **batch({...})**
Commands: clear, fill, pixel, text, ctext, line, tri, gtri, disc, arc, grad, glow, dim, afill, image
The image **"logo"** is the SQ Nuclear logo
The picture only goes to players who can see the monitor, afterwards only changed rows
compendium.data_monitor.tip: Drawing many parts? One batch call per picture, otherwise every command waits a tick.
compendium.data_monitor.title: Image Monitor
compendium.data_net.text:
Use **data cables** to control your plants remotely.
## Setup
Run cable to a **controller** or a **port** of a large machine or turbine
**Every large machine** has a visible **data port** (flange with a small screen): it takes the data cable, a **ComputerCraft** cable or modem (peripheral **sqc_machine**) and a monitor right next to it
**Every single-block machine** is its own data port: cable to any side (solar panel, castor, shower, area monitor)
At the other end a **terminal**, a **console**, instruments, the control room or the control desk
A device placed right next to the plant works without cable
A network may hold many plants; each one counts once
## On and off
Everything that uses power switches with **enable** (console: **set 1 enable off**); on a battery it holds the output
Empty tanks with **dump.<tank>**
## Data terminal
Right-click shows every plant on the network as a **folder**: click expands it
Inside are **values** (live), **controls** (on/off, steps such as throttle or rack priority) and for server racks the **bays**: drives expand again and show their items
**Open terminal** in the folder opens the plant's own terminal, **Locate** shows a light column above it
At the top filters (All, Faults, Storage) and **search**: it also finds items on the drives
At the bottom faults, storage and computing power on the network
The terminal stays open while you stand near the data terminal
compendium.data_net.tip: Cable to any port is enough. You don't need to reach the controller.
compendium.data_net.title: Data Network
compendium.data_power.text:
The **Power Monitor** measures, for all plants on the data network, how much power is made and how much is used.
## Connection
Place it on a wall at the **data cable** (or right next to a plant), like the logbook monitor
It finds **producers** (turbines, solar, wind, RTG, fusion, coal generator), **consumers** (every machine with a power buffer) and **batteries** on the network
Several blocks side by side (up to 4 x 4) make a big screen with more numbers
## Display
**Production** in FE/t, plus how loaded the producers are
**Consumption** in FE/t: what the machines really draw
**Balance**: production minus consumption. Minus means the batteries are being drawn down
**Storage**: fill level of all batteries together, also as a graph
**Forecast**: when the batteries will be empty or full at this balance
**Biggest consumers** and all producers as a list, identical plants are grouped
## Use
**Right-click** opens the window. The graph shows the last **2 minutes** (per second) or the last **hour**; hover the graph to read the values at any point in time
The tab at the top switches between **CRT** and **console view**
**Sneak + right-click** switches the graph on the screen in the world between seconds and half an hour
The histories stay in the block, also after a restart
## Good to know
Substations only pass power through and are not counted twice
Power flowing into batteries does not count as consumption
## ComputerCraft
Peripheral **sqc_power**: **status()**, **history(n, slow)**, **producers()**, **consumers()** and **storages()**
compendium.data_power.tip: A power monitor in the control room shows whether your plant delivers more than the facility eats.
compendium.data_power.title: Power Monitor
compendium.data_scanner.text:
The **Network Scanner** shows you what is attached to a data network. Ideal when you set up a terminal, a console or a program and do not know why a machine is missing.
## Pick a network
**Right-click** a **data cable** to pick its network
**Sneak + right-click** picks it from any part of the network: machine, port, terminal, console, control desk
**Sneak + right-click in the air** forgets the network
## What you see
Everything glows **through walls** while the scanner is in your hand (up to 160 blocks around you)
**Cyan**: data cables, with lines between them so the route is clear
**White**: terminals, consoles, instruments and logbook on the network
A **colored frame** around each machine with its **name**: green running, yellow notice, red fault, gray off
A **bright field** on the machine shows where the network attaches
## Typical questions
**Why is the machine missing in the terminal?** It has no frame: its cable is not connected to the network
**Two separate networks?** Pick one: the other stays dark
**Cable through the containment?** Inside and outside belong together, the scanner follows the feedthrough
If a chunk is not loaded, the network ends there
compendium.data_scanner.tip: Not sure which cable leads where? The network scanner draws the whole data network through the walls.
compendium.data_scanner.title: Network Scanner
compendium.data_wall.text:
The **control room** is a screen wall for every plant on the network.
## Setup
**3×2 to 5×3** screens as a full rectangle, all facing the same way
A data cable to any screen of the wall
## Picture
One **tile per plant**: name, state, three values with bars
Tiles adapt to the wall size
If not all plants fit, the wall pages every 5 seconds
Faults blink red
**Right-click a tile** to open that plant's terminal
compendium.data_wall.tip: A bigger wall shows more plants at once.
compendium.data_wall.title: Control Room
compendium.decon_dock.text:
## Decon dock (4×2×2)
Open parking bay, on the right the switch cabinet with power port and terminal, on the left the chemical cabinet with data port, lye port, diesel port and rubble output
## Charging and refilling
Drive the **decon robot in backwards** to the middle, the rear with the charging contacts to the back wall
The dock charges its **battery** (500 FE/t) and refills its **cleaning agent** (**lye** from the chemical lab, 10 mB/t)
If the power of the dock is not enough, it burns **diesel** from the distillation column into battery charge (up to 5 mB/t, 200 FE per mB)
The **rubble tank** empties into the rubble output (contaminated rubble, it radiates: take it straight to a waste barrel or the crusher)
The robot only cleans with cleaning agent (5 mB per cleaning pulse); at the rear three bars show battery, cleaning agent and rubble
## Ports
Seen from the front: **power** rear right, **lye** rear left, **diesel** rear left top, **data port** front left, **rubble output** (item port) front left top
Power, lye, diesel and a second **rubble output** are also on the **back wall**, so the dock can stand against a wall
## Crafting
Controller in the **Equipment Assembler**, kit in the **Heavy Assembler**
compendium.decon_dock.tip: The robot only charges when its rear points at the back wall. The lye comes from the chemical lab.
compendium.decon_dock.title: Decon Dock
compendium.distillation_column.text:
The **distillation column** (**3×6×3**) is the refinery. **Crude oil** enters at the bottom (on the right, seen from the front) and separates by density in the tower: **tar** at the bottom, **diesel** in the middle, **naphtha** at the top, all three leave on the left. The warning light on top turns while it works.
## Operation
Processes **20 mB/t** crude oil at **1,200 FE/t**. Every 1000 mB of crude oil makes **300 mB naphtha**, **350 mB diesel** and **250 mB tar**, plus **1 sulfur dust**. The remaining 100 mB burn off as flare gas. The sulfur slides out of the chute on the right. When an output is full the column stops.
## Setup
Kit from the Heavy Assembler.
compendium.distillation_column.tip: All three outputs need a consumer, otherwise the column backs up: tar goes to the polymer plant, diesel to the gas generator or the decon dock, naphtha to the cracker. A fluid buffer catches what nobody takes. The sulfur comes on top of roasting ore.
compendium.distillation_column.title: Distillation Column
compendium.eff_overview.text:
Two plants get more out of the same reactor power. They are optional. Without them the plant runs at its base values.
## Overview
**Reheater**: steam → superheated steam, the turbine makes **+20 %** power from it
**Feedwater heater**: turbine exhaust preheats the feedwater, the **steam generator** makes **+15 %** steam with it
## Loop with everything
Primary water: fuel rod drive → steam generator → back to the drive
Feedwater → **feedwater heater** → steam generator → wet steam → separator and dryer → **reheater** → turbine
Turbine exhaust: half → **feedwater heater** (1 mB per 2 mB of exhaust), the rest → condenser → water
Heat, fuel and safety of the core stay the same.
compendium.eff_overview.tip: Start with the reheater: it gives the most for the effort.
compendium.eff_overview.title: More Power from Steam
compendium.eff_preheater.text:
The **feedwater heater** (5×3×3) uses the waste heat in the turbine exhaust.
## Ports (seen from the front)
Right: **feedwater in** (640 mB/t)
Top: **exhaust steam in** (320 mB/t, from the turbine condensate port)
Left: **preheated feedwater out** (640 mB/t)
Bottom: **condensate out** (320 mB/t water)
## Effect
The **steam generator** takes preheated feedwater like normal feedwater
The same heat of the primary water makes **15 % more** steam (and use 15 % more feedwater)
The heater replaces part of the condenser
compendium.eff_preheater.tip: Do not mix with normal feedwater in the same tank.
compendium.eff_preheater.title: Feedwater Heater
compendium.eff_reheater.text:
The **reheater** (5×3×3) turns steam into **superheated steam**.
## Ports (seen from the front)
Right: **steam in** (1,280 mB/t)
Left: **superheated steam out** (1,024 mB/t) → turbine
Bottom: **condensate out** (256 mB/t water)
## Numbers
Without: 40 mB steam × 256 FE = **10,240 FE/t**
With: 32 mB superheated × 384 FE = **12,288 FE/t**
## Note
The turbine takes steam **or** superheated steam. Do not mix, the tank holds one kind
Needs no power
compendium.eff_reheater.tip: Kit in the heavy assembler, controller in the assembler.
compendium.eff_reheater.title: Reheater
compendium.energy_chain.text:
## The chain
1. The **fuel rods** in the fuel rod drive create heat.
2. The **reactor pressure vessel** below the drive heats **primary water** with it, up to 640 mB per tick.
3. The **steam generator** uses the hot primary water to turn feedwater into **wet steam** (320 mB per tick), the primary water goes back cold.
4. The **steam separator** and **steam dryer** turn it into dry steam.
5. The **turbine** turns the steam into power.
6. The power flows to every adjacent consumer.
## Units
The turbine shows its output in **SU** (Create stress units)
Internally the power is FE, the display converts with **1 FE/t = 8 SU**
compendium.energy_chain.tip: Power can only flow out if a consumer is connected. Plan your cables early.
compendium.energy_chain.title: From Heat to Power
compendium.energy_loop.text: This is how the loop closes. Hover a machine for a hint, click to open its page.
compendium.energy_loop.title: Reactor Loop
compendium.energy_parts.text:
Translators (Basic, Brass, Composite, Glowstone): **right-click the turbine controller**, shift + empty hand takes them out. Without a translator the turbine runs at its base values
Tier 1 Basic: power ×1.0, throughput ×1 · tier 2 Brass: ×1.1 and ×1.5 · tier 3 Composite: ×1.25 and ×2 · tier 4 Glowstone: ×1.5 and ×3
Power is the yield per mB of steam, throughput the highest steam consumption of the turbine (400 mB/t without a translator). Provided there is enough steam and condenser reserve
Turbine parts: Basic, Brass Rotor, Steel Blades, Glowstone Generator
Pressure chambers: part of the turbine, hold the pressure
Cooling tower segments: components of the cooling tower kits
Pumps: components of the pump machines, see page Pumps

Note: turbine parts, pressure chambers and cooling tower segments are components of the machine kits (chapter Machine basics).
compendium.energy_parts.tip: You can find all tiers in the NuclearSQ creative tab, sorted by part.
compendium.energy_parts.title: Plant Parts
compendium.energy_rtg.keywords: RTG, radioisotope thermoelectric generator, nuclear battery, Pu-238, plutonium, strontium
compendium.energy_rtg.text:
## Radioisotope generator (RTG)
**2 blocks tall** (cylinder with cooling fins and glow windows, the block above has to be free), from the **reactor assembler**: 4 steel sheets, 2 lead shieldings, 4 copper coils, 2 osmium heat plates, 1 control board I
Fuel is the **isotope capsule** (reactor assembler: 15 uranium oxide, 1 lead shielding, 2 steel sheets). Uranium oxide is a by-product of the enrichment centrifuge
**Plutonium-238 capsule** (15 plutonium-238 oxide from reprocessing bred neptunium): **9,000 FE/t**, lasts four times as long, about 3.52 billion FE
**Strontium-cesium capsule** (15 strontium-cesium from the vitrification plant): **6,400 FE/t**, lasts twice as long, about 1.24 billion FE
**Right-click** with the capsule inserts it, **sneaking** with an empty hand takes it out, right-clicking with an empty hand shows output and what is left
## Output
**3,600 FE/t** fresh (coal generator 720, solar collector 312), then it halves every **3 Minecraft days** (one hour real time)
After four half-lives (4 hours real time) the capsule is spent, 225 FE/t at the end. One capsule gives about **352 million FE** in total, as much as about 610 coal
It only decays while the capsule is inside the generator, but always, even when nobody takes the power
**No storage**, connections all around both blocks: power goes straight to cables, batteries and machines next to it
## Radiation
The generator radiates slightly, 0.5 mSv/h at one block when fresh, less with the remaining output
A wall in between shields it; do not stand next to it for long, the dosimeter keeps count
If it is broken or blown up, the capsule drops out
compendium.energy_rtg.tip: An outpost needs just a few generators, a battery and a cable. Stock up on capsules, decay only starts inside the generator.
compendium.energy_rtg.title: Stepping stone: radioisotope generator
compendium.energy_shaft.text:
Instead of outputting energy from the controller, the turbine can deliver its power over the **shaft**.
1. Place a **shaft coupling** 1 block behind the exhaust ring, exactly on the rotor axis (level 4, center)
2. The **consumer** goes directly behind it
## Shaft generator (3×5×4)
Place it with the **shaft generator kit**: controller at the front on the axis, against the coupling
Turns shaft power into energy, **energy out** at the back (cell 2 from the left, level 4), up to 160,000 FE/t
Buffer 64,000,000 FE, the terminal sits in the cabinet at the front right
## Create shaft output (Create only)
One block instead of the generator, the shaft points away from the turbine
Speed follows the turbine, up to **256 RPM**
Capacity: **32 SU** per FE/t, so 102,400 SU at 3,200 FE/t
## No double energy
The consumer gets the power **first**, only the rest goes into the turbine buffer
Without a coupling the turbine outputs its power at the controller
compendium.energy_shaft.tip: While the shaft runs, the turbine terminal shows SHAFT instead of DELIVERED.
compendium.energy_shaft.title: The Turbine Shaft
compendium.energy_solar.text:
## Solar
**Solar panel** from the reactor assembler (11 glass, 8 lapis, 4 copper ingots, 8 iron ingots, 4 redstone): up to **69 FE/t**, 5 connectors (4 sides and bottom)
**Solar collector** from the reactor assembler (4 solar panels, 4 steel sheets, 15 copper ingots, copper coil): up to **312 FE/t**, 1 power port, place them in a grid, one cable at the edge is enough
**Solar field** (5×2×5): kit from the heavy assembler with 4 solar panels, up to **2400 FE/t**, power out on the left, built-in buffer for **1 million FE**
Full output at noon, less in the morning and evening, **nothing at night**. Collector and field follow the sun and keep **full output from late morning to mid afternoon**
Needs a **clear sky** (for the field above its middle); does nothing in the Nether and End
Rain −60 %, thunder another −50 %
**Built-in buffer**: panel 27,600 FE, collector 124,800 FE, field 1 million FE. Whatever nobody takes right now is stored and released in the evening. Put a battery behind it for more
Height pays off: from Y 64 to Y 192 up to **+25 %**
compendium.energy_solar.tip: Pair solar with a battery: charge during the day and keep the coal generator as a night-time backup.
compendium.energy_solar.title: Starter power: solar
compendium.energy_start.text:
The assemblers need power before any reactor runs. For the small parts assembler at the start one coal generator is enough.
## Coal generator (3×3×3)
1. Kit from the **crafting table**: 4 iron ingots, blast furnace, 2 copper ingots, redstone block, iron block
2. Place it like any kit (hologram, right-click)
3. Right-click the monitor: insert fuel
Burns anything that burns in a furnace: coal, charcoal, wood, coal block, lava bucket
**720 FE/t**, one coal lasts 40 seconds (576,000 FE)
Fuel in on the right (hoppers work), power out on the left, empty buckets (from lava buckets) out at the back (seen from the front)
No storage: it only burns while a cable or consumer takes the power, otherwise it waits
The fire window flickers and the flywheel spins while it burns
compendium.energy_start.tip: The small parts assembler gets by with one coal generator. The other assemblers need a lot more (1,350 to 9,600 FE/t): set up several generators and a battery.
compendium.energy_start.title: Starter power: coal generator
compendium.energy_steam.text:
## Two loops
**Primary loop**: fuel rod drive → hot primary water → **steam generator** → cold primary water → back to the drive. Closed, no bucket, hot primary water is slightly radioactive
**Secondary loop**: feedwater → steam generator → **wet steam** → separator and dryer → turbine. This steam is not radioactive
## How much steam?
Up to **71 mB/t** of primary water per rod, times insertion depth and remaining charge: nine full rods fully inserted = **640 mB/t**
The steam generator turns that into **320 mB/t of wet steam**, 15 % more with preheated feedwater
Nothing is heated without a rod, without fuel or while overheated
## When it stalls
If feedwater runs out or the steam backs up, the primary water stays hot and the flow at the drive stops
Without flow the core heats up, up to the explosion
compendium.energy_steam.tip: Without a consumer the steam backs up, then the primary water too, and the core keeps heating. Plan the whole loop before you insert the rods.
compendium.energy_steam.title: The Steam
compendium.energy_turbine.text:
The turbine is a large multiblock (7×7×16) of pressure chambers, rotor, blades and generator.
Place it with the **turbine kit** (from the reactor assembler, chapter Machine basics)
The **turbine controller** takes in steam and outputs power to all neighbors
Only **clean steam**, by pipe; contaminated steam after a tube leak is cleaned by the steam purifier first
The **condensate port** outputs exhaust steam for the condenser
## The menu
Gauges: speed, power in **SU**, temperature
Bars: steam, power, throttle, load
**Start/Stop** and a **throttle slider** for the steam flow
## Numbers
Up to **400 mB/t** steam at 100 % throttle
1 mB steam = 256 FE, so up to 102,400 FE/t = **819,200 SU**
Steam tank 640,000 mB, power buffer 128,000,000 FE
**One line is enough**: with one steam generator a single turbine with a Glowstone translator (up to 1,200 mB/t) and one shaft generator will do
compendium.energy_turbine.tip: Speed and temperature are display only, they follow the steam flow.
compendium.energy_turbine.title: The Steam Turbine
compendium.energy_wind.text:
## Wind in three sizes
**Small Wind Turbine** (7×14×5): kit from the Heavy Assembler, slim mast, up to **352 FE/t**, about 96 FE/t on average on flat land
**Wind Turbine** (17×36×7): tall tower, rotor 16 blocks across, up to **1,760 FE/t**, about 616 FE/t on average
**Wind Power Plant** (35×72×14): giant tower (55 blocks to the hub), rotor 32 blocks across, up to **7,040 FE/t**, about 2,948 FE/t on average on flat land, much more on a hill
## How much wind arrives
Output = peak × **hub height** × **open surroundings** × **wind strength**
**Hub height**: only 30 % at Y 40, full from Y 160. A hill or a tall base pays off
**Surroundings**: mountains, forests and houses in the way take wind away (checked up to 20, 40 and 64 blocks); fully built in leaves 20 %
**Wind strength**: changes slowly over time (gusts between 20 and 100 %), rain and thunderstorms add storm
No wind in the Nether and the End, or under a roof over the hub; in a lull the rotor stands (state NO WIND)
**No storage**: power nobody takes is lost. Power out on the right, data port on the left
The data network shows hub height, surroundings and wind strength separately
compendium.energy_wind.tip: Put the plant out in the open on a hill and pair it with a battery: the storage evens out gusts and lulls.
compendium.energy_wind.title: Wind Power
compendium.equipment_assembler.text:
The **equipment assembler** is a manufacturing cell (**3×2×2**) with a fitting dummy on a turntable, an assembly arm and a press. Like the reactor assembler it works in a **3×3 grid**: ingredients in any slots, power at the power port, the result comes out on the left.
## What it makes
**Exoskeleton**: helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots, cores, modules and the exo station
**Protective suits** of tiers I to III
**Decon devices**: shower, sprayer, robot and remote
**Pocket batteries** in three sizes
**Respirator mask**
## Setup
Kit from the **Reactor Assembler**, placed like any machine. Power on the right (seen from the front), items on top, result on the left, data cables at the data port.
compendium.equipment_assembler.tip: The parts for suits and modules (lead shielding, control boards, steel sheets) come from the other assemblers: stocking raw materials in the grid input does not help, the assembler only takes complete recipes.
compendium.equipment_assembler.title: Equipment Assembler
compendium.example_assembler_line.note.a: The small parts assembler (3×2×3) is the first machine: it builds plates, casings and ports. It needs 960 FE/t, one part takes 5 seconds. Ingredients come in through an item pipe at the right input, the finished parts go from the left output to the reactor assembler and through a second pipe to the equipment assembler.
compendium.example_assembler_line.note.b: The reactor assembler (3×3×3) builds controllers, boards, seals and fuel rod parts in a 3×3 grid. It needs 1,350 FE/t (reactor parts 3,840 FE/t), one part takes 20 seconds. The small parts enter at the yellow input on top, the controllers go from the output at the bottom left to the heavy assembler.
compendium.example_assembler_line.note.c: The heavy assembler (5×3×5) builds the machine kits in a 5×5 grid: the controller from the reactor assembler sits in the middle, casings and ports come through a second item pipe on the same input on top. It needs 5,760 FE/t (reactor parts 9,600 FE/t). The finished kit comes out at the bottom left.
compendium.example_assembler_line.note.d: The equipment assembler (3×2×2) builds the exoskeleton, hazmat suits, decon devices and pocket batteries. It gets small parts straight from the small parts assembler; lead shielding and control boards come through a second item pipe on the same input on top. It only accepts complete recipes, the result comes out on the left.
compendium.example_assembler_line.text: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_assembler_line.title: Assembler line
compendium.example_autocrafting.note.asm: The component assembler (5×4×5) builds to order from the terminal: it takes the ingredients from the racks and puts the result back. It needs 1,440 FE/t per working core. One data cable comes from the computing cluster, a second from the pattern rack. 1 core always runs, every free CPU core adds one (up to 8); each free GB of RAM lets a job hold 16 more units.
compendium.example_autocrafting.note.bat: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and delivers up to 131,072 FE/t per port. Power cables run from the first output to the rack (24 FE/t plus drives) and the computing cluster (780 FE/t), from the second to the component assembler and the pattern rack. It is charged through the input on the other side.
compendium.example_autocrafting.note.clu: The computing cluster gives the network a fixed 32 CPU cores and 512 GB RAM, so no CPU or RAM modules are needed. It needs 780 FE/t from the battery, a data cable to the rack and cooling water on the blue port (8,000 mB tank, not shown here): without water it overheats and shuts down. A second data cable continues to the component assembler.
compendium.example_autocrafting.note.cra: The crafting terminal is a storage terminal with a 3×3 crafting grid. It needs no power, but 2 CPU and 32 GB RAM on the network, here supplied by the cluster, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the rack. When a grid slot runs empty while crafting, it pulls one more of the same item from the racks.
compendium.example_autocrafting.note.pat: The pattern rack (4×5×3) stores 40 written pattern cards and needs only 12 FE/t. Through the data cable the component assembler sees the recipes without the cards sitting in it. Blank cards are built by the small parts assembler and written in the component assembler. Without power new jobs from these cards are blocked, running jobs continue.
compendium.example_autocrafting.note.rac: The large server rack (4×5×3) has 40 bays, here it holds only drives. It needs 24 FE/t plus the power of each drive. From the data port at the back one data cable runs to the computing cluster and one to the crafting terminal: this puts them all on the same network. CPU and RAM come from the cluster.
compendium.example_autocrafting.text: Animated 3D build of autocrafting: battery, a rack with drives only, a computing cluster that supplies CPU and RAM (so no CPU or RAM modules are needed), crafting terminal, component assembler and pattern rack.
compendium.example_autocrafting.title: Autocrafting with a computing cluster
compendium.example_base_oil.note.bat: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE. Both gas generators feed it through one input each, up to 131,072 FE/t each. It buffers the power the generators cannot store themselves and hands it out again at the outputs, for example to the derrick (450 FE/t), the column (1,200 FE/t) and the cracker (1,800 FE/t).
compendium.example_base_oil.note.column: The distillation column (5×18×5) splits 20 mB/t of crude oil at 1,200 FE/t: 1,000 mB become 300 mB naphtha, 350 mB diesel and 250 mB tar, plus 1 sulfur dust. Naphtha goes by pipe to the cracker, tar to the polymer plant, diesel to the second gas generator. When one of the three tanks is full it stops.
compendium.example_base_oil.note.cracker: The cracker (3×3×3) cracks 20 mB/t of naphtha at 1,800 FE/t: 1,000 mB become 400 mB ethylene. The naphtha arrives by pipe from the column at the right input, the ethylene leaves the vessel at the top left. It is a gas, but runs through the same kind of pipe on to the gas generator.
compendium.example_base_oil.note.derrick: The oil derrick (5×15×5) stands on an oil well: its core has to lie beneath the tower. It pumps 40 mB/t of crude oil and needs 450 FE/t. The crude goes by pipe into the crude input of the distillation column. When the well is empty it waits until it refills (1 % per Minecraft day).
compendium.example_base_oil.note.gasgen: The gas generator (5×5×7) burns up to 6 mB/t of ethylene from the cracker and delivers 10,000 FE/t for it, that is 1,667 FE per mB. The gas arrives at the intake rail on the right, the power leaves on the left. It has no storage: what nobody takes is lost. That is why its power cable leads into the large battery.
compendium.example_base_oil.note.gasgen2: A second gas generator burns the diesel from the column: diesel burns just as fast and yields just as much as ethylene (6 mB/t for 10,000 FE/t), but the tank may hold only one kind. This keeps the diesel tank from filling up and the column from stopping. Its power also goes into the battery, through the second input.
compendium.example_base_oil.note.polymer: The polymer plant (3×3×3) receives the tar from the column at the tar port at the back left bottom. 2 sulfur + 400 mB tar give 6 rubber (2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds), 1 coal + 200 mB tar give 2 coke (1,800 FE/t, 8 seconds). Sulfur and coal go into the item input on top, the result slides out over the chute on the left.
compendium.example_base_oil.text: Pump and refine oil: the derrick feeds the distillation column, naphtha goes to the cracker, ethylene fuels the gas generator that feeds power back, and tar goes to the polymer plant.
compendium.example_base_oil.title: Stage 3: Oil
compendium.example_base_ore.note.asm: The component assembler (5×4×5) accepts the milled parts from the CNC mill at the item input on top and stores them straight into the racks. Only what no longer fits there comes out on the left. To build it needs 1,440 FE/t per working core and a data cable to the storage network, which is added in the next stage.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.blast: The blast furnace (5×4×5) melts 8 iron ingots and 8 coke or coal into 8 steel ingots, one batch takes 10 seconds at 3,600 FE/t. Both go into the scrap bin in the back: the coke by item pipe from the kiln, the iron through a second pipe on the same input. The steel ingots come out of the ladle in front and go by item pipe to the plate mill.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.cnc: The CNC mill (2×2×3) mills steel sheet into parts for later machines: 61 lead and 4 steel sheets make 1 lead shielding, 30 osmium and 8 steel sheets make 1 osmium heat plate. The sheet arrives by item pipe from the plate mill high on the back of the feeder tower, lead or osmium through a second pipe on the same input. The finished part comes out on the left and goes by item pipe to the component assembler.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.hammer: The hammer mill (3×2×3) crushes finished ingots: 1 iron, copper or gold ingot gives 1 dust, with a 25 % chance of a second (50 % with one, 100 % with two cycle modules). Ingots go into the hopper on top, the dust leaves at the bottom left, power arrives on the right. Ores remain the job of the ore mill.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.kiln: The kiln (3×3×3) fires 2 coal or charcoal into 1 coke, one firing takes 5 seconds at 300 FE/t. The coal goes in on top, the coke leaves the kiln at the lower side and goes by item pipe into the scrap bin of the blast furnace. The same kiln also fires zirconium ingots, glass plates and glass seals. It also smelts everything a normal furnace smelts with power, ores and clay into bricks included.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.mill: The ore mill (3×3×4) grinds ore and raw metal into dust: 1 iron, copper or gold ore gives 2 dust (5 % a third), which smelts into ingots in a furnace. It needs 120 FE/t and 10 seconds per run. Ore goes into the feed hopper on top, the dust comes out at the bottom left. Power arrives on the right.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.plate: The plate mill (3×2×3) rolls ingots into plates: 1 iron, copper or gold ingot gives 1 plate, 7 steel give 1 steel sheet. The steel ingots arrive by item pipe from the step before into the hopper on top. The sheet leaves the plate mill at the bottom left and continues by item pipe to the CNC mill.
compendium.example_base_ore.note.sub: The substation (5×5×5) brings the power in over the overhead line and hands it out at four outputs, up to 131,072 FE/t each. Here the four outputs feed the six machines of this stage: the kiln and the CNC mill share the outputs of the blast furnace and the plate mill. The ore mill needs only 120 FE/t of it.
compendium.example_base_ore.text: Process metal into parts: the ore mill and hammer mill grind ore and ingots into dust for the furnace, the kiln fires coal into coke, the blast furnace turns iron ingots and coke into steel, the plate mill rolls it into steel sheet, the CNC mill mills parts from it, and those go into the component assembler by item pipe.
compendium.example_base_ore.title: Stage 4: Ore processing
compendium.example_base_power.note.bat: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE. The turbine charges it; power cables run from its first output to the power port of the containment and to the condenser (240 FE/t), the second output feeds the substation. Each port handles up to 131,072 FE/t.
compendium.example_base_power.note.cond: The large condenser (5×4×4) turns the exhaust steam of the turbine back into water: up to 640 mB/t at 240 FE/t. The exhaust steam comes in on top, the water comes out on the left and belongs back in the water treatment. For full output it needs coolant from a cooling tower (not shown here), otherwise it only cools with air and manages 40 mB/t.
compendium.example_base_power.note.hull: The containment (31×32×31) encloses the drive, steam generator, pump and pressurizer. Nothing passes through open walls: every line has one port outside and one inside, what flows in outside comes out inside. This is how feedwater, wet steam, emergency cooling, injection, relief, hydraulic water and power (up to 4,000 FE/t) get through. It needs 150 FE/t itself.
compendium.example_base_power.note.sep: The steam separator (3×6×3) dries the wet steam: 40 mB become 36 mB steam and 4 mB water. The wet steam comes in at the front bottom from the port outside the containment, the steam leaves at the top towards the turbine. The water comes out on the left and belongs back in the water treatment (not shown here). It needs no power.
compendium.example_base_power.note.sg: The steam generator (7×16×7) turns feedwater into wet steam: the heat comes from the hot primary water in its heating tubes, the steam itself only touches the secondary loop and is not radioactive. The feedwater comes in through the containment port, the wet steam leaves at the top and goes out through the containment. At most 1,280 mB/t, no power needed.
compendium.example_base_power.note.sub: The battery output feeds the substation (5×5×5). It is the start of the overhead line: the conductor rope hangs it onto pylons or the next substation, each line consists of two ropes. All substations on the grid share the power without loss and hand it out at four outputs, up to 131,072 FE/t each.
compendium.example_base_power.note.tur: The turbine (7×7×16) takes up to 400 mB/t of clean steam from the separator: 1 mB steam gives 256 FE, so up to 102,400 FE/t. The power goes by cable into the large battery, the exhaust steam from the condensate port by pipe to the condenser. Start/stop and the throttle control are in the menu.
compendium.example_base_power.text: Turn the reactor heat into power: the steam generator stands inside the containment, wet steam runs through the separator to the turbine, the turbine charges the battery and the substation distributes the power.
compendium.example_base_power.title: Stage 2: Steam and power
compendium.example_base_reactor.note.dri: The fuel rod drive (5×10×5) is the reactor: up to nine fuel rods move into its vessel and heat the primary water. Cold primary water comes from the pump into the cold input, hot water goes from the hot output to the steam generator. It needs 60 FE/t and hydraulic water, both through the ports of the containment: every stroke of the rods costs water.
compendium.example_base_reactor.note.eme: Emergency cooling (5×3×4) is the only source of primary water: it turns water into 320 mB/t of primary water and needs 360 FE/t. It goes into the emergency cooling port outside the containment and continues inside to the cold input of the drive. This is how you fill the loop for the first time; it stops when the drive is 75 % full and starts again when pressure drops below 20 %.
compendium.example_base_reactor.note.hul: The containment (31×32×31) encloses the drive, steam generator, pump and pressurizer. Nothing passes through open walls: every line has one port outside and one inside, what flows in outside comes out inside. This is how feedwater, wet steam, emergency cooling, injection, relief, hydraulic water and power (up to 4,000 FE/t) get through. It needs 150 FE/t itself.
compendium.example_base_reactor.note.pre: The pressurizer (3×8×3) hangs with its surge line on the cold side behind the pump and holds the pressure at 155 bar (50 %). Below that it heats with 1,200 FE/t. Above 90 % the relief valve on top opens: up to 160 mB/t of hot primary water go through the containment to the relief tank until the pressure is back at 85 %.
compendium.example_base_reactor.note.pum: The main coolant pump (3×3×3) drives the primary loop: it draws cold primary water from the steam generator and pushes it into the cold input of the drive, up to 2,560 mB/t. It needs 3,600 FE/t through the power port of the containment. If it stops, the flow breaks off and the core heats up.
compendium.example_base_reactor.note.sg: The steam generator (7×16×7) separates the two loops: hot primary water from the drive flows through its heating tubes and continues cold to the pump. The heat turns feedwater into wet steam that is not radioactive: 1 mB primary water gives 0.5 mB wet steam, at most 1,280 mB/t. Feedwater comes in through the containment, the wet steam leaves at the top. No power needed.
compendium.example_base_reactor.text: Build the reactor core and its primary loop: the drive heats the water, the pump circulates it, the steam generator takes the heat, and the pressurizer and emergency cooling protect the loop.
compendium.example_base_reactor.title: Stage 1: Reactor
compendium.example_base_storage.note.asm: The component assembler (5×4×5) builds to order from the terminal: it takes the ingredients from the racks and puts the result back. It needs 1,440 FE/t per working core. One data cable comes from the module rack, a second from the pattern rack. 1 core always runs, every free CPU core adds one (up to 8); each free GB of RAM lets a job hold 16 more units.
compendium.example_base_storage.note.cra: The crafting terminal is a storage terminal with a 3×3 crafting grid. It needs no power, but 2 CPU and 32 GB RAM on the network, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the module rack. When a grid slot runs empty while crafting, it pulls one more of the same item from the racks.
compendium.example_base_storage.note.pat: The pattern rack (4×5×3) stores 40 written pattern cards and needs only 12 FE/t. Through the data cable the component assembler sees the recipes without the cards sitting in it. Blank cards are built by the small parts assembler and written in the component assembler. Without power new jobs from these cards are blocked, running jobs continue.
compendium.example_base_storage.note.rac: The large server rack (4×5×3) has 40 bays for drives and needs 24 FE/t plus the power of each drive. Its data cable runs to the module rack and to the storage terminal. CPU and RAM modules need a bay too: here next to the drives or in the separate rack beside it. Without power the rack is offline, the items stay on the drives.

The normal server rack (2×4×2) has 12 bays, here only for CPU and RAM modules. They supply the computing power that terminals and component assemblers need. The data cable comes from the large rack and continues to the crafting terminal and the component assembler. It needs 24 FE/t plus the power of the modules.
compendium.example_base_storage.note.sub: The substation (5×5×5) brings the power in over the overhead line and hands it out at four outputs, up to 131,072 FE/t each. Here one output each supplies the large rack, the module rack, the component assembler and the pattern rack. The outputs convert by themselves: cables and machines receive FE.
compendium.example_base_storage.note.ter: The storage terminal shows all racks on the network as one single store. It needs no power, but 1 CPU and 16 GB RAM on the network, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the large rack. Left-click takes a stack, right-click half, shift-click in the inventory stores items.
compendium.example_base_storage.text: Add the ME system: the substation powers the racks and crafters, data cable ties the racks to the terminals, and the pattern rack tells the assembler what to autocraft. CPU and RAM go into the drive rack or a separate rack.
compendium.example_base_storage.title: Stage 5: Storage and autocrafting
compendium.example_chip_line.note.a: Makes Chip I: 1 wafer, 1 copper ingot and 2 redstone give 1 chip. The ingredients come in through an item pipe at the top input, the finished chip leaves at the bottom output. The input only accepts, the output only hands out.
compendium.example_chip_line.note.b: Makes Chip III: 1 Chip II, 3 pure silicon, 1 ender pearl, 1 diamond, 2 gold ingots and 1 HDPE sheet. Chip II comes from the soldering machine, the rest through a second item pipe on the same input. The clean room only works with a robot arm targeting it.
compendium.example_chip_line.note.c: Builds machine controllers and needs 1 chip for each, for example Chip III for the quantum computer and the fusion reactor. Casings, boards and cables come through a second item pipe on the same input. With a data cable and free computing power it works up to 128 times faster.
