compendium.example_chip_line.note.s: The soldering machine (2×2×3) makes Chip II: 1 Chip I, 1 pure silicon, 1 rubber, 2 photoresist and 2 gold ingots. Chip I comes from the micro assembler, the other ingredients through a second item pipe on the same input on top. No robot arm is needed.
compendium.example_chip_line.text: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_chip_line.title: Chip line
compendium.example_control_room.note.con: The command console needs 1 CPU and 16 GB RAM. It is a command line for every machine on the network: list shows them with numbers, info 1 all values, set 2 throttle 80 sets a value, watch 1 heat refreshes it every second. Its data cable comes from the rack, a second one continues to the cracker.
compendium.example_control_room.note.cra: The cracker is on the network by data cable as well, here behind the command console. info shows its values, set with enable off switches it off. A network may hold many machines, each counts once. Power and pipes are not shown here.
compendium.example_control_room.note.der: The oil derrick stands here as an example of a large machine: each one has a visible data port, a flange with a small screen. That is where the data cable from the data terminal ends. After that you read its fill level and output in the terminal and switch it on and off. It still needs power and pipes as usual.
compendium.example_control_room.note.des: The control desk (3×2×2) needs 2 CPU, 32 GB RAM and 24 FE/t of power at the back left. The data cable from the rack arrives at the back right. Three monitors show the selected machine, the list of all machines and the alarms. The red emergency stop pulls the rods of every fuel rod drive on the network.
compendium.example_control_room.note.rac: The server rack (2×4×2) holds the CPU and RAM modules of the network here. Each device takes its share: data terminal 1 CPU and 8 GB, command console 1 CPU and 16 GB, control desk 2 CPU and 32 GB. From the data port at the back one data cable each runs to the terminal, the console and the desk. It needs 24 FE/t plus the power of the modules.
compendium.example_control_room.note.ter: The data terminal needs 1 CPU and 8 GB RAM. It shows every machine on the network as a folder with readings and controls, plus search and a filter for faults. Its data cable comes from the rack, a second one continues to the data port of the oil derrick. A cable to any port is enough, it does not have to reach the controller.
compendium.example_control_room.text: Animated 3D build of a data network: a rack with the CPU and RAM modules, data terminal, command console and control desk, reaching an oil derrick and a cracker over data cables. CPU and RAM modules go into a bay of a rack, next to drives or in a rack of their own.
compendium.example_control_room.title: Data network and control room
compendium.example_decon_dock_supply.not: A fluid buffer (3×3×3) takes the naphtha that nobody needs here. It holds 256,000 mB of a single kind and needs no power. At the output on the opposite side it passes on up to 200 mB/t, for example to a cracker. Once it is full the column still backs up: empty it in time or pass the naphtha on.

A second fluid buffer takes the tar, because a buffer only ever holds one kind. It also holds 256,000 mB. Pass the tar on from the opposite output into a polymer plant (400 mB tar and 2 sulfur give 6 rubber) or empty the buffer before it is full.

The distillation column (5×18×5) supplies the diesel: 1,000 mB of crude oil become 350 mB diesel, 300 mB naphtha and 250 mB tar. The diesel goes by pipe to the diesel port of the dock. Naphtha and tar each run into a fluid buffer, because the column stops with one full tank. It needs 1,200 FE/t and crude oil from the derrick.

The decon dock (4×2×2) charges the battery of the decon robot (500 FE/t) and refills its cleaning agent with lye (10 mB/t). If its power is not enough, it burns diesel into battery charge (up to 5 mB/t, 200 FE per mB). The robot parks in reverse, its rear towards the back wall. The rubble comes out at the item output and is radioactive.

The chemical lab (3×3×3) makes the lye: 6 dried kelp + 400 mB water give 500 mB (2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds). Kelp goes into the item input on top, water by pipe on the right. The lye goes by pipe from the lye output on the left to the lye port of the dock.
compendium.example_decon_dock_supply.tex: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_exo_station_power.not: The medium battery (2×4×2) holds 16 million FE and delivers up to 16,000 FE/t per port. It charges from the solar field during the day and keeps the setup running at night: power cables run from its output to the exo station and the equipment assembler.

The equipment assembler (3×2×2) builds the exo pieces, the cores and the kit of the exo station. It works in a 3×3 grid and only accepts complete recipes. Power arrives on the right from the battery, ingredients by item pipe on top, the result comes out on the left.

The exo station (2×2×2) outfits the exoskeleton: place an exo piece with a right-click, then insert core and modules in the window. Power arrives on the right, the buffer holds 40,000 FE. While a core is inside it charges it with up to 20,000 FE per tick. Depending on the core tier a piece has 2 to 6 module slots.

The solar field (5×2×5) delivers up to 2,400 FE/t and tracks the sun: full output from mid-morning to mid-afternoon, nothing at night, 60 % less in rain. It needs open sky above its centre. The built-in buffer holds 1 million FE; the power cable runs from the output on the left to the battery.
compendium.example_exo_station_power.tex: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.ba: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and buffers the turbine power. Power cables run from its output to the power port of the containment (for the pump, drive and pressurizer inside), to emergency cooling, the intake pump, the water treatment and the other pumps. For the first start-up it has to be charged already: the pumps need power before any steam arrives.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.dr: The fuel rod drive (5×10×5) is the reactor: up to nine fuel rods move into its vessel and heat the primary water. Cold primary water comes from the pump into the cold input, hot water goes from the hot output to the steam generator. It needs 60 FE/t and hydraulic water, both through the ports of the containment: every stroke of the rods costs water.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.em: Emergency cooling (5×3×4) is the only source of primary water: it turns water into 320 mB/t of primary water and needs 360 FE/t. It goes into the emergency cooling port outside the containment and continues inside to the cold input of the drive. This is how you fill the loop for the first time; it stops when the drive is 75 % full and starts again when pressure drops below 20 %.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.hp: High-pressure injection (3×2×4) takes cold primary water from the relief tank and pushes up to 320 mB/t back into the primary loop through the injection port of the containment. It starts by itself when the pressurizer reports below 20 %, otherwise it waits on standby and needs no power. While running it draws 1,800 FE/t.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.hu: The containment (31×32×31) encloses the drive, steam generator, pump and pressurizer. Nothing passes through open walls: every line has one port outside and one inside, what flows in outside comes out inside. This is how feedwater, wet steam, emergency cooling, injection, relief, hydraulic water and power (up to 4,000 FE/t) get through. It needs 150 FE/t itself.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.in: The intake pump (9×9×9) stands by the lake, its two suction pipes have to stand in the water below. It delivers 5,120 mB/t at 1,200 FE/t, the water is not used up. The large pipe (2×2 thick, straight only) feeds the water treatment; two small outputs supply water for emergency cooling and for the hydraulic water of the containment.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.pr: The pressurizer (3×8×3) hangs with its surge line on the cold side behind the pump and holds the pressure at 155 bar (50 %). Below that it heats with 1,200 FE/t. Above 90 % the relief valve on top opens: up to 160 mB/t of hot primary water go through the containment to the relief tank until the pressure is back at 85 %.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.pu: The main coolant pump (3×3×3) drives the primary loop: it draws cold primary water from the steam generator and pushes it into the cold input of the drive, up to 2,560 mB/t. It needs 3,600 FE/t through the power port of the containment. If it stops, the flow breaks off and the core heats up.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.re: The relief tank (9×3×9) takes the hot primary water the pressurizer blows off (up to 160 mB/t): it comes from the relief port outside the containment into the top of the tank. Coolant from the cooling tower cools it down, 1 mB per mB of relief, which returns hot to the tower. The cold primary water stays as a reserve (128,000 mB) for high-pressure injection. No power needed.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.se: The steam separator (3×6×3) dries the wet steam: 40 mB become 36 mB steam and 4 mB water. The wet steam comes in at the front bottom from the port outside the containment, the steam leaves at the top towards the turbine, the water goes back on the left to a small input of the water treatment. It needs no power.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.sg: The steam generator (7×16×7) separates the two loops: hot primary water from the drive flows through its heating tubes and continues cold to the pump. The heat turns feedwater into wet steam that is not radioactive: 1 mB primary water gives 0.5 mB wet steam, at most 1,280 mB/t. Feedwater comes in through the containment, the wet steam leaves at the top. No power needed.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.to: The cooling tower (21×40×21) cools up to 960 mB/t of hot coolant, a little evaporates in the process. The cold coolant goes by pipe to the relief tank, the hot coolant comes back from there. Both ports sit side by side at the front bottom. It needs no power and is also enough for six small condensers.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.tr: The water treatment (7×4×5) turns water into feedwater: 1,280 mB/t at 720 FE/t. The water comes through the large pipe from the intake pump, the return water of the steam separator at a small input on top. The feedwater leaves at the front bottom towards the feedwater port outside the containment.
compendium.example_extended_loop.note.tu: The turbine (7×7×16) takes up to 400 mB/t of clean steam from the separator: 1 mB steam gives 256 FE, so up to 102,400 FE/t. The power goes by cable into the large battery. Start/stop and the throttle control are in the menu. Its exhaust steam belongs in a condenser, shown in the full loop.
compendium.example_extended_loop.text: Animated 3D build of the extended primary loop: the primary loop plus pressurizer, relief tank, high-pressure injection and a large cooling tower.
compendium.example_extended_loop.title: Extended Primary Loop
compendium.example_full_loop.note.bat: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and buffers the turbine power. Power cables run from its output to the power port of the containment (for the pump, drive and pressurizer inside), to emergency cooling, the intake pump, the water treatment and the other pumps. For the first start-up it has to be charged already: the pumps need power before any steam arrives.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.cond: The large condenser (5×4×4) turns up to 640 mB/t of turbine exhaust steam back into water and needs 240 FE/t. For every mB of exhaust steam 1 mB of coolant from the cooling tower turns hot and returns there. The exhaust steam comes in on top, the water leaves on the left to a small input of the water treatment. Without coolant it only manages 40 mB/t.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.drive: The fuel rod drive (5×10×5) is the reactor: up to nine fuel rods move into its vessel and heat the primary water. Cold primary water comes from the pump into the cold input, hot water goes from the hot output to the steam generator. It needs 60 FE/t and hydraulic water, both through the ports of the containment: every stroke of the rods costs water.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.emerg: Emergency cooling (5×3×4) is the only source of primary water: it turns water into 320 mB/t of primary water and needs 360 FE/t. It goes into the emergency cooling port outside the containment and continues inside to the cold input of the drive. This is how you fill the loop for the first time; it stops when the drive is 75 % full and starts again when pressure drops below 20 %.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.fwp: The large feedwater pump (3×2×4) draws the feedwater from the water treatment and pushes 960 mB/t on to the feedwater port outside the containment; inside it continues to the steam generator. It needs 480 FE/t. This closes the secondary loop: without feedwater the primary water stays hot and the core heats up.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.hpi: High-pressure injection (3×2×4) takes cold primary water from the relief tank and pushes up to 320 mB/t back into the primary loop through the injection port of the containment. It starts by itself when the pressurizer reports below 20 %, otherwise it waits on standby and needs no power. While running it draws 1,800 FE/t.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.hull: The containment (31×32×31) encloses the drive, steam generator, pump and pressurizer. Nothing passes through open walls: every line has one port outside and one inside, what flows in outside comes out inside. This is how feedwater, wet steam, emergency cooling, injection, relief, hydraulic water and power (up to 4,000 FE/t) get through. It needs 150 FE/t itself.
compendium.example_full_loop.note.intake: The intake pump (9×9×9) stands by the lake, its two suction pipes have to stand in the water below. compendium.example_fusion_fuel.note.b: The fusion reactor (21×10×21) needs deuterium, coolant and 1.8 billion FE from its buffer for ignition, charged through the power inputs. Switch it on in the terminal, then pick heating and plasma. The plasma burns for 10 seconds and returns 75 % of the ignition power at the power outputs, 105 % with 6 plasma optimizers. That is what the superconductor cable is for.
compendium.example_fusion_fuel.note.c: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and takes the power of the reactor. One battery port handles 131,072 FE/t, so use several batteries and cables side by side.

The cracker (3×3×3) cracks 20 mB/t of naphtha at 1,800 FE/t: 1,000 mB become 400 mB ethylene. The naphtha comes from a distillation column (not shown here) to the right input, the ethylene leaves the vessel at the top left and goes by pipe to the gas generator. One column yields a little over 2 mB/t of ethylene this way.

The gas generator (5×5×7) burns up to 6 mB/t of ethylene into 10,000 FE/t, that is 1,667 FE per mB. The gas arrives at the intake rail on the right, the power leaves on the left into the battery. It has no storage: what the battery does not take at once is lost. Without gas it stands still.

The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and buffers the power of the gas generator, which stores nothing itself. A power cable runs from the output to the substation, up to 131,072 FE/t per port. In the terminal you set up to what percentage it charges and from when it delivers.

The battery output feeds the substation (5×5×5). It is the start of the overhead line: the conductor rope hangs it onto pylons or the next substation, each line consists of two ropes. All substations on the grid share the power without loss and hand it out at four outputs, up to 131,072 FE/t each.

compendium.example_hydrogen_power.note.a: The electrolyzer (3×3×3) splits water: 1 mB water gives 1 mB hydrogen and 0.5 mB oxygen, up to 2 mB/t of hydrogen at 2,400 FE/t. Both gases go through separate pipes from the two gas ports to the fuel cell. When one of the gas tanks is full or water is missing, it stands still.
compendium.example_hydrogen_power.note.b: The fuel cell (3×3×3) turns hydrogen and oxygen (2 to 1) back into power: 15 mB/t hydrogen and 7 mB/t oxygen give 15,000 FE/t. Hydrogen arrives at the bottom right, oxygen at the top left, the power leaves at the back right. It has no storage, so a battery follows. The electrolyzer needs 18,000 FE/t for the same amount of gas: useful as emergency power.
compendium.example_hydrogen_power.note.c: The small battery (2×2×2) holds 4 million FE and takes up to 4,000 FE/t. It catches the power of the fuel cell, which stores nothing itself. For the full 15,000 FE/t of the cell you need a medium battery (16,000 FE/t per port) or several small ones.

The component assembler (5×4×5) builds to order from the terminal out of the rack stock and needs 1,440 FE/t per working core. Data cables come from the module rack and the pattern rack. The milled parts from the CNC mill arrive by item pipe at the input on top and are stored right away. Every free CPU core adds a core (up to 8).

The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and buffers the turbine power. Power cables run from its output to the power port of the containment (for the pump, drive and pressurizer inside), to emergency cooling, the intake pump, the water treatment and the other pumps. For the first start-up it has to be charged already: the pumps need power before any steam arrives.

The blast furnace (5×4×5) melts 8 iron ingots and 8 coke or coal into 8 steel ingots, one batch takes 10 seconds at 3,600 FE/t. Both go into the scrap bin in the back: the coke by item pipe from the kiln, the iron through a second pipe on the same input. The steel ingots come out of the ladle in front and go by item pipe to the plate mill.

The CNC mill (2×2×3) mills steel sheet into parts for later machines: 61 lead and 4 steel sheets make 1 lead shielding, 30 osmium and 8 steel sheets make 1 osmium heat plate. The sheet arrives by item pipe from the plate mill high on the back of the feeder tower, lead or osmium through a second pipe on the same input. The finished part comes out on the left and goes by item pipe to the component assembler.

The distillation column (5×18×5) splits 20 mB/t of crude oil at 1,200 FE/t: 1,000 mB become 300 mB naphtha, 350 mB diesel and 250 mB tar, plus 1 sulfur dust. Naphtha goes by pipe to the cracker, tar to the polymer plant, diesel to the second gas generator. When one of the three tanks is full it stops.

The cracker (3×3×3) cracks 20 mB/t of naphtha at 1,800 FE/t: 1,000 mB become 400 mB ethylene. The naphtha arrives by pipe from the column at the right input, the ethylene leaves the vessel at the top left. It is a gas, but runs through the same kind of pipe on to the gas generator.

The crafting terminal is a storage terminal with a 3×3 crafting grid. It needs no power, but 2 CPU and 32 GB RAM on the network, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the module rack. When a grid slot runs empty while crafting, it pulls one more of the same item from the racks.

The oil derrick (5×15×5) stands on an oil well: its core has to lie beneath the tower. It pumps 40 mB/t of crude oil and needs 450 FE/t. The crude goes by pipe into the crude input of the distillation column. When the well is empty it waits until it refills (1 % per Minecraft day).

The fuel rod drive (5×10×5) is the reactor: up to nine fuel rods move into its vessel and heat the primary water. Cold primary water comes from the pump into the cold input, hot water goes from the hot output to the steam generator. It needs 60 FE/t and hydraulic water, both through the ports of the containment: every stroke of the rods costs water.

Emergency cooling (5×3×4) is the only source of primary water: it turns water into 320 mB/t of primary water and needs 360 FE/t. It goes into the emergency cooling port outside the containment and continues inside to the cold input of the drive. This is how you fill the loop for the first time; it stops when the drive is 75 % full and starts again when pressure drops below 20 %.

The gas generator (5×5×7) burns up to 6 mB/t of ethylene from the cracker and delivers 10,000 FE/t for it, that is 1,667 FE per mB. The gas arrives at the intake rail on the right, the power leaves on the left. It has no storage: what nobody takes is lost. That is why its power cable leads into the large battery.

A second gas generator burns the diesel from the column: diesel burns just as fast and yields just as much as ethylene (6 mB/t for 10,000 FE/t), but the tank may hold only one kind. This keeps the diesel tank from filling up and the column from stopping. Its power goes straight into the second input of the substation.

The hammer mill (3×2×3) crushes finished ingots: 1 iron, copper or gold ingot gives 1 dust, with a 25 % chance of a second (50 % with one, 100 % with two cycle modules). Ingots go into the hopper on top, the dust leaves at the bottom left, power arrives on the right. Ores remain the job of the ore mill.

High-pressure injection (3×2×4) takes cold primary water from the relief tank and pushes up to 320 mB/t back into the primary loop through the injection port of the containment. It starts by itself when the pressurizer reports below 20 %, otherwise it waits on standby and needs no power. While running it draws 1,800 FE/t.

The containment (31×32×31) encloses the drive, steam generator, pump and pressurizer. Nothing passes through open walls: every line has one port outside and one inside, what flows in outside comes out inside. This is how feedwater, wet steam, emergency cooling, injection, relief, hydraulic water and power (up to 4,000 FE/t) get through. It needs 150 FE/t itself.

The intake pump (9×9×9) stands by the lake, its two suction pipes have to stand in the water below. It delivers 5,120 mB/t at 1,200 FE/t, the water is not used up. The large pipe (2×2 thick, straight only) feeds the water treatment; two small outputs supply water for emergency cooling and for the hydraulic water of the containment.

The kiln (3×3×3) fires 2 coal or charcoal into 1 coke, one firing takes 5 seconds at 300 FE/t. The coal goes in on top, the coke leaves the kiln at the lower side and goes by item pipe into the scrap bin of the blast furnace. The same kiln also fires zirconium ingots, glass plates and glass seals. It also smelts everything a normal furnace smelts with power, ores and clay into bricks included.

The ore mill (3×3×4) grinds ore and raw metal into dust: 1 iron, copper or gold ore gives 2 dust (5 % a third), which smelts into ingots in a furnace. It needs 120 FE/t and 10 seconds per run. Ore goes into the feed hopper on top, the dust comes out at the bottom left. Power arrives on the right.

The pattern rack (4×5×3) stores 40 written pattern cards and needs only 12 FE/t. Through the data cable the component assembler sees the recipes without the cards sitting in it. Blank cards are built by the small parts assembler and written in the component assembler. Without power new jobs from these cards are blocked, running jobs continue.

The plate mill (3×2×3) rolls ingots into plates: 1 iron, copper or gold ingot gives 1 plate, 7 steel give 1 steel sheet. The steel ingots arrive by item pipe from the step before into the hopper on top. The sheet leaves the plate mill at the bottom left and continues by item pipe to the CNC mill.

The polymer plant (3×3×3) receives the tar from the column at the tar port at the back left bottom. 2 sulfur + 400 mB tar give 6 rubber (2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds), 1 coal + 200 mB tar give 2 coke (1,800 FE/t, 8 seconds). Sulfur and coal go into the item input on top, the result slides out over the chute on the left.

The pressurizer (3×8×3) hangs with its surge line on the cold side behind the pump and holds the pressure at 155 bar (50 %). Below that it heats with 1,200 FE/t. Above 90 % the relief valve on top opens: up to 160 mB/t of hot primary water go through the containment to the relief tank until the pressure is back at 85 %.

The main coolant pump (3×3×3) drives the primary loop: it draws cold primary water from the steam generator and pushes it into the cold input of the drive, up to 2,560 mB/t. It needs 3,600 FE/t through the power port of the containment. If it stops, the flow breaks off and the core heats up.

The large server rack (4×5×3) has 40 bays for drives and needs 24 FE/t plus the power of each drive. Its data cable runs to the module rack and to the storage terminal. CPU and RAM modules need a bay too: here next to the drives or in the separate rack beside it. Without power the rack is offline, the items stay on the drives.

The normal server rack (2×4×2) has 12 bays, here only for CPU and RAM modules. They supply the computing power that terminals and component assemblers need. The data cable comes from the large rack and continues to the crafting terminal and the component assembler. It needs 24 FE/t plus the power of the modules.

The relief tank (9×3×9) takes the hot primary water the pressurizer blows off (up to 160 mB/t): it comes from the relief port outside the containment into the top of the tank. Coolant from the cooling tower cools it down, 1 mB per mB of relief, which returns hot to the tower. The cold primary water stays as a reserve (128,000 mB) for high-pressure injection. No power needed.

The steam separator (3×6×3) dries the wet steam: 40 mB become 36 mB steam and 4 mB water. The wet steam comes in at the front bottom from the port outside the containment, the steam leaves at the top towards the turbine, the water goes back on the left to a small input of the water treatment. It needs no power.

The steam generator (7×16×7) separates the two loops: hot primary water from the drive flows through its heating tubes and continues cold to the pump. The heat turns feedwater into wet steam that is not radioactive: 1 mB primary water gives 0.5 mB wet steam, at most 1,280 mB/t. Feedwater comes in through the containment, the wet steam leaves at the top. No power needed.

The substation (5×5×5) is the power hub of the plant: it receives power from the second output of the large battery and from the second gas generator. Through four outputs (up to 131,072 FE/t each) it supplies the two racks, the component assembler and pattern rack, and the ore processing.

The storage terminal shows all racks on the network as one single store. It needs no power, but 1 CPU and 16 GB RAM on the network, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the large rack. Left-click takes a stack, right-click half, shift-click in the inventory stores items.

The cooling tower (21×40×21) cools up to 960 mB/t of hot coolant, a little evaporates in the process. The cold coolant goes by pipe to the relief tank, the hot coolant comes back from there. Both ports sit side by side at the front bottom. It needs no power and is also enough for six small condensers.

The water treatment (7×4×5) turns water into feedwater: 1,280 mB/t at 720 FE/t. The water comes through the large pipe from the intake pump, the return water of the steam separator at a small input on top. The feedwater leaves at the front bottom towards the feedwater port outside the containment.

The turbine (7×7×16) takes up to 400 mB/t of clean steam from the separator: 1 mB steam gives 256 FE, so up to 102,400 FE/t. The power goes by cable into the large battery. Start/stop and the throttle control are in the menu. Its exhaust steam belongs in a condenser, shown in the full loop.

compendium.example_server_room_power.not: The computing cluster is the biggest consumer in the room: 780 FE/t at the red port. In return it gives the data network 32 CPU cores and 512 GB RAM. Power turns into heat inside it: without cooling water on the blue port (8,000 mB tank) CPU output drops from heat 500, at 1,000 it shuts down.

The control desk (3×2×2) needs only 24 FE/t, power arrives at the back left. Without power its screens stay dark. For the display it also needs a data cable at the back right and 2 CPU and 32 GB RAM on the network.

The large server rack (4×5×3) needs 24 FE/t plus the power of every drive and module. Power arrives at the red port at the back, the turquoise data port sits next to it. Without power it is offline: the items stay on the drives but cannot be reached.

The substation (5×5×5) brings the power into the server room over the overhead line and hands it out at four outputs, up to 131,072 FE/t each. Here one power cable each runs to the large rack (24 FE/t plus drives), the computing cluster (780 FE/t) and the control desk (24 FE/t). The fourth output stays free.
compendium.example_server_room_power.tex: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_solar_and_wind.note.b: The medium battery (2×4×2) holds 16 million FE. The solar field and the wind turbine charge it through the same input; it evens out night, lulls and gusts. A power cable runs from the output to the substation, up to 16,000 FE/t.
compendium.example_solar_and_wind.note.s: The solar field (5×2×5) delivers up to 2,400 FE/t and tracks the sun: full output from mid-morning to mid-afternoon, nothing at night, 60 % less in rain. It needs open sky above its centre. The built-in buffer holds 1 million FE; the power cable runs from the output on the left to the battery.

The battery output feeds the substation (5×5×5). It is the start of the overhead line: the conductor rope hangs it onto pylons or the next substation, each line consists of two ropes. All substations on the grid share the power without loss and hand it out at four outputs, up to 131,072 FE/t each.
compendium.example_solar_and_wind.note.w: The small wind turbine (7×14×5) delivers up to 352 FE/t, on flat land about 96 FE/t on average. The output depends on hub height, open surroundings and wind strength: only 30 % at Y 40, full from Y 160. It has no storage, so its power goes from the output on the right into the battery.
compendium.example_solar_and_wind.text: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_solar_and_wind.title: Solar and wind
compendium.example_starter_power.note.a: The coal generator (3×3×3) burns coal, charcoal, wood or lava buckets into 720 FE/t; one piece of coal lasts 40 seconds. Fuel goes in on the right (hoppers work), the power leaves on the left into the battery. It has no storage and only burns while something takes the power.
compendium.example_starter_power.note.b: The small battery (2×2×2) holds 4 million FE and delivers up to 4,000 FE/t. It buffers the power of the coal generator and passes it on to the small parts assembler. This keeps the assembler running when the coal briefly runs out, and the generator does not burn for nothing.
compendium.example_starter_power.note.c: The small parts assembler (3×2×3) is the first machine. It needs 960 FE/t while building, for the reactor assembler kit only 480 FE/t: one coal generator is enough for that. Power and items go in on the right, the result comes out on the left. Its energy store holds 300,000 FE.
compendium.example_starter_power.text: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_starter_power.title: Starter power
compendium.example_steam_path.note.cond: The large condenser (5×4×4) turns the exhaust steam of the turbine back into water: up to 640 mB/t at 240 FE/t. The exhaust steam comes in on top, the water comes out on the left and belongs back in the water treatment. For full output it needs coolant from a cooling tower (not shown here), otherwise it only cools with air and manages 40 mB/t.
compendium.example_steam_path.note.fwp: The large feedwater pump (3×2×4) draws the feedwater from the water treatment and pushes 960 mB/t on to the feedwater port outside the containment; inside it continues to the steam generator. It needs 480 FE/t. This closes the secondary loop: without feedwater the primary water stays hot and the core heats up.
compendium.example_steam_path.note.hull: The containment (31×32×31) encloses the drive, steam generator, pump and pressurizer. Nothing passes through open walls: every line has one port outside and one inside, what flows in outside comes out inside. This is how feedwater, wet steam, emergency cooling, injection, relief, hydraulic water and power (up to 4,000 FE/t) get through. It needs 150 FE/t itself.
compendium.example_steam_path.note.sep: The steam separator (3×6×3) dries the wet steam: 40 mB become 36 mB steam and 4 mB water. The wet steam comes in at the front bottom from the port outside the containment, the steam leaves at the top towards the turbine, the water goes back on the left to a small input of the water treatment. It needs no power.
compendium.example_steam_path.note.sg: The steam generator (7×16×7) turns feedwater into wet steam: the heat comes from the hot primary water in its heating tubes, the steam itself only touches the secondary loop and is not radioactive. The feedwater comes in through the containment port, the wet steam leaves at the top and goes out through the containment. At most 1,280 mB/t, no power needed.
compendium.example_steam_path.note.treat: The water treatment (7×4×5) turns water into feedwater: 1,280 mB/t at 720 FE/t. Fresh water comes through the large pipe from the intake pump, the return water from the steam separator and the condenser at the small inputs on top. The feedwater leaves at the front bottom towards the feedwater pump.
compendium.example_steam_path.note.tur: The turbine (7×7×16) takes up to 400 mB/t of clean steam from the separator: 1 mB steam gives 256 FE, so up to 102,400 FE/t. Its exhaust steam goes from the condensate port by pipe to the condenser. The power output is not shown here: a battery belongs there.
compendium.example_steam_path.text: Animated 3D build of the secondary loop: steam generator inside the containment, separator, turbine, condenser, water treatment and feedwater pump, connected by pipes.
compendium.example_steam_path.title: Steam path
compendium.example_storage_system.note.a: The component assembler (5×4×5) builds to order from the terminal: it takes the ingredients from the racks and puts the result back. It needs 1,440 FE/t per working core. One data cable comes from the module rack, a second from the pattern rack. 1 core always runs, every free CPU core adds one (up to 8); each free GB of RAM lets a job hold 16 more units.
compendium.example_storage_system.note.b: The large battery (3×5×3) holds 64 million FE and delivers up to 131,072 FE/t per port. Power cables run from the first output to both racks (24 FE/t each plus drives and modules), from the second to the component assembler and the pattern rack. It is charged through the input on the other side.
compendium.example_storage_system.note.c: The crafting terminal is a storage terminal with a 3×3 crafting grid. It needs no power, but 2 CPU and 32 GB RAM on the network, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the module rack. When a grid slot runs empty while crafting, it pulls one more of the same item from the racks.
compendium.example_storage_system.note.p: The pattern rack (4×5×3) stores 40 written pattern cards and needs only 12 FE/t. Through the data cable the component assembler sees the recipes without the cards sitting in it. Blank cards are built by the small parts assembler and written in the component assembler. Without power new jobs from these cards are blocked, running jobs continue.
compendium.example_storage_system.note.r: The large server rack (4×5×3) has 40 bays for drives and needs 24 FE/t plus the power of each drive. Its data cable runs to the module rack and to the storage terminal. CPU and RAM modules need a bay too: here next to the drives or in the separate rack beside it. Without power the rack is offline, the items stay on the drives.

The normal server rack (2×4×2) has 12 bays, here only for CPU and RAM modules. They supply the computing power that terminals and component assemblers need. The data cable comes from the large rack and continues to the crafting terminal and the component assembler. It needs 24 FE/t plus the power of the modules.
compendium.example_storage_system.note.t: The storage terminal shows all racks on the network as one single store. It needs no power, but 1 CPU and 16 GB RAM on the network, otherwise it will not open. Its data cable comes from the large rack. Left-click takes a stack, right-click half, shift-click in the inventory stores items.
compendium.example_storage_system.text: Animated 3D build of a basic digital storage: battery, a rack with the drives, a separate rack for CPU and RAM modules, storage and crafting terminals, component assembler and pattern rack, joined by power and data cables. CPU and RAM modules go into a bay of a rack: next to the drives or in a rack of their own.
compendium.example_storage_system.title: Basic storage system
compendium.example_uranium_line.note.aci: The acid plant (5×3×4) supplies both acids: 1 sulfur dust + 400 mB water give 500 mB sulfuric acid, 1 fluorite + 250 mB sulfuric acid give 500 mB hydrofluoric acid. The sulfuric acid goes by pipe to the leaching plant, the hydrofluoric acid through its own pipe to the UF6 conversion. When an acid tank is full it stands still.
compendium.example_uranium_line.note.cen: The enrichment centrifuge (3×4×3) turns 1 UF6 cylinder into 2 enriched and 1 depleted uranium (240 FE/t, 10 seconds). The cylinders go in on top, the uranium comes out at the bottom left and continues by item pipe to the fuel pellet factory. Yellowcake works directly as well, but yields only 1 enriched uranium from 2 yellowcake.
compendium.example_uranium_line.note.lea: The leaching plant (5×3×4) dissolves the uranium: 2 yellowcake + 250 mB sulfuric acid + 500 mB water give 2 uranium oxide and with a 50 % chance 1 uranium sludge (1,200 FE/t, 10 seconds). Yellowcake comes in on top from the ore mill, the acid by pipe from the acid plant. The uranium oxide continues by item pipe to the UF6 conversion.
compendium.example_uranium_line.note.mil: The ore mill (3×3×4) grinds uranium ore: 1 ore gives 2 yellowcake, with a 25 % chance of a third (120 FE/t, 10 seconds). The ore goes into the feed hopper on top, the yellowcake goes by item pipe from the output at the bottom left to the leaching plant.
compendium.example_uranium_line.note.pel: The fuel pellet factory (5×3×4) presses 2 uranium oxide dust + 1 enriched uranium into 3 uranium pellets (1,800 FE/t, 8 seconds) and sinters 2 pellets into 1 uranium core (2,700 FE/t, 12 seconds). The enriched uranium comes from the centrifuge and belongs in the extra slot, the oxide dust in the input on top. 15 cores fill one fuel rod casing.
compendium.example_uranium_line.note.uf6: The UF6 conversion plant (5×4×4) turns 2 uranium oxide + 300 mB hydrofluoric acid into 1 UF6 cylinder (2,400 FE/t, 15 seconds). The oxide comes from the leaching plant into the input on top, the hydrofluoric acid by pipe from the acid plant. Without acid it also works with 1 fluorite in the extra slot. The cylinders go by item pipe to the centrifuge.
compendium.example_uranium_line.text: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_uranium_line.title: Uranium line
compendium.example_waste_line.note.a: The reprocessing plant (5×4×5) breaks down decayed fuel: 1 piece gives 6 uranium oxide dust and 2 ash, plus enriched uranium with a 30 % chance and plutonium oxide with 40 %. The waste goes into the yellow input on top, the results come out at the bottom left. The ash goes by item pipe to the waste crusher.
compendium.example_waste_line.note.b: The waste crusher (3×3×3) grinds the ash: 3 ash give 2 lead dust, with a 75 % chance 1 zirconium dust and with a 30 % chance 1 neptunium oxide (1,200 FE/t, 8 seconds). The ash goes in on top, the dust comes out at the copper-orange output. It goes back into the assembler recipes: this closes the loop.
compendium.example_waste_line.note.c: The vitrification plant (3×3×3) works in two steps: 8 filter residue + 400 mB sulfuric acid give 500 mB high-level liquid waste (4,500 FE/t, 15 seconds), then 4 sand + 500 mB of it give 1 glass canister (7,500 FE/t, 30 seconds). Waste and sand go in on top, the acid comes from the acid plant. The canister goes by item pipe into the waste repository.
compendium.example_waste_line.note.d: The waste repository (5×9×5) accepts the glass canisters at the drop slot: up to 4 pieces go down the shaft every second. It needs 600 FE/t, but only while there is waste. Spent fuel rods, filter residue and spent resin may go in as well. Nothing can be taken back out: the repository is final.
compendium.example_waste_line.note.e: The acid plant (5×3×4) supplies the sulfuric acid for vitrification: 1 sulfur dust + 400 mB water give 500 mB (1,800 FE/t, 5 seconds). Sulfur goes into the input on top, water by pipe. The acid goes by pipe to the sulfuric acid port at the back right of the vitrification plant.
compendium.example_waste_line.text: Animated 3D build of this plant, machine by machine, with the connections between them.
compendium.example_waste_line.title: Waste line
compendium.examples_all.text: Animated 3D builds of plants, sorted by area: manufacturing, chemistry, robotics, computing, energy and reactor.
compendium.examples_all.title: Overview
compendium.exo.text:
The **exoskeleton** is armor with **module slots**: four pieces (**helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots**) and the **Exo Core** as battery. The modules (run, jump, jetpack, magnet and more) sit in the pieces and work as long as the core has **power**.
## The four pieces
Armor a bit stronger than **netherite** (helmet 4, chestplate 9, leggings 7, boots 4, toughness 3 per piece)
An exo piece is the shell for **modules**, the modules stay stored in the piece
## The Exo Core
**Tier 1 to 5** with a battery of **100 kFE, 400 kFE, 1.6 MFE, 6.4 MFE and 25.6 MFE**
The tier also sets the **module slots per piece**: **2 to 6**
The core sits in your **inventory** (any slot) and supplies power to all worn pieces
## Charging
In the **Exo Station**: power from any side, up to **20,000 FE per tick** into the core
With any **charger** (the core has an energy interface but gives nothing back out)
**Pocket batteries** in your inventory top the core up when the nano bots need power
The core also powers the **nano bots** (20 FE per work step)
## Power in use
Every module costs **10 FE per tier and second** while the piece is **worn**
If the core is empty or missing, **all modules are off**; after charging they come back within a second
Some modules need extra power when they act (jetpack while rising, magnet per item, mining per extra block)
## Crafting
Everything is made in the **Equipment Assembler**
**Core tier 1** from steel sheets, control board II, copper coils and **Chip I**; **tier 2** and **3** from a core plus **Chip II** or **Chip III**; **tier 4** and **5** from a core, **Chip III** and **elite** or **ultimate circuits**
The pieces from steel sheets and control board I
## Next
Install in the **Exo Station**, the modules on the following pages
compendium.exo.tip: Without a core in your inventory no module does anything: always carry it.
compendium.exo.title: Exoskeleton
compendium.exo_modules.text:
**Exo Modules** boost a piece of the exoskeleton. There are **seven kinds** in **five tiers** (I to V), each module is its own item. They are inserted in the **Exo Station**.
## Which module goes where
**Boots**: Jump (jump strength), Suspension (safe fall)
**Leggings**: Run (movement speed), Step (step height)
**Chestplate**: Plating (armor), Mining (mining speed), Reach (block reach)
The station accepts a module **only in the matching piece**
How many slots a piece has depends on the **Exo Core tier**: 2 to 6
## Effect per tier
Run **+10 %**, Step **+0.2 blocks**, Jump **+10 %**, Suspension **+2 blocks**
Plating **+1**, Mining **+20 %**, Reach **+0.5 blocks**
## Power
Modules only work on the **worn** piece and only if an **Exo Core with charge** is in your **inventory**
Every second the piece draws **10 FE per tier and module** from the core
With an empty core the modules are **off**; after charging they come back within a second
## Crafting
All modules are made in the **Equipment Assembler**
Tier **I** from 4 steel sheets, 2 control boards I, the kind-specific ingredient and **2 Chip I**
Higher tiers need the **module of the previous tier** plus:
**II**: 4 Chip I, 2 control boards I
**III**: 2 Chip II, 2 control boards II
**IV**: 4 Chip II, 2 control boards II, 2 elite circuits
**V**: 3 Chip III (clean room only), 2 control boards III, 2 ultimate circuits
compendium.exo_modules.tip: An empty core switches all modules off. Charge it in the Exo Station, with a charger or with pocket batteries in your inventory.
compendium.exo_modules.title: Exo Modules
compendium.exo_modules_battery.text:
An **Exo Module** for the **leggings**, tiers I to V. Inserting and crafting work like the other modules.
## Effect
Raises the **capacity of the Exo Core** by **20 %** per tier, tier V doubles it
Cores in your **inventory** get the bonus as long as the leggings with the module are **worn** (within a second)
If several battery modules are fitted, only the **strongest** counts
## Power
The battery module needs **no power** and works even with an empty core
Take the leggings off and the capacity drops again, but the stored charge is kept and is available again after putting them back on
compendium.exo_modules_battery.tip: Charge above the normal capacity is not lost, it just cannot be used without the leggings.
compendium.exo_modules_battery.title: Battery Module
compendium.exo_modules_hotbar.text:
An **Exo Module** for the chestplate, one tier. Inserting, power and crafting work like the other modules.
## Second Bar
The **inventory row above the hotbar** shows as a second bar left of the hotbar as long as the module has **power**
**Alt+1 to Alt+9** swaps the **held item** with that slot of the second bar, pressing again swaps back
The keys can be rebound under Controls / NuclearSQ
## Power
**10 FE per second** like all modules
compendium.exo_modules_hotbar.tip: Swapping works in the world only, not while a screen is open.
compendium.exo_modules_hotbar.title: Hotbar Module
compendium.exo_modules_mining.text:
Four more **Exo Modules** for chestplate and helmet. Inserting, power and crafting work like the other modules.
## Area Mining (chestplate)
Three modules: **2×2**, **3×3** and **5×5** (one tier per size)
When **sneaking** and mining, an **area across the face you hit** goes with it: for 2×2 towards the side of the hit point, otherwise around the block
Only blocks your **tool** mines properly; **chests and machines** stay
## Vein Mining (chestplate)
**Tier I to V** = up to **6, 12, 24, 48 or 96** connected blocks of the same kind (like the Vein Miner, but with sneaking)
If area and vein are both installed, the **area** applies
**5 FE** per extra block from the core, without power or with a **broken tool** mining stops
Every block goes through **normal mining**: drops, durability and protection mods work as for a single block
## Claws (chestplate)
In the air at a wall **hold the right mouse button**: you slide about **2 more blocks** and then **hang**
While hanging you can **build and mine**, no fall damage
## Ore Finder (helmet)
**Tier I to V**: range **8, 16, 24, 32 or 40** blocks
Every second the **action bar** shows arrow, distance and kind of the nearest **ore** (loaded areas only)
## Power
Base cost **10 FE per tier and second** like all modules; mining costs **5 FE** more per extra block
compendium.exo_modules_mining.tip: Sneaking turns area and vein mining on: mining normally breaks only the single block.
compendium.exo_modules_mining.title: Mining, Climbing and Search Modules
compendium.exo_modules_more.text:
Six more **Exo Modules** in tiers **I to V**. Inserting, power and crafting work like the other modules.
## Jetpack (chestplate)
**Hold jump** = rise, **release** = sink slowly, **Sneak** = sink fast
**Ctrl** in the air = **speed boost**, about twice as fast (up to 12 blocks/s)
From **tier 2**: **double jump** = hover on and off
Keys can be changed in Options > Controls > NuclearSQ (**Jetpack up**, **Jetpack down**, **Jetpack boost**)
Rising and hovering cost **100 FE per tick** from the Exo Core, sinking, gliding and boost are free
The tier sets the **climb speed**; while the jetpack runs there is **no fall damage**
## Strength (chestplate)
**+1 melee damage** per tier
## Fire Protection (leggings)
**-20 % fire and lava damage** per tier, at tier **V** (or a total of 5) you are **immune**
## Underwater Breathing (helmet)
**+4 oxygen bonus** per tier, at tier **V** air lasts **21 times longer**
## Looting (helmet)
Killing gives **0 up to tier** extra on stackable drops
## Fortune (chestplate)
When mining, drops that are **not the block itself** (ores, gems) give **0 up to tier** extra
## Base cost
Every module costs **10 FE per tier and second** like all the others, an empty core switches these modules off as well
compendium.exo_modules_more.tip: The jetpack needs extra power while rising: a charged core in your inventory is required.
compendium.exo_modules_more.title: More Exo Modules
compendium.exo_modules_rd.text:
Two more **Exo Modules** in tiers **I to V**. Inserting, power and crafting work like the other modules.
## Radiation Shield (helmet)
Works in the **radiation system** like a part of the **hazmat suit** and like the **filter mask** at once, as long as the helmet has **power**
**Shielding** against outside radiation in the helmet share: **20, 35, 50, 65 or 80 %** (the helmet is a quarter of the whole suit)
**Dust** from the ground and rain: **30 to 70 %** less intake, **steam at leaks**: **50 to 95 %**
The module needs **no filter** and does not wear out
Tier **V** replaces the **filter mask** and beats it as a helmet, but does **not replace the whole suit**: chest, legs and boots of the hazmat suit are still needed
If you wear a mask or the suit helmet those apply; the module works on the **Exo helmet**
## Magnet (chestplate)
Pulls items in range to you: radius **3, 5, 7, 10 or 14** blocks
Works **every 5 ticks** and only while active
**2 FE** per pulled item from the Exo Core, free in creative mode
**Freshly thrown** items (pickup delay) stay where they are
## Power
Base cost **10 FE per tier and second** like all modules
compendium.exo_modules_rd.tip: The radiation shield on the Exo helmet costs power but no filters: an empty core switches it off.
compendium.exo_modules_rd.title: Radiation Shield and Magnet Modules
compendium.exo_station.text:
The **Exo Station** is a **chamber** (**2×2×2**) for the **exoskeleton**. You lay an **exo piece** (helmet, chestplate, leggings or boots) inside by clicking the chamber **with the piece in your hand**: it then lies visibly on the couch. Another right-click (without a piece in your hand) opens the window with the **Exo Core** and the **module slots**.
## Power
The **power port** is on the right side of the chamber (seen from the front), it has a buffer of **40,000 FE**
As long as a **core** is inside, it pushes up to **20,000 FE per tick** into its battery
The core holds **100 kFE**, **400 kFE**, **1.6 MFE**, **6.4 MFE** or **25.6 MFE** (tier 1 to 5), the window shows the charge
## Module slots
**2** to **6** slots per piece, depending on the **core tier**
The modules are stored as a list **in the piece** and travel with it
While modules are inside, the **core** stays in the chamber
The modules are described on the Exo Modules pages (Small Parts Assembler, chip by tier)
## Setting up and crafting
The **kit** is made in the **Equipment Assembler** from casing, power port, data port, a **Robot Arm**, steel sheets, control board II and copper coils
Breaking it gives the kit back, an inserted piece and the core drop out
compendium.exo_station.tip: The core stays in the station while modules are inside: take out the modules first, then swap the core.
compendium.exo_station.title: Exo Station
compendium.fast_breeder.keywords: breeder, breeder reactor, FBR, SNR, fast reactor, neptunium, plutonium
compendium.fast_breeder.text:
## Fast breeder (9×11×9)
Sodium-cooled reactor with its **own loop**: four **driver cores** (uranium core or plutonium core) heat the sodium, which turns feedwater into **wet steam**
Power follows the steam demand: up to 60 mB/t per driver, four drivers 240 mB/t (1920 FE/t in the turbine). One core burns **12 minutes** at full load
In the blanket **eight breeder blanket elements** breed in the neutron flux of the drivers into **bred elements** (4 minutes at full load, 25 % faster with plutonium drivers)
Ports seen from the front: power bottom left, **sodium** right at the back (level 3), feedwater left (level 3), **wet steam** top left, items in on **top**, bred elements out bottom right
## Operation
Slots of the item input: 1 to 4 drivers, 5 to 12 blankets
Put sodium into the loop by bucket (right-click) or pipe, below **8,000 mB** the plant stops
A **sodium leak** (wear: the longer it runs, the likelier) loses 40 mB/t and radiates: switch off and **maintain** in the terminal
The plant radiates while running, bred elements strongly
## Chain
The centrifuge gives **depleted uranium**, reprocessing bred elements returns it
30 of them + zircaloy + steel → **breeder blanket element** (reactor assembler)
**Bred element** → reprocessing → plutonium oxide, uranium, ash
4 plutonium oxide → **plutonium core**
compendium.fast_breeder.tip: A plutonium core as driver breeds faster. With four drivers and eight blankets about 24 bred elements come out per core lifetime, enough for six plutonium cores.
compendium.fast_breeder.title: Fast breeder
compendium.fluid_buffer.text:
The **fluid buffer** (**3×3×3**) is an upright tank for **one** fluid or gas of any kind.
## Operation
Holds **256000 mB**, takes through the **input** and pushes by itself into attached pipes through the **output** on the opposite side (200 mB/t each). It needs no power. Once one kind is inside it takes no other until it is empty.
## Setup
Kit from the Heavy Assembler.
compendium.fluid_buffer.tip: Put it behind the diesel or tar output of the distillation column so that it does not stand still when nobody takes the product.
compendium.fluid_buffer.title: Fluid Buffer
compendium.fluids.contaminated_steam.tex: If a **heating tube** in the steam generator breaks, its wet steam port puts out contaminated steam. Separator and dryer pass it on. Turbine and reheater refuse it, it has to go through the **steam purifier**.
compendium.fluids.coolant.text: Cold **coolant** comes from the **cooling tower** and cools the **condenser** and the **relief tank**. Liquid sodium and cryo coolant go into the same ports and cool twice or four times as much.
compendium.fluids.exhaust_steam.text: Exhaust steam comes out of the **turbine**. Its port is called the condensate port but puts out exhaust steam. The **condenser** turns it into water, the **feedwater heater** uses it to preheat feedwater. If nobody takes it, the turbine's tank fills up and the rest is lost.
compendium.fluids.feedwater.text: The **water treatment** turns water into feedwater. It goes into the **steam generator**, optionally through the feedwater pump and the feedwater heater. With a containment it enters **feedwater in** outside and comes out inside. Emergency cooling and hydraulic water take feedwater as well.
compendium.fluids.hot_coolant.text: **Hot coolant** comes out of the condenser and the relief tank and goes back into the **cooling tower**. There it gets cold again, a part evaporates.
compendium.fluids.hot_primary_water.text: In the **fuel rod drive** the rods heat the primary water, it goes straight into the **steam generator**. Above **90 %** pressure the **pressurizer** blows hot primary water into the **relief tank**.
compendium.fluids.preheated_feedwater.te: The **feedwater heater** preheats feedwater with the exhaust steam of the turbine. The steam generator makes **15 % more** wet steam from it. Without exhaust steam the heater passes plain feedwater through.
compendium.fluids.primary_water.text: Cold **primary water** circulates in the primary loop and has no bucket. The **emergency cooling** makes it from water and fills the loop. From the steam generator it goes through the **main coolant pump** back into the fuel rod drive. The **pressurizer** hangs on it with its surge line, the **ion exchanger** in a side stream. The **relief tank** hands cooled primary water to the **high-pressure injection**.
compendium.fluids.steam.text: Clean steam from separator, dryer or steam purifier. It drives the **turbine** or goes through the **reheater** first. The purifier passes clean steam without power. The turbine takes steam or superheated steam, never both mixed.
compendium.fluids.superheated_steam.text: The **reheater** turns steam into superheated steam and puts out condensate. The turbine makes more power per mB from superheated steam.
compendium.fluids.water.text: Plain water. The **intake pump** takes it from the lake: the large pipe goes into the water treatment, the small pipes into the emergency cooling and the hydraulic water of the fuel rod drive. **Condensate** is water too: condenser, feedwater heater, separator, dryer and reheater put it out, it goes back into the water treatment through the small ports.
compendium.fluids.wet_steam.text: The **steam generator** turns feedwater into wet steam. It goes into the **steam separator** or the **steam dryer**. Both only take wet steam, so do not chain them. With a containment it enters **wet steam in** inside and comes out outside.
compendium.fusion_deuterium.text:
The **deuterium separator** pulls the heavy hydrogen isotope out of water for the fusion reactor.
## Deuterium Separator (3×3×3)
**Water in** (64 mB/t), **deuterium out** (2 mB/t, enough for one reactor), every 32 mB of water give 1 mB of deuterium
Needs **2,400 FE/t**, stops when the tank is full
The deuterium runs by pipe to the **deuterium in** port of the fusion reactor
Kit in the heavy assembler, controller in the assembler
compendium.fusion_deuterium.title: Deuterium Separator
compendium.fusion_fuel.text:
The fusion reactor needs three gases and lithium. All of them only flow through pipes and tanks, **without buckets**.
## Fuel
**Deuterium** (D) from the **deuterium separator**, 1.6 mB/t at full rate
**Tritium** (T), 1.6 mB/t; it is bred in the blanket from **lithium pellets**: one pellet every 150 ticks gives **260 mB** of tritium
**Helium** (He) is the ash, 1.6 mB/t; when the helium tank is full the reactor vents the surplus
## Start without tritium
Without tritium the reactor burns **deuterium against deuterium** at up to **12 %** burn rate and breeds the first tritium
## Lithium
**Lithium ore** generates in every world , raw lithium smelts to an ingot
The assembler turns 4 lithium ingots and enriched carbon into 8 **lithium pellets**
## Cooling
**160 mB/t** of coolant at full rate (**sodium 80**, **cryo 40**), it leaves hot and belongs to the cooling tower
Without it the **wall heat** rises; after 20 seconds without cooling the plasma collapses (**disruption**), the wall takes damage and radiates briefly
## Wall tile
Lasts **144,000 ticks** (2 hours) at full rate; the machine swaps it from the input, the old one comes out activated and belongs in the **repository**
compendium.fusion_fuel.title: Fuel and Cooling
compendium.fusion_overview.text:
The **fusion reactor** (tokamak) is the end goal after the pressurized water reactor: a torus of magnet coils in which a **plasma** of deuterium and tritium burns.
## Fusion Reactor (21×10×21)
**1,893 cells**, the largest kit of the mod, from the heavy assembler
**Ignite** with **1.8 B FE** from the buffer (up to 262,144 FE/t at the power input), plus fuel and coolant
The plasma burns for **10 seconds** per ignition and returns **75 %** of the ignition power in that time (6,750,000 FE/t), then the reactor ignites again
Without upgrades every shot costs power: the reactor is research first, power plant later
**Burn rate** 25 to 100 % in the terminal or by signal (1 to 15)
Radiates at **40 %** of a fuel rod drive while running; the wall tiles become activated and are **repository waste**
**Upgrades**: on about **5 %** of successful ignitions a **plasma optimizer** drops into the item output. In the item input it is installed: each one makes the ignition cost **5 %** more power and raises the return by **5 points** (at most 6: 105 %, a **5 % gain**)
## Ports
2 power inputs, 2 power outputs, data port
Coolant in and out
Gas: deuterium in, tritium in and out, helium out
Item in (lithium pellets, wall tiles) and out (activated tiles)
Signal in (burn rate) and out (plasma 0 to 15)
compendium.fusion_overview.tip: Kit in the heavy assembler, controller in the assembler. The tokamak is the final stage of power supply.
compendium.fusion_overview.title: Fusion Reactor Overview
compendium.fusion_reactor.text:
Building, igniting and running the **fusion reactor** (21×10×21) step by step.
## Building
Kit on free ground, **right-click** builds the 1,893 cells: plinth, vacuum vessel, magnet coils, central solenoid
Ports at the back of the plinth; the plinth sides carry power, coolant, gas, items and signals
## Igniting
1. Connect **deuterium** and **tritium** (or only deuterium at first) and **coolant**
2. Power to the **power inputs**: the buffer charges, ignition draws up to **262,144 FE/t**
3. Terminal **On**, pick a burn rate: **heating**, then **plasma**
## Running
Terminal: plasma temperature, net power, wall heat, wear; tanks for coolant and gases
Signal in (1 to 15) sets the burn rate, without a signal the terminal setting applies
Signal out: burn rate of the plasma 0 to 15
The power leaves at the **power outputs** (8,388,608 FE/t each), that is what the **superconducting cable** is for
## Terminal
The terminal shows the **ignition sequence**: charging, preheating (from 60 %), confinement (from 85 %), ignition, burning, plus time left, history and log
## Faults
**No fuel**, **no coolant**, **tritium tank full**, **wall tile worn**: the plasma goes out, ignite again
Too long without cooling: **disruption**, 10 second pause, wall damage
compendium.fusion_reactor.title: Fusion Reactor
compendium.gas_generator.text:
The **gas generator** (**5×5×7**) is an inline five-cylinder engine driving a generator. The **flywheel** between engine and generator turns while it works, the exhaust leaves through the stack at the back right. The **ethylene** enters at the intake rail from the right (seen from the front), the **power** leaves on the left.
## Operation
Burns **6 mB/t** ethylene and delivers **10000 FE/t**, that is 1667 FE per mB. The gas generator has no storage: what the consumer does not take at once is lost. The tank also takes **diesel** from the distillation column, which burns just as fast and as rich (one kind in the tank). Without gas it stands still.
## Setup
Kit from the Heavy Assembler.
compendium.gas_generator.tip: One distillation column with a cracker delivers a little over 2 mB/t ethylene, a gas generator needs 3 mB/t. Better lead the power into a battery. The full diesel tank of the column finds a consumer here.
compendium.gas_generator.title: Gas Generator
compendium.guide.alldone: All done: you have finished every step of the guide.
compendium.guide.help: Not sure how to operate things? There is no PLC here, and you do not have to program anything. Every machine has its own terminal (right-click its little screen). You control all of them together over the data network: data cables to the machines, and at the other end a data terminal, a console, a control desk or instruments. The chapter "Control room" walks you through it step by step.
compendium.guide.main: Main path to the first power
compendium.guide.ms.data_terminal_net: The terminal lists at least one machine
compendium.guide.ms.rods: Fuel rod inserted in the control rod drive
compendium.guide.step.acid_plant.text:
The **acid plant** roasts ore into **sulfur** and makes sulfuric acid. You need the sulfur for rubber in the polymer plant and for the acid chains after it.
Make the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up
Raw ore in on top, sulfur dust comes out below
compendium.guide.step.acid_plant.title: Acid plant: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.arm.text: The **robot arm** carries parts from machine to machine without you touching them. The clean room does not run without it. It is built in the Reactor Assembler, hangs on the power, and you set source and target with the link tool.
compendium.guide.step.arm.title: Make the robot arm
compendium.guide.step.battery_small.text: A **battery** buffers power, for example for pump start-up. There are three sizes (4, 16 and 64 million FE). Power in on one side, power out on the other; in the terminal you switch each port individually. The data port sits on the roof.
compendium.guide.step.battery_small.titl: Battery: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.blast_furnace.text: The **blast furnace** (5×4×5) pours **steel** in batches: 8 iron ingots + 8 coal make 8 steel ingots. Make the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up. Material into the scrap bin in the back, ingots from the ladle in front.
compendium.guide.step.blast_furnace.titl: Blast Furnace: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.board.text: **Control board I** (4 circuits, 30 redstone, 4 reactor plates) controls the simple machines. Stage II and III follow later.
compendium.guide.step.board.title: Make control board I
compendium.guide.step.cable.text: The **data cable** (23 black wool, 8 copper ingots, 4 redstone make 8) connects machines to terminals. It attaches to a controller, to a **port** of a large machine or to a single machine. A cable to a port is enough.
compendium.guide.step.cable.title: Make data cable
compendium.guide.step.casing.text: The Small Parts Assembler makes **4 reactor casings** from 4 reactor plates + 2 steel sheets: the shell of every large machine.
compendium.guide.step.casing.title: Make reactor casings
compendium.guide.step.castor.text: The **castor** (2×3×2) transports spent rods and decayed fuel: 36 × 16 slots, the contents do not radiate and stay inside when you take it down. Placed next to an item port it loads rods and picks up decayed ones.
compendium.guide.step.castor.title: Castor container
compendium.guide.step.chemical_lab.text:
In the **chemical lab** you clean **raw silicon** with sulfuric acid into **pure silicon**. You need it for wafers and chips; without chips there are no component, compute or particle assemblers and no special plants such as fusion or the fast breeder.
Make the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up
Connect sulfuric acid, put raw silicon in, pure silicon comes out
compendium.guide.step.chemical_lab.title: Chemical lab: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.chip_1.text: The micro assembler builds **chip I** from wafers. It sits in the controller of the waste repository, for example. Hover the picture to see the exact recipe.
compendium.guide.step.chip_1.title: Make Chip I
compendium.guide.step.chip_2.text: The Soldering Machine builds **chip II**. It needs chip I, pure silicon, rubber, 2 photoresist and 2 gold.
compendium.guide.step.chip_2.title: Make Chip II
compendium.guide.step.chip_3.text: **Chip III** is made in the clean room from chip II, 3 pure silicon, an ender pearl, a diamond, 2 gold and an HDPE sheet. The controllers of the fast breeder, the fusion reactor and the quantum computer need it.
compendium.guide.step.chip_3.title: Make Chip III
compendium.guide.step.circuit.text: The **micro assembler** builds the **basic circuit**. Without it there is no control board, and without a control board no machine kit. If another mod provides a basic control circuit, you use that instead; the control board accepts both.
compendium.guide.step.circuit.title: Make the basic circuit
compendium.guide.step.clean_room.text: The **clean room** (3×3×3) builds **chip III** and the highest CPU and RAM tiers, only with a docked robot arm. Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler (5,760 FE/t), the controller needs a chip II. It needs 1,920 FE/t while building.
compendium.guide.step.clean_room.title: Clean Room: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.cnc_mill.text: The **CNC mill** (2×2×3) mills the **HDPE seal**, **osmium heat plate**, **obsidian composite plate** and **lead shielding**. Make the kit in the Small Parts Assembler and set it up. Power at the back, parts on top, result on the left.
compendium.guide.step.cnc_mill.title: CNC Mill: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.coal_kit.text: The assemblers need power. A **coal generator** (720 FE/t) is enough to begin with. The kit is made at the crafting table: 4 iron ingots, blast furnace, 2 copper ingots, redstone block and iron block.
compendium.guide.step.coal_kit.title: Build the coal generator kit
compendium.guide.step.coal_place.text: Hold the kit: a **hologram** shows the spot, **blue** means free, **red** means something is in the way. **Right-click** sets the machine up. Look at the hologram: the action bar names the block that belongs there. To take it down later you use the wrench, the kit comes back.
compendium.guide.step.coal_place.title: Set up the coal generator
compendium.guide.step.component_assemble: The **component assembler** (5×4×5) builds on order: you order at the storage terminal, it fetches the ingredients from the racks and puts the result back. For this you need **pattern cards** (blank cards from the Small Parts Assembler, written in the menu). Power on the left, 1,440 FE/t per working core.
Component assembler: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.compute.text: The data terminal, the console and the storage terminal need **computing power** from the network: the data terminal 1 CPU and 8 GB RAM, the console and the storage terminal 1 CPU and 16 GB each. Build a **CPU module** and **RAM sticks** (with chip I) in the Small Parts Assembler, for example 1 CPU Module 1 Core and 4 RAM Sticks 2 GB, and put them into the slots of a powered rack. Every module takes one slot, all racks on the same data cable add up. For more devices you need bigger modules or a second rack.
compendium.guide.step.compute.title: Put RAM and CPU into the rack
The **compute assembler** (3×3×3) works like the Reactor Assembler, but the faster the more **free computing power** (CPU and RAM) is left on the data network. Kit from the Heavy Assembler, controller from the Reactor Assembler. Data cable to the data port, on the same network as racks with CPU and RAM modules.
Compute Assembler: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.condenser.text: Turns exhaust steam back into water (640 mB/t). The heat is taken up by **coolant** and leaves at the top as hot coolant to the cooling tower. Without coolant it only condenses air-cooled at 40 mB/t.
compendium.guide.step.condenser.title: Condenser: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.console.text: The **console** is a command line for all machines in the network. Try: **list** (all machines with number), **info 1** (all values), **set 1 enable off** (switch off), **watch 1 heat** (live value). Arrow up brings back earlier commands. Part of a name works instead of the number.
compendium.guide.step.console.title: Command console: type instead of click
compendium.guide.step.containment.text: The **containment** (31×32×31) encloses the whole primary loop. Feedwater, wet steam, power and data pass through feed-through ports in the wall. The control rod drive stands on a pedestal right under the hatch. Strongly recommended in case something goes wrong.
compendium.guide.step.containment.title: Containment: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.control_desk.text: The **control desk** (3×2×2) is the control center: the middle is a command line for the selected machine, the left shows all machines, the right shows alarms. The red **emergency stop** pulls the rods of all control rod drives in the network out (SCRAM). Data cable to the data port at the back right, power at the back left (24 FE/t).
compendium.guide.step.control_desk.title: Control desk: build and set up the kit
The **heart of the reactor** (5×10×5) lowers up to nine fuel rods into its pressure vessel. It needs power (60 FE/t) and **hydraulic water** on the back. Controller in the Reactor Assembler, kit in the Heavy Assembler. Right-click the terminal port at the front to open the reactor terminal.
Control rod drive: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.controls.text: With the **data button**, **data lever** and **data slider** you operate machines right on the wall: the button triggers an action (emergency stop, empty tank), the lever switches on and off, the slider sets values in 16 steps, for example the rod position. **Sneak + right-click** picks machine and value, **right-click** operates.
compendium.guide.step.controls.title: Button, lever and slider
compendium.guide.step.cooling_tower_larg: Cools the hot coolant down again (960 mB/t, 21×40×21, no power). One tower is enough for one and a half condensers. What evaporates you refill with coolant.
Cooling tower: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.core.text: In the fuel pellet factory 2 **uranium oxide dust** (from uranium oxide in the ore mill) and 1 enriched uranium make 3 pellets, and 2 pellets sinter into 1 **uranium core**. One fuel rod casing needs 15 cores to build.
compendium.guide.step.core.title: Make a uranium core
compendium.guide.step.cracker.text: The **cracker** (3×3×3) splits **naphtha** into **ethylene**, a gas (400 mB from 1000 mB). The naphtha enters on the right seen from the front, the gas leaves at the top left: you need a gas port and a gas pipe for it. Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up.
compendium.guide.step.cracker.title: Cracker: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.crafting.text: A storage terminal with a 3×3 crafting grid: recipes are made straight from storage, missing ingredients are fetched from the racks. It needs **2 CPU and 32 GB RAM** in the network (CPU and RAM module in the rack).
compendium.guide.step.crafting.title: Crafting terminal
compendium.guide.step.decon_dock.text: The **dock** (4×2×2) charges the decon robot and refills its cleaning agent (lye from the chemical lab). The rubble runs into the rubble output and radiates: put it straight into a waste barrel or the Waste Crusher. Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up.
compendium.guide.step.decon_dock.title: Decon Dock: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.deuterium_separato: Pulls deuterium (2 mB/t, enough for one reactor) out of water (64 mB/t) and needs 2,400 FE/t. The gas runs through a pipe to the **deuterium in** port of the fusion reactor.
Deuterium separator: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.distillation_colum: The **distillation column** (3×6×3) is the refinery: crude oil becomes **naphtha**, **diesel** and **tar**, plus some **sulfur dust**. All three outputs need a consumer, otherwise the column backs up. Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up. Crude oil comes in on the west side, the products leave on the east side.
Distillation Column: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.dosimeter.text: The **dosimeter** counts your daily dose and beeps at half and at the limit. It also shows in the hotbar; hold Alt and drag to move the display.
compendium.guide.step.dosimeter.title: Dosimeter
compendium.guide.step.drive.text: **Hard drive I** stores 4,096 items in 32 kinds and comes from the Small Parts Assembler. Right-click the front of the rack to open the slots. The contents stay on the drive even if you take it out.
compendium.guide.step.drive.title: Hard drive
Turns water into **primary water**: it fills the loop on the first start and tops it up (320 mB/t). It always runs with power. Primary water has no bucket.
Emergency cooling: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.enriched.text: Put **yellowcake** into the centrifuge: 2 yellowcake make 1 enriched uranium, plus some uranium oxide and depleted uranium.
compendium.guide.step.enriched.title: Enrich uranium
compendium.guide.step.enrichment_centrif: The **centrifuge** (3×4×3) turns yellowcake into **enriched uranium**. Ports like the ore mill: power on the right, items in at the top, result out on the left.
Enrichment centrifuge: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.equipment_assemble: The **equipment assembler** (3×2×2) makes protective suits, the respirator mask, decon devices, pocket batteries and the exoskeleton. Make the kit in the Reactor Assembler and set it up. Power on the right (seen from the front), items on top, result on the left.
Equipment Assembler: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.fast_breeder.text: The **fast breeder** (9×11×9) is a sodium-cooled reactor with its own loop. In its blanket, breeder elements breed plutonium: the bred elements go to reprocessing. It radiates in operation.
compendium.guide.step.fast_breeder.title: Fast breeder: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.feedwater_pump.tex: Pushes the feedwater (up to 960 mB/t) back into the steam generator. **Without feedwater** the steam generator takes no heat away and the core heats up.
compendium.guide.step.feedwater_pump.tit: Feedwater pump: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.first_power.text: The steam reaches the turbine, it spins and delivers **power**. This is the goal of the main path: you run a nuclear power plant. Watch turbine and reactor at the terminal, the instruments or the control desk.
compendium.guide.step.first_power.title: First power from the reactor
compendium.guide.step.fluid_buffer.text: The **fluid buffer** (3×3×3) holds any fluid, for example diesel or tar of the distillation column. Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up, then lay one pipe to the input and one to the output.
compendium.guide.step.fluid_buffer.title: Fluid Buffer: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.foundry.text:
The **foundry** turns sand and coal into **raw silicon** and later **wafers**. They become the chips for the controllers of the precision and special machines.
Make the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up
Put sand and coal in, raw silicon comes out
compendium.guide.step.foundry.title: Foundry: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.fusion_power.text: The plasma burns for 10 seconds and returns 75 % of the ignition power at the power outputs, 105 % with 6 plasma optimizers. Connect superconducting cables and batteries there.
compendium.guide.step.fusion_power.title: Power from fusion
compendium.guide.step.fusion_reactor.tex: The **fusion reactor** (21×10×21, 1,893 cells) is the biggest kit of the mod. Ignition needs 1.8 billion FE from the buffer, plus fuel and coolant. In the terminal switch to **On** and choose a burn rate: first heating, then plasma.
compendium.guide.step.fusion_reactor.tit: Fusion reactor: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.gas_generator.text: The **gas generator** (5×5×7) burns **ethylene** to power: 6 mB/t gives **10000 FE/t**. It has no buffer, so feed the power into a battery.
