Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up. The ethylene arrives from the west at the intake rail, the power leaves on the east side.
compendium.guide.step.gas_generator.titl: Gas Generator: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.gauge.text: A **dial gauge**, a **bar display** or a **digit display** shows one value of a machine, for example the reactor heat. Connect a cable, **right-click** switches to the next value, **sneak + right-click** to the next machine. Without a connection it says NO SIGNAL.
compendium.guide.step.gauge.title: Hang instruments on the wall
compendium.guide.step.geiger.text: The **Geiger counter** measures the radiation where you stand. In your hand a needle points to the strongest source within 64 blocks. In the hotbar it clicks and shows the value above the hotbar.
compendium.guide.step.geiger.title: Geiger counter
compendium.guide.step.hammer_mill.text: The **hammer mill** (3×2×3) crushes ingots to **dust**: iron, copper and gold, 1 ingot → 1 dust, 25 % chance of a second. The ore mill stays for uranium. Build the kit in the Small Parts Assembler and set it up. Power on the right (seen from the front), ingots in at the top, dust out at the bottom left.
compendium.guide.step.hammer_mill.title: Hammer Mill: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.heat.text: Move the rods in slowly and watch the **heat** in the terminal: red from 80 %, at 100 % the core overheats and explodes after 12.5 seconds. Cooling and flow must be right. When in doubt **SCRAM**: all rods move out.
compendium.guide.step.heat.title: The reactor delivers power
compendium.guide.step.heavy_assembler.te: The **Heavy Assembler** (5×3×5) builds the kits of all large machines. Its kit is made in the Reactor Assembler. While building it needs **5760 FE/t** (reactor parts 9,600 FE/t): plan generators and batteries accordingly. From now on: controller in the Reactor Assembler, kit in the Heavy Assembler.
compendium.guide.step.heavy_assembler.ti: Heavy Assembler: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.high_pressure_inje: Feeds up to 320 mB/t of primary water from the relief tank when the pressure falls below 20 %: a safety system against loss of coolant.
High-pressure injection: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.kiln.text: The **kiln** (3×3×3) fires **zirconium dust** into ingots, coal into coke and glass into glass plates and glass seals. It also smelts everything a furnace smelts with power, ores included. Make the kit at the crafting table and set it up. Power in the back, material on top.
compendium.guide.step.kiln.title: Kiln: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.leaching_plant.tex: The **leaching plant** dissolves yellowcake with acid from the acid plant and water: 2 yellowcake make 2 **uranium oxide**. This yields more than the short way straight into the centrifuge.
compendium.guide.step.leaching_plant.tit: Leaching plant: build and set up the kit
It drives the primary loop and pushes cold primary water back into the vessel. **Without flow the core heats up** until it explodes. It needs power.
Main coolant pump: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.mask.text: The **filter mask** (helmet slot) with a filter inserted blocks 60 % of dust and 95 % of steam from leaks. A filter lasts 10 minutes of contaminated air; right-click with the filter in hand inserts it.
compendium.guide.step.mask.title: Filter mask with filter
compendium.guide.step.mast.text: For long distances without cables: **pylons** up to 64 blocks apart (up to 256 between two **large pylons**) and **overhead wire** between them. With the wire click substation, pylon, pylon and so on up to the target substation. Pylons take no power themselves.
compendium.guide.step.mast.title: High-voltage pylon and wire
compendium.guide.step.medicine.text: Helps when you have already taken too much (radiation sickness) but does not protect against new radiation. A high dose is deadly: take warnings seriously and leave the hall in time.
compendium.guide.step.medicine.title: Anti-radiation medicine
compendium.guide.step.micro_assembler.te: The **micro assembler** (2×2×2) builds **chip I** and the first CPU and RAM tiers. It runs without a computer and needs only 360 FE/t. Build the kit in the Small Parts Assembler and set it up.
compendium.guide.step.micro_assembler.ti: Micro Assembler: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.oil_derrick.text: The **oil derrick** (2×4×2) stands on an **oil well** and pumps **40 mB/t** of crude oil into its tank at 450 FE/t. Find the well first, otherwise it stands idle. Build the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up. Seen from the front: power on the right, crude oil on the left.
compendium.guide.step.oil_derrick.title: Oil Derrick: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.ore_mill.text: The **ore mill** (3×3×4) grinds uranium ore into **yellowcake**. Seen from the front: power in on the right, ore in at the top (a hopper works), result out on the left.
compendium.guide.step.ore_mill.title: Ore mill: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.particle_assembler: The **particle assembler** (5×3×3) lets two spheres collide and makes a **random item** from it: mostly cobblestone and gravel, rarely zircon, uranium or osmium. Controller from the Reactor Assembler (needs chip II), kit from the Heavy Assembler. A hopper at the output collects the results.
Particle Assembler: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.pattern_rack.text: The **pattern rack** (4×5×3) stores 40 written pattern cards. All component assemblers on the same data network build from these recipes. Build the kit in the Reactor Assembler and set it up, power at the back, data cable to the data port.
compendium.guide.step.pattern_rack.title: Pattern Rack: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.pellet.text: From lithium ingots (lithium ore exists in every world) the fuel pellet factory makes **lithium pellets**. In the reactor's blanket they breed tritium: one pellet every 150 ticks gives 260 mB.
compendium.guide.step.pellet.title: Make lithium pellets
compendium.guide.step.pellet_factory.tex: The **fuel pellet factory** presses oxide dust and enriched uranium into pellets and sinters them into **uranium cores**. Later it also makes the lithium pellets for the fusion reactor. Make the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up.
compendium.guide.step.pellet_factory.tit: Fuel Pellet Factory: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.pipes.text: Water, primary water and steam run through **pipes**. The basic pipe carries 1,000 mB/t, the reinforced 4,000 mB/t, the hardened 16,000 mB/t. The throughput of a line follows its weakest piece. Pipes connect to ports by themselves; with the wrench you set a side to suck or to disconnect.
compendium.guide.step.pipes.title: Make and lay pipes
compendium.guide.step.plate.text: In the Small Parts Assembler, 15 iron sheets (iron ingots without Create) make **2 reactor plates**.
compendium.guide.step.plate.title: Make reactor plates
compendium.guide.step.plate_mill.text: The **plate mill** (3×2×3) rolls ingots into plates and makes the **zircaloy sheet**. Make the kit in the Small Parts Assembler and set it up. Power on the right (seen from the front), ingots on top, result at the lower left.
compendium.guide.step.plate_mill.title: Plate Mill: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.polymer_plant.text:
The **polymer plant** (3×3×3) vulcanizes **rubber** from slime or kelp, sulfur and water and presses **rubber seals** from it. With **tar** from the distillation column (port on the east side) there is more rubber from sulfur and a **sealing compound**: rubber seals from rubber and tar, no glass seal needed. You need the seal for the respirator mask and the tier II hazmat suit.
Make the kit in the Heavy Assembler and set it up
Connect water, put sulfur in the extra slot, feed the raw material in on top
compendium.guide.step.polymer_plant.titl: Polymer plant: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.ports.text: Every large machine needs **power ports** and, depending on its job, item, water or steam ports. Make the power and the item port; you find the other kinds in the item list of the compendium. Empty hand on a port: its name and purpose. The power and item port come from the Small Parts Assembler. The plate mill and the hammer mill also need the **terminal port**, the plate mill 1 **brass bearing** (without Create made from gold ingots and andesite housings) and the hammer mill 4 **copper coils**; the Small Parts Assembler builds all of them.
compendium.guide.step.ports.title: Make ports
compendium.guide.step.power_cable.text: A full turbine delivers up to 3,200 FE/t. The basic cable only carries 4,096 FE/t, the reinforced 32,768, the hardened 524,288. For several turbines on one line use the reinforced one.
compendium.guide.step.power_cable.title: Stronger power cable
compendium.guide.step.power_small.text: Lay a **power cable** from the coal generator (power out, left) to the Small Parts Assembler (power in, right, seen from the front). Then right-click the generator's monitor and put in coal. The generator only burns while something draws power: as soon as the assembler charges, it glows.
compendium.guide.step.power_small.title: Connect power and assembler
compendium.guide.step.pressurizer.text: Keeps the pressure in the primary loop at 155 bar (50 %) and vents into the relief tank on overpressure. It needs power for heating (1,200 FE/t) and reports the pressure to the control rod drive.
compendium.guide.step.pressurizer.title: Pressurizer: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.reactor_kit.text: The Small Parts Assembler builds the kit: put **6 iron ingots, 4 redstone, 4 copper ingots, a crafting table and a blast furnace** into the 3×3 grid of its terminal (the layout does not matter). Once the recipe is right and there is power, it starts building. It only needs 480 FE/t for this. The result comes out on the right, a hopper picks it up.
compendium.guide.step.reactor_kit.title: Make the Reactor Assembler kit
compendium.guide.step.reactor_place.text: The **Reactor Assembler** (3×3×3) makes plates, seals, boards and the first kits. While building it needs **1,350 FE/t**, that is 2 coal generators, reactor parts even 3,840 FE/t (6 coal generators). So set up several generators right away, a battery buffers the peaks. Power comes in on the right.
compendium.guide.step.relief_tank.text: Catches what the pressurizer vents, cools it with coolant into primary water and is the supply for the high-pressure injection.
compendium.guide.step.relief_tank.title: Relief tank: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.reprocessing_plant: The **reprocessing plant** (5×4×5) turns enriched uranium into the **uranium cores** for fuel rods. Later it also takes back spent rods and residue. Power in on the right, items in at the top, results out on the left.
Reprocessing plant: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.rod_head.text: The **docker** sits on top of the casing and locks into the control rod drive. In the Reactor Assembler: 4 andesite housings, 30 iron sheets (iron ingots without Create) and 61 redstone.
compendium.guide.step.rod_head.title: Make a fuel rod docker
compendium.guide.step.rod_hull.text: In the Reactor Assembler **16 reactor plates + 15 uranium cores + 8 zircaloy sheets** make the casing of a fuel rod. Alternatively, without reprocessing, 9 single fuel rods made from uranium oxide dust and iron work.
compendium.guide.step.rod_hull.title: Make a fuel rod casing
compendium.guide.step.rods.text: Put the fuel rod (casing + docker) on top of the clamp frame of a shaft. In the reactor terminal press **Lock Rod** for that shaft, then choose the setpoint 0 to 15: only locked rods move in. Wear your protective gear.
compendium.guide.step.rods.title: Insert a fuel rod
compendium.guide.step.scanner.text: The **Network Scanner** (Small Parts Assembler: 2 steel sheets, 4 glass panes, control board I, 4 data cables, a compass) draws the data network through the walls. **Right-click** a data cable to pick the network, machines glow in the color of their state. This quickly shows which cable is missing.
compendium.guide.step.scanner.title: Build the network scanner
The small **rack** (1×3×2) has 6 drive slots. Power (red) and data port (teal) at the back. Base use 24 FE/t. Without power the rack is offline: the items stay on the drives but cannot be reached.
Server rack: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.shaft.text: One line is enough: the **shaft coupling** goes one block behind the exhaust ring, exactly on the rotor axis. Behind it stands the **shaft generator** (3×5×4, up to 160,000 FE/t). Its power comes out at the back.
compendium.guide.step.shaft.title: Shaft generator on the turbine
compendium.guide.step.shower.text: Hang the **shower** from the ceiling at the exit of the reactor hall and supply it with water. Whoever stands under it loses four fifths of the contamination every second.
compendium.guide.step.shower.title: Decontamination shower
compendium.guide.step.silicon.text: The **foundry** turns 4 sand and 1 coal into 2 **raw silicon**. In the **chemical lab**, 3 raw silicon and sulfuric acid become 2 **pure silicon**. You need both for the wafers.
compendium.guide.step.silicon.title: Make Silicon
compendium.guide.step.small_kit.text: The **Small Parts Assembler** is your first machine, everything else builds on it. The kit is made at the **crafting table**: 4 iron blocks, gold ingot, 2 redstone blocks, crafting table and comparator. Hover the picture on the right to see the recipe.
compendium.guide.step.small_kit.title: Build the Small Parts Assembler kit
compendium.guide.step.small_place.text: Just like the generator: kit in hand, check the hologram, right-click. It needs room for 3×2×3 blocks. Ports seen from the front: **power and items in on the right**, **result out on the left**.
compendium.guide.step.small_place.title: Set up the Small Parts Assembler
compendium.guide.step.solder_machine.tex: The **Soldering Machine** (2×2×3) solders **chip II**, the middle **CPU** and **RAM tiers** and the **hard drives II to NVMe**. Make the kit in the Small Parts Assembler and set it up. Power at the back, parts on top, result on the left.
compendium.guide.step.solder_machine.tit: Soldering Machine: build the kit and set it up
compendium.guide.step.spent_fuel_rack.te: A spent rod must decay under water for about 5 minutes. You **build the pool yourself** (at least 3×3, 11 blocks deep, watertight and full of water), the **spent fuel rack** (3×6×3, 9 shafts) goes in at the bottom. Water must keep flowing in at the water port. Without inflow or water column nothing decays.
compendium.guide.step.spent_fuel_rack.ti: Spent fuel rack: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.steam_dryer.text: Makes the steam dry (40 → 39 + 1). Wet steam in on the right, steam out on the left. After that it is ready for the turbine.
compendium.guide.step.steam_dryer.title: Steam dryer: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.steam_generator.te: With the hot primary water it turns **feedwater into wet steam**; the primary water goes back cold. 7×16×7, one steam generator manages up to 1,280 mB/t of wet steam.
compendium.guide.step.steam_generator.ti: Steam generator: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.steam_separator.te: Separates water from the wet steam (40 → 36 steam + 4 water). Wet steam comes in at the front, steam leaves at the top.
compendium.guide.step.steam_separator.ti: Steam separator: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.steel.text: **Steel sheet** is in almost every machine. One sheet costs 7 steel, in the Small Parts Assembler as well as in the plate mill. The Small Parts Assembler makes the steel itself.
compendium.guide.step.steel.title: Make steel sheets
compendium.guide.step.storage_monitor.te: A wall screen for the storage network: usage of every rack and the total storage. Connect with a data cable or put it right next to the racks.
compendium.guide.step.storage_terminal.t: It shows all racks in the network as **one** storage. Connect it with a data cable to the racks or put it right next to them. Left-click takes a stack, right-click half, Shift-click stores. It needs no power itself.
compendium.guide.step.substation.text: The **substation** (5×5×5) is the start and end of the overhead line. Cables to the two power-in ports at the front. The four power outputs feed cables and machines directly. Up to 262,144 FE/t pass over the line without loss.
compendium.guide.step.substation.title: Substation: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.suit.text: The **protective suit** blocks radiation from outside and lowers contamination from the ground. There are three stages (yellow, orange, white). Stage I is made of leather, wool and a glass pane and is the base for the higher stages. You need helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.
compendium.guide.step.suit.title: Protective suit stage I
compendium.guide.step.terminal.text: Every machine has a **terminal**. Right-click (empty hand) the little screen on the front of the Small Parts Assembler to open it: grid, state, power, off/on. This is how you operate every large machine later. Hover any display for a tooltip.
compendium.guide.step.terminal.title: Open a terminal
compendium.guide.step.terminal_net.text: Lay a data cable from the terminal to a machine, for example to the **data port** (flange with a small screen) of the Reactor Assembler, and open the terminal again. The machine appears as a **folder**: click to unfold it, inside are live **readings** and **controls** (on/off, levels). **Locate** shows a light beam above the machine, **Open terminal** opens the machine's own terminal.
compendium.guide.step.terminal_net.title: See machines in the terminal
compendium.guide.step.terminal_open.text: The **data terminal** shows all machines in the network. It is made in the Small Parts Assembler (6 steel sheets, 4 glass panes, control board I, data cable). Place it and **right-click**.
compendium.guide.step.terminal_open.titl: Build and open a data terminal
compendium.guide.step.turbine.text: The **turbine** (7×7×16) takes steam at the top (up to 400 mB/t) and delivers power; the exhaust steam goes through the **condensate port** to the condenser. Its kit is made in the Reactor Assembler. You set start/stop and throttle in the terminal.
compendium.guide.step.turbine.title: Steam turbine: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.uf6_converter.text: The **UF6 conversion plant** turns 2 uranium oxide with fluorite or hydrofluoric acid into one **UF6 cylinder**. In the centrifuge one cylinder makes 2 enriched uranium.
compendium.guide.step.uf6_converter.titl: UF6 conversion: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.wafer.text: In the **foundry**, 2 pure silicon make 4 **wafers**. The chips are made from wafers.
compendium.guide.step.wafer.title: Cast Wafers
compendium.guide.step.wall.text: The **control wall** shows one tile per machine with name, state and three values. Build **3×2 to 5×3** screens as a full rectangle, all facing the same way, and attach a data cable to any of them. Faults blink red, right-clicking a tile opens the machine's terminal.
compendium.guide.step.wall.title: Control wall
compendium.guide.step.waste_repository.t: Nuclear waste belongs in the **repository** (5×9×5): spent rods, decayed fuel, filter residue and fallout. What goes in does not come back. It needs 600 FE/t, only while there is waste.
Waste repository: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.water_treatment.te: Turns the condenser's water into **feedwater** (1,280 mB/t). Make up losses here with fresh water.
compendium.guide.step.water_treatment.ti: Water treatment: build and set up the kit
compendium.guide.step.wrench.text: The **wrench** (15 iron ingots, 2 copper ingots) takes finished machines down: Shift + right-click any part and the kit drops out. On pipes and cables right-click switches a side, Shift + right-click removes them.
compendium.guide.step.wrench.title: Build the wrench
compendium.guide.step.yellowcake.text: Put **uranium ore** or raw uranium into the ore mill. The result is yellowcake.
compendium.guide.step.yellowcake.title: Grind yellowcake
compendium.guide.step.zirc_dust.text: Zirconium is the cladding material of fuel rods. In the Reactor Assembler **4 diamonds + 15 quartz** or **4 zircon** (zircon ore) make **4 zirconium dust**.
compendium.guide.step.zirc_dust.title: Make zirconium dust
compendium.guide.step.zirc_ingot.text: **8 zirconium dust** make 1 zirconium ingot in the **kiln**.
compendium.guide.step.zirc_ingot.title: Make zirconium ingots
compendium.guide.step.zircaloy.text: In the plate mill, **4 zirconium ingots + 8 tin** make **2 zircaloy sheets**. One fuel rod casing needs 8 of them.
compendium.guide.step.zircaloy.title: Make zircaloy sheets
compendium.guide_assemblers.text: With chips you get the special assemblers: the component assembler for orders at the storage, the particle assembler for random finds, the compute assembler for more speed and the equipment assembler for suits and gadgets.
compendium.guide_assemblers.title: More Assemblers
compendium.guide_chem.text: Sulfur, rubber and oil: the acid plant makes sulfur and sulfuric acid, the polymer plant makes rubber, and crude oil becomes naphtha, diesel, tar and ethylene. You need rubber soon for chips and protective suits, and ethylene can make power in the gas generator. The chemical lab follows in the next chapter.
compendium.guide_chem.title: Oil and Chemistry
compendium.guide_chips.text: Chips are the heart of every later machine. They are made from silicon from the foundry and the chemical lab and come in three tiers: chip I in the micro assembler, chip II in the Soldering Machine, chip III in the clean room.
compendium.guide_chips.title: Silicon and Chips
compendium.guide_control.text: Looking for a PLC? There is none here, and you do not have to program anything. Every machine has its own terminal. You control all of them together over the data network: data cables to the machines, and at the other end a terminal, a console, a control desk or instruments. ComputerCraft is only an option for automation.
compendium.guide_control.title: Control Room: How to Operate Everything
compendium.guide_cycle.text: Spent rods radiate very strongly. Here you let them decay, store them or reuse them.
compendium.guide_cycle.title: Fuel Cycle
compendium.guide_distribute.text: Store power and carry it over long distances.
compendium.guide_distribute.title: Distributing Power
compendium.guide_first.text: The Small Parts Assembler builds the micro assembler, steel, plates, casings and ports. With them you make the plate mill and the hammer mill, then the kit for the Reactor Assembler. Everything can be made from vanilla raw materials and your starting power, but it is a lot of work: the plate mill and the hammer mill each cost several hundred iron ingots plus about 770 steel, the plate mill also gold and andesite, the hammer mill also copper. Stock up on ore first and keep the coal generator running.
compendium.guide_first.title: First Assemblers
compendium.guide_fuel.text: Uranium ore becomes fuel: ore mill, centrifuge, then the long way through leaching and UF6 conversion, and finally the fuel pellet factory presses the uranium cores. Only then can you build the first fuel rod.
compendium.guide_fuel.title: Fuel and Fuel Rod
compendium.guide_fusion.text: The final goal: a fusion reactor (tokamak). It needs deuterium from the separator, tritium from lithium pellets, coolant and a lot of power to ignite.
compendium.guide_fusion.title: Fusion
compendium.guide_loop.text: Behind the turbine, exhaust steam becomes feedwater again. The loop must be closed, otherwise the flow breaks off and the core heats up.
compendium.guide_loop.title: Closing the Cooling Loop
compendium.guide_materials.text: The Reactor Assembler turns raw materials into the ingredients for all large machines. Every line here is an intermediate product you will need in quantity later. Missing ores spawn by themselves if no other mod provides them.
compendium.guide_materials.title: Ingredients and the Heavy Assembler
compendium.guide_overview.text:
Tasks step by step, from the crafting table to the first power from the reactor and on to fusion. A check mark appears by itself as soon as you finish a step.
Items count once they have been in your inventory. Machines count once they stand finished and you were near them (up to 96 blocks), power once they deliver some. Hover an item to see its recipe, the button "Open page" jumps to the detailed page.
compendium.guide_overview.title: Guided Start
compendium.guide_reactor.text: The reactor is a pressurized water reactor with two separate water loops. Here you build the primary loop, which is radioactive. Order: set up, pipe, fill with the emergency cooling, power the pressurizer, only then insert rods.
compendium.guide_reactor.title: Reactor and Primary Loop
compendium.guide_run.text: Now it gets serious. Check first: everything piped and powered, loop filled by the emergency cooling, pump running, pressurizer powered. Test new builds in a copy of your world.
compendium.guide_run.title: Start-up: The First Power
compendium.guide_safety.text: Radiation clings to surfaces and a high dose is deadly. Before you start the reactor you need instruments and protection.
compendium.guide_safety.title: Radiation Protection
compendium.guide_start.text: From the crafting table to the first power. You only need vanilla items and patience: first the Small Parts Assembler, then a coal generator for starting power, then you open your first terminal.
compendium.guide_start.title: Start: Power and First Assemblers
compendium.guide_steam.text: The secondary loop is clean: feedwater becomes wet steam in the steam generator, separator and dryer make it dry, the turbine makes power.
compendium.guide_steam.title: Steam and Turbine
compendium.guide_storage.text: The digital storage needs no controller: every powered server rack on the data cable belongs to the network. On top come hard drives, terminal and monitor. The crafting terminal follows later with the assemblers.
compendium.guide_storage.title: Storage and Servers
compendium.hammer_mill.text:
The **hammer mill** (**3×2×3**) has a rotor with two hammer bars that turns while it works. Ingots go into the hopper on top, the dust leaves the machine at the lower left.
## Recipes
1 ingot → 1 dust, 25 % chance of a second (50 % with one, 100 % with two working overclock modules)
**Iron dust**: 1 iron ingot
**Copper dust**: 1 copper ingot
**Gold dust**: 1 gold ingot
## Setup
Kit from the **Small Parts Assembler**, placed like any machine. Power on the right (seen from the front), ingots on top, dust at the lower left, data cables at the data port.
compendium.hammer_mill.tip: The ore mill stays in charge of ores: the hammer mill only crushes finished ingots.
compendium.hammer_mill.title: Hammer Mill
compendium.intro_assembly.text: Every assembler in the order you build them. Drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom, click to open the page.
compendium.intro_assembly.title: The Road to Assembly
compendium.intro_book.text:
Everything in the mod has a page here. You do not have to memorize anything.
## Finding things
Pick a section on the left, then a chapter and a page. The **search** at the top right (Ctrl+F) finds pages, machines and items, also by short names. The arrow keys turn pages.
Blue underlined names in the text are links: a click opens the page of that machine. The arrow at the top left goes back.
Hover an item to see its recipe. A click on its picture opens the **build path** down to the raw materials.
## Progress
A green frame means built, a gold frame is your next goal, a grey frame means never built.
**Achievements** shows all lines, all machines and all items with your progress. The **Guided Start** leads you step by step to the first power.
## Trees
The trees of the lines and **The Road to Power** can be dragged and zoomed with the mouse wheel. A click on a machine opens its page.
## Controls
There is no PLC here, and you do not have to program anything. Every machine has its own terminal (right-click its little screen). You control all of them together over the data network: data cables to the machines, and at the other end a data terminal, a console, a control desk or instruments.
compendium.intro_book.title: How this book works
compendium.intro_materials.text:
Most raw materials are found as ore in the world, the rest you make in the assemblers. This page shows where a material comes from and what you need it for.
## Ores and Metals
**Lead**: ore, ingot and dust. For radiation protection, lead shielding and lead glass
**Tin**: ore and ingot. Rolled together with zirconium into zircaloy
**Osmium**: ore, ingot and dust. For heat plates and heat resistant parts
**Iron, copper and gold**: from vanilla, as dust and plates from the hammer mill and plate mill
**Steel**: ingot and sheet from the small parts assembler. For turbine blades and sturdy parts
## Zirconium Chain
Zirconium dust: 4 diamonds + 15 quartz or 4 zircon make 4 dust
Zirconium ingot: 8 dust
Zircaloy sheet (plate mill): 4 ingots + 8 tin make 2 sheets. Fuel rod cladding is made of it
## Uranium and Fuel
**Uranium**: ore and raw uranium, via acid and leaching to yellowcake and uranium oxide, then UF6, enrichment and fuel pellets
**Enriched and depleted uranium**: come from the centrifuge, pellets become fuel rods
**MOX and plutonium cores**: made from spent fuel in reprocessing
## Chemistry and Moderators
**Fluorite**: ore. For UF6 and as a moderator
**Borax**: ore. Becomes boric acid, which slows the chain reaction
**Lithium**: ore and ingot. For lithium pellets in the fusion reactor
**Heavy water, deuterium and tritium**: from the heavy water and fusion plants
**Sulfur and sulfuric acid**: for uranium processing
## Oil and Plastics
**Crude oil**: from the oil derrick. The distillation column splits it into **naphtha** and **diesel**, among others
**Ethylene**: made by the cracker from naphtha. The polymer plant turns it into **HDPE**, which becomes sheets and seals
**Gas**: powers the gas generator
## Intermediate Products
Copper coil, glass seal, brass bearing, lead shielding, HDPE seal
Create parts (iron sheet, brass …) are used when Create is installed, otherwise a vanilla substitute
compendium.intro_materials.tip: Create is not needed. NuclearSQ generates its own ores (uranium, lead, tin, osmium, fluorite, zircon, borax, lithium) and steel and the higher circuits come from the small parts assembler, HDPE from the reactor assembler, the basic circuit from the micro assembler.
compendium.intro_materials.title: Materials
compendium.intro_roadmap.text: Every plant in the order you connect them (the assemblers are under "The Road to Assembly"). Drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom, click to open the page.
compendium.intro_roadmap.title: The Road to Power
compendium.intro_welcome.text: From uranium ore to the power grid: plan, build and run your own nuclear power plant.
compendium.intro_welcome.title: Welcome to SQ Nuclear
compendium.item.acid_plant_controller_sq: Rotary kiln, contact tower and Teflon reactor: ore becomes sulfur, sulfur becomes acid.
compendium.item.acid_plant_kit_sqc: Builds the finished acid plant (5×3×4). In hand it shows a hologram, right-click builds.
compendium.item.advanced_reactor_casing_: Reinforced casing for later machine kits. CNC mill: 4 reactor casings, 2 osmium heat plates, 1 lead shielding make 4.
compendium.item.airlock_control_sqc: Couples two doors into an airlock, only one is open.
compendium.item.airlock_door_panel_sqc: Building block for pressure-tight airlock doors.
compendium.item.area_monitor_sqc: Spot radiation sensor for walls, ceilings or floors: measures the radiation at its spot every second, keeps the peak and raises an alarm above the threshold (default 10 µSv/h): red lamp, redstone signal 15. On a data cable it provides dose_rate (Sv/h), dose_rate_usv, peak, threshold and alarm; "set … threshold_usv 50" sets the threshold, "reset_peak" clears the peak. Right-click: readings, sneak + right-click: reset peak.
compendium.item.area_sensor_sqc: Measures radiation within a **radius** (default 8 blocks, adjustable 1-16) instead of only at its spot: every second on a grid and right next to every source in range. Reports the **maximum** and the **average**; the alarm works like the spot sensor (red lamp, redstone signal 15) and follows the maximum. On a data cable: dose_rate_max_usv, dose_rate_avg_usv, hottest_x/y/z, radius; "set … radius 12" sets the radius. Right-click: readings, sneak + right-click: reset peak.
compendium.item.battery_large_controller: Heart of the large battery: 64M FE, 131,072 FE/t per connection.
compendium.item.battery_large_kit_sqc: Places the large battery (3×5×3). From the heavy assembler. The charge stays in the kit when dismantled.
compendium.item.battery_medium_controlle: Heart of the medium battery: 16M FE, 16,000 FE/t per connection.

compendium.item.decon_remote_sqc:
The **remote** controls the decon robot. **Right-click the robot** to bind it, **right-click in the air** to start control: you see through its camera, **arrow keys** (like walking) drive and turn, **Right-click** lowers and raises the arm (it only cleans with the arm down), **Shift** ends. Range **48 blocks**. In strong radiation the picture gets **noise**.
**Zone job**: **Shift + right-click two blocks** to mark a zone (up to **32 x 32**), **Shift + right-click in the air** sends the robot off. It drives through it in lanes with the arm down and then parks **backwards at its start spot**, for example in the decon dock. It turns back early when the tank is full, the cleaning agent is empty or the battery is at 25 %. **Shift + right-click in the air** again calls it back.
compendium.item.decon_robot_sqc: The **decon robot** drives over contaminated ground and sucks **contamination** and **fallout** in front of its scoop (radius 1, every half second). What it takes ends up as **rubble** in its tank (200 points): right-click with an empty hand empties it as **contaminated rubble**, Shift + right-click picks the robot up (empty tank only). **Battery** 50,000 FE, charges next to a power source (battery port, generator). In radiation it takes **damage**; a **lead block** (right-click) gives it a **lead plate** (only a tenth), **steel sheet** repairs it. When broken it stays where it is. The **arm** is up at rest; **right-click** with the remote lowers it, only then the robot cleans. Every cleaning pulse costs **cleaning agent** (lye, 1000 mB tank, 5 mB per pulse), which the **decon dock** refills (it also empties the rubble tank). At the rear **bars** show battery, cleaning agent and rubble.

compendium.kiln.text:
The **kiln** (**3×3×3**) is a chamber furnace with firebrick and heating coils. The door is closed while it works and stands open when idle. Material goes in on top, the result leaves the kiln at the lower side.
## Recipes
**Coke**: 2 coal or charcoal make 1 coke
**Zirconium ingot**: 8 zirconium dust make 1 ingot
**Glass plate**: 2 glass + 1 quartz (second input) make 2 plates
**Glass seal**: 30 glass + 8 clay (second input) make 1 seal
Each firing takes 5 s at 300 FE/t
**Furnace recipes**: everything a normal furnace smelts (ores, raw metals, sand, clay into bricks, food) the kiln smelts 1 to 1 with power instead of fuel, faster than a furnace (7 instead of 10 s) at 300 FE/t. Its own recipes come first. Clay only goes into the second input when glass sits in the first. JEI lists the kiln with the furnace recipes
**Experience**: taking items from the output gives experience like a furnace, 0.5 per item for its own recipes. Items taken out by pipes give none
## Setup
Kit from the **crafting table** (4 iron ingots, 1 glass, 2 bricks, 1 furnace, 1 redstone block), placed like any machine. Power and data cables at the power unit in the back, material on top, result at the lower side.
compendium.kiln.tip: Zirconium ingots are made only here: the Reactor Assembler no longer fires dust.

compendium.loop.assembler.hint: The reactor assembler builds fuel rod parts, boards and the first kits. New fuel rods go from here into the drive.
compendium.loop.assembler.name: Reactor assembler
compendium.loop.condenser.hint: The condenser turns the turbine's exhaust steam back into water. Coolant takes the heat and goes to the cooling tower.
compendium.loop.condenser.name: Condenser
compendium.loop.dryer.hint: The steam separator and the steam dryer pull the water out of the wet steam. The turbine gets dry steam.
compendium.loop.dryer.name: Separator and dryer
compendium.loop.pump.hint: The feedwater pump draws feedwater from the treatment and pushes it into the steam generator (960 mB/t).
compendium.loop.pump.name: Feedwater pump
compendium.loop.pwr_containment.hint: Fuel rod drive, steam generator and main coolant pump stand inside. Feedwater, wet steam, power and the emergency cooling pass through feed-throughs in the wall.
compendium.loop.pwr_containment.name: Containment
compendium.loop.pwr_drive.hint: The rods in the reactor pressure vessel heat the cold primary water. It flows hot to the steam generator. As much as the pumps report cools the core.
compendium.loop.pwr_drive.name: Fuel rod drive
compendium.loop.pwr_emergency.hint: Turns water into primary water (320 mB/t). Use it to fill the loop the first time. Always runs with power.
compendium.loop.pwr_emergency.name: Emergency cooling
compendium.loop.pwr_flow.hydraulic.hint: Hydraulics of the fuel rod drive: every rod step uses %s mB, the tank holds %s mB. Without hydraulic water the rods do not move.
compendium.loop.pwr_hp_injection.hint: Starts on its own below 20 % pressure and pushes up to 320 mB/t of primary water from the relief tank back into the loop.
compendium.loop.pwr_hp_injection.name: High-pressure injection
compendium.loop.pwr_intake.hint: The intake pipes must stand in the water at the bottom. At the back it sends water through the large pipe to the water treatment, a small outlet feeds the emergency cooling.
compendium.loop.pwr_intake.name: Intake pump
compendium.loop.pwr_pressurizer.hint: The pressurizer heats below the set point and vents hot primary water into the relief tank above 90 %. Below 20 % the emergency cooling starts.
compendium.loop.pwr_pressurizer.name: Pressurizer
compendium.loop.pwr_pump.hint: The pump pushes the cold primary water back into the vessel, 2,560 mB/t (high-pressure tier 5,120 mB/t). If it stops, the flow breaks off.
compendium.loop.pwr_pump.name: Main coolant pump
compendium.loop.pwr_relief.hint: Cools the vented primary water with coolant and keeps it as a reserve for the high-pressure injection.
compendium.loop.pwr_relief.name: Relief tank
compendium.loop.pwr_separator.hint: Pulls the water out of the wet steam, the turbine gets steam. The separated water must be able to drain, otherwise it stops.
compendium.loop.pwr_separator.name: Steam separator
compendium.loop.pwr_steam_generator.hint: Hot primary water turns feedwater into wet steam and comes out cold. A tube leak makes the steam contaminated.
compendium.loop.pwr_steam_generator.name: Steam generator
compendium.loop.pwr_steam_generator.shor: passes heat to the secondary loop
compendium.loop.pwr_treatment.hint: The large pipe from the intake pump docks on the left or right. Feedwater leaves at the front bottom for the steam generator.
compendium.loop.pwr_treatment.name: Water treatment
compendium.loop.reactor.hint: The fuel rod drive moves the rods into the reactor pressure vessel. Their heat warms the primary water, which flows to the steam generator and comes back cold.
compendium.loop.reactor.name: Reactor
compendium.loop.reactor.short: fuel rods heat the primary water
compendium.loop.shaft.hint: Instead of the controller, the turbine can deliver its power via shaft coupling and shaft generator.
compendium.loop.shaft.name: Shaft generator
compendium.loop.steam_generator.hint: The steam generator takes the heat of the hot primary water and turns feedwater into wet steam (up to 1,280 mB/t). It separates the radioactive primary loop from the clean secondary loop.
compendium.loop.steam_generator.name: Steam generator
compendium.loop.substation.hint: The substation feeds the power into the overhead line. At the destination a second substation hands it straight to cables, as FE, RF or Power Grid. SU does not travel over the line; the Create shaft output sits right at the turbine for that.
compendium.loop.substation.name: Substation
compendium.loop.tower.hint: The cooling tower cools the hot coolant from the condenser back down, no power needed. A little evaporates.
compendium.loop.tower.name: Cooling tower
compendium.loop.treatment.hint: Water treatment turns the condenser's water into feedwater (1,280 mB/t).
compendium.loop.treatment.name: Water Treatment
compendium.loop.turbine.hint: The turbine turns steam into power. What remains is exhaust steam for the condenser.
compendium.loop.turbine.name: Turbine
compendium.mach_blueprint.text:
Big machines come out of the assembler as a **finished kit**. Pumps, vent grilles, casings, pressure chambers, cooling tower segments and ports are the **components** for the kits.
## Crafting
**Small parts assembler**: the reactor assembler kit, micro assembler, plate mill, hammer mill as well as steel, plates, casings and ports
**Reactor assembler**: turbine, heavy assembler, equipment assembler, pattern rack and computing cluster
**Equipment assembler**: Exo Station, decon dock and the robo pets
**Heavy assembler** (5×5 grid): every other machine including control desk and server racks, the controller goes in the middle
**Crafting table**: only the small parts assembler and coal generator, so you can start without power
## What goes into a kit
The machine's **controller** and **reactor casing** for the frame
Exactly the **ports** the finished machine has (power, steam, water, items …)
A **control board** and the parts the machine is made of (pumps, pressure chambers, coils, lead …)
Hover a golden kit to see every ingredient and the **5×5 pattern** for the heavy assembler
## Placing
1. Hold the kit: a hologram follows your crosshair
2. The machine stands **on** the block you aim at and grows in your view direction
3. **Blue** = space free, **red** = something is in the way (water counts as free)
4. **Right-click** places the finished machine and uses up the kit
## Removing
Break **any part** of a finished machine (by hand or shift + wrench) and the whole machine disappears, the **kit drops**
Tank contents are lost
## Sizes (width × height × depth)
**Turbine** 7×7×16
**Cooling tower** 21×40×21 · **Cooling tower XL** 63×120×63 · **Containment** 31×32×31 · **Relief tank** 9×3×9 · **Pressurizer** 3×8×3 · **High-pressure injection** 3×2×4
**Fuel rod drive** 5×10×5 · **Steam generator** 7×16×7
**Heavy assembler** 5×3×5 · **Reprocessing plant** 5×4×5 · **Emergency cooling** 5×3×4 · **Spent fuel rack** 3×6×3 (in your own pool)
**Small parts assembler** 3×2×3 and **coal generator** 3×3×3, both kits from the crafting table · **Reactor assembler** 3×3×3 · **Solar field** 5×2×5
**High-pressure main coolant pump** 3×4×5 · **Main coolant pump** 3×3×3 · **Steam separator** 3×6×3 · **Steam dryer** 5×3×3
**Shaft generator** 3×5×4, behind the turbine shaft coupling

compendium.mach_heavy.keywords: heavy assembler, large assembler, big assembler
compendium.mach_heavy.text:
## Heavy assembler (5×3×5)
Assembly hall with a gantry crane and a **5×5 grid** for large recipes: the machine kits of the large machines (controller in the middle), plus the large castor and the Create shaft output. Controllers, fuel rod cladding, dockers and pressure chambers come from the reactor assembler
Power on the right (seen from the front)
Items **in on top** (yellow port at the feed hopper on the crane rail): refills grid cells that already hold the same item
**Result out** on the left at the bottom (copper orange port)
**5760 FE/t** (as much as 8 coal generators), reactor parts **9,600 FE/t**, power buffer **1,200,000 FE**
The terminal shows state, power, demand and progress, plus operation off/on
compendium.mach_heavy.tip: Automation: a hopper on top of the yellow input refills it, a hopper under the copper orange output collects the result. Pipes and Create funnels work the same way.
compendium.mach_heavy.title: Heavy assembler
compendium.mach_menus.text:
Every device opens a terminal in the same style on right-click (empty hand), CRT or modern (page Terminals).
**Fuel rod drive**: reactor core (heat, cooling, power), slider, SCRAM, one card per shaft with Lock Rod, vessel
**Reactor assembler**: state, progress, power, off/on
**Turbine**: start/stop and throttle
**Large machines and batteries**: state, power, structure, fill level or switch per port, operation off/on
**Recipes button** at the right of the window: shows the machine's recipes in JEI, without JEI the compendium search
Hover any element to see a tooltip
compendium.mach_menus.tip: Buckets still work: right-click with a bucket fills or empties pump and turbine.
compendium.mach_menus.title: Device Menus
compendium.mach_terminals.text:
All large machines, the turbine, the fuel rod drive, the reactor assembler, the pumps and machines have a terminal.
## Opening
Right-click (empty hand) the **monitor** in the model: the whole screen area works, no matter which block is behind it
Right-clicking the controller works too
## Style
Top right above the window: **CRT | MODERN**
**CRT**: green tube monitor with scanlines and a monospace font
**MODERN**: dark cards, colored bars, normal font
The choice applies to **all terminals** and is saved (config/nuclearsq-client.toml, option terminalStyle)
## Tooltips
Hover any display, bar, button or port: what it is, the value with its unit, what the button does and what is missing (e.g. hydraulic water)
For large machines the tooltip of a port row names direction, type, rate, tank and contents
Note: the cooling tower has no monitor. Right-click its controller to see the state in chat.
compendium.mach_terminals.tip: You can switch the style at any time, even while running.
compendium.mach_terminals.title: Terminals
compendium.mach_tests.text:
Two blocks only in the creative tab, without a recipe, for trying out machines without a whole loop:
**Creative power source**: gives unlimited power to all 6 neighbors every tick
**Creative fluid source**: delivers water to all neighbors. Right-click with a filled bucket switches to its fluid, with an empty hand it shows what it delivers
Place it directly at a power or water port, e.g. at the water port of an emergency cooling (primary water has no bucket)
Note: meant for testing only, not for survival worlds.
compendium.mach_tests.tip: The position of every port is listed under Reactor > Heat & Coolant on the page "Sizes and ports".
compendium.mach_tests.title: Test blocks (creative)
compendium.micro_assembler.text:
The **micro assembler** is a small precision workbench (**2×2×2**) with a soldering arm. It makes the **basic circuit**, **chip I** and the first RAM and CPU tiers. It runs **without a computer**.
## What it makes
**Basic circuit**
**Chip I**
**CPU modules** with 1 and 2 cores
**RAM modules** with 1 GB and 2 GB
Everything else from the small parts assembler is not made here
## Setting up
1. Make the **kit** in the **small parts assembler**: 4 iron ingots, 4 copper ingots, 4 redstone, 1 comparator and 2 gold (480 FE/t)
2. Place it like any kit (hologram, right click)
## Operation
**360 FE/t** while crafting, one part takes **5 seconds** (a recipe may have its own values), energy storage **120,000 FE**
**Power** on the right (west, seen from the front), **items in** on top, **result out** on the left (east)
Right click on the controller opens the terminal with the **3×3 grid**; the position in the grid does not matter, only the amounts
Data cable to the data port if you want to see the machine in the network. There is no speed bonus from computing power
compendium.micro_assembler.tip: The micro assembler is small enough to stand right next to the foundry: wafers in, chip I out.
compendium.micro_assembler.title: Micro Assembler
compendium.module_fan.text:
A **half block** with a fan wheel.
## Effect
Cools **one overclock module** on the same machine
On its own it does nothing
One fan per overclock module, more do not help
## Crafting
Small parts assembler: 4 iron ingots, 1 copper coil, 2 redstone, 2 iron bars
compendium.module_fan.tip: The fan may sit on a different side than the overclock module.
compendium.module_fan.title: Fan Module
compendium.module_overclock.text:
A block with a circuit board and cooling fins.
## Effect
Per module **+25 %** speed and **+40 %** power
At most **2** per machine
Each one needs a **fan module** on the same machine, otherwise it overheats (yellow lamp) and does nothing
## Crafting
Small parts assembler: 1 control board II, 2 copper coils, 4 gold ingots, 2 steel sheets, 4 quartz
compendium.module_overclock.tip: Add an energy saver cabinet and the power stays almost the same.
compendium.module_overclock.title: Overclock Module
compendium.module_overview.text:
**Modules** are small machines of their own that you place right against a machine. Each has its own size.
## Setup
The module has to **touch** the machine (any block, the top works too)
It works on every machine with recipes: small parts, reactor, heavy and particle assembler, ore mill, centrifuge, reprocessing
The machine looks for its modules once per second
## Lamp
**Green**: active
**Yellow**: placed on a machine but not active
**Off**: no suitable machine next to it
**Right-click** tells you which machine it is on and why it is not active
## Crafting
All modules come from the **small parts assembler**
compendium.module_overview.tip: Two overclock modules with two fans plus two energy saver cabinets: 50 % faster at almost the same power.
compendium.module_overview.title: Machine Modules
compendium.module_saver.text:
A **switch cabinet**, 1 block wide and **2 blocks tall**.
## Effect
Per cabinet **−20 %** power
At most **2** per machine
Together with overclock modules: their +40 % is added first, then the saving applies
## Crafting
Small parts assembler: 1 control board I, 4 steel sheets, 2 copper coils, 4 redstone, 1 comparator
compendium.module_saver.tip: The block above the cabinet has to be free.
compendium.module_saver.title: Energy Saver Cabinet
compendium.oil_derrick.text:
The **oil derrick** (**2×4×2**) stands on an **oil well**: the well's core must lie under one of its four floor cells. The drill string turns while it works, the winch and the crown sheave run with it.
## Operation
Pumps **40 mB/t** crude oil into its tank at **450 FE/t**. When the well is empty it stops and waits until it refills.
## Oil well
A well only exists from world generation, roughly one per 16 chunks, in four sizes: small 2 million mB, medium 6 million, large 12 million, huge 24 million (each ±15 %)
Right-click on the well shows class and fill level
An empty well slowly refills, 1 % of its maximum per Minecraft day
## Setup
Kit from the Heavy Assembler. Seen from the front: power on the right, crude oil on the left, data port at the front left.
compendium.oil_derrick.tip: Find the oil well first. The derrick only makes sense on top of one.
compendium.oil_derrick.title: Oil Derrick
compendium.oil_overview.text:
From the oil well to power: a chain of four machines.
## The path
**Oil derrick**: pumps **crude oil** from an **oil well**
**Distillation column**: splits the crude oil into **naphtha**, **diesel** and **tar**, plus **sulfur dust**
**Cracker**: splits naphtha into **ethylene**
**Gas generator**: burns ethylene or diesel into power
## Who takes what
**Tar**: polymer plant, more rubber and sealing compound, with coal coke
**Diesel**: gas generator, and the decon dock as emergency power, and the chemical lab for grease
**Naphtha**: cracker, and the polymer plant for photoresist (chip II)
**Ethylene**: gas generator, and the polymer plant for HDPE sheet (chip III)
**Sulfur dust**: the same as from roasting ore
## Good to know
1000 mB of crude oil make 900 mB of product, the rest burns off as flare gas
Pipes carry any kind, only gases need a gas port
The **fluid buffer** catches diesel or tar when nobody takes it
compendium.oil_overview.tip: Build the consumers first, then the column, otherwise it backs up after a few seconds.
compendium.oil_overview.title: Oil and Gas Overview
compendium.particle_assembler.text:
The particle assembler is a kind of **miner**: a box (**5×3×3**) with two arms. On the left and right stand containers of **blue** and **red** balls. The arms each take a ball and slowly carry them to the middle, where the grippers tilt towards each other. When they meet, a bright **ender ball** flashes and a **random item** appears.
## Setting up
1. **Controller** from the reactor assembler (2 control boards II, 8 copper coils, 15 ender pearls, chip II)
2. Turn it into the **kit** in the heavy assembler
3. Place it like any kit (hologram, right-click)
## Weight classes
**Light** (55 %): cobblestone, cobbled deepslate, gravel, sand, andesite, diorite, granite, tuff, clay
**Medium** (26 %): coal, raw copper, redstone, flint, quartz, tin, coal and copper ore
**Heavy** (13 %): raw iron, raw gold, lapis, osmium, lead, uranium, zircon, borax, glowstone, obsidian, iron and gold ore
**Rare** (5 %): diamond, emerald, uranium, amethyst, fluorite, diamond and emerald ore
**Exotic** (1 %): ancient debris, ender pearl, netherite scrap, echo shard, prismarine crystals
Tin, osmium, lead, uranium, fluorite, zircon and borax come as NuclearSQ raw materials. That way you get them in worlds that are already explored
## Class cards
Without a card only the **light** class is made, the terminal shows the others as locked
A card in the **card slot** (right of the upgrades) unlocks every class up to its tier
**Medium** (4,800 FE/t): 2 control boards I, 61 iron ingots, 61 redstone
**Heavy** (5760 FE/t): medium card, 2 control boards II, 61 gold ingots, 61 lapis
**Rare** (7,680 FE/t): heavy card, 4 control boards II, 30 diamonds, 30 ender pearls
**Exotic** (11,520 FE/t): rare card, 4 control boards II, 61 eyes of ender, 8 diamond blocks
The higher the card, the more power (values without upgrades, 3,840 FE/t without a card)
All cards come from the reactor assembler, each needs the previous one
## Upgrades
Four slots below the power bar, up to **8** each, made in the reactor assembler
**Speed**: cycles down to a third of the time, costs more power
**Energy**: up to −52 % power
**Efficiency**: heavier classes come up more often
**Output**: chance of a second batch (up to 100 %)
## Power and operation
**3,840 FE/t** (as much as 6 coal generators), one cycle takes **8 seconds**, power buffer **1,200,000 FE**
**Power** on the right, **results out** on the left at the bottom (seen from the front), 9 result slots
Right-click the monitor on the desk: the terminal shows the chance of every class and marks the last one hit
compendium.particle_assembler.tip: A hopper or pipe at the output collects the results. When all 9 slots are full, the machine waits.
compendium.particle_assembler.title: Particle Assembler
compendium.pattern_rack.text:
The **pattern rack** (**4×5×3**) stores **40 written pattern cards**. Every component assembler and the quantum computer on the same data network see the recipes of the cards and build from them, without the cards having to sit in the machine.
## Setting up
1. Make the **kit** in the **Reactor Assembler**: 4 steel sheets, 8 iron bars, a server rack kit, 15 pattern cards, control board II and 4 reactor casings
2. Place it like any kit (hologram, right click)
3. Connect **power** at the back and a **data cable** to the data port
## Cards
Blank cards are made by the **small parts assembler**
The card is written in the **component assembler** (lay the recipe out as a template, insert a card, **Write**)
Put the written card into one of the rack's **40 slots**. Right click on the controller opens them
## Power
The rack needs only **12 FE/t**
Without power **new orders** from these cards are blocked, **running orders** keep going
compendium.pattern_rack.tip: One rack for all recipes instead of eight slots per assembler keeps the network tidy.
compendium.pattern_rack.title: Pattern Rack

compendium.plant_condenser.text:
## Large Condenser (5×4×4)
**640 mB/t** exhaust steam → water, 240 FE/t
Per mB of exhaust steam 1 mB **coolant** becomes **hot coolant** (to the cooling tower). Without coolant only air-cooled at **40 mB/t**
Instead of coolant you can use **sodium** (1 mB per 2 mB exhaust steam) or **cryo coolant** (1 mB per 4 mB). It is used up and comes out as hot coolant, so the cooling tower has less to do
**Exhaust steam in**: top, cell 3 from the left, cell 3 from the front
**Coolant in**: right, cell 2 from the front, level 2
**Hot coolant out**: right, cell 3 from the front, level 2
**Water out**: left, cell 3 from the front, level 1
**Energy in**: right, cell 1 from the front, level 1
## Good to know
Without power or with a full output they stand still and use nothing
Outputs go to all pipes and tanks at the port, not straight into other machine ports
compendium.plant_condenser.title: Large Condenser
compendium.plant_fwpump.text:
## Large Feedwater Pump (3×2×4)
Pulls from pipes and tanks at its inlet and pushes on **960 mB/t**, 480 FE/t. Preheated feedwater stays preheated
**Feedwater in**: right, cell 2 from the front, level 1
**Feedwater out**: left, cell 2 from the front, level 2
**Energy in**: left, cell 4 from the front, level 1
## Good to know
Without power or with a full output they stand still and use nothing
Outputs go to all pipes and tanks at the port, not straight into other machine ports
compendium.plant_fwpump.title: Large Feedwater Pump
compendium.plant_intake.text:
## Intake Pump (9×9×9)
**5120 mB/t** of water from the lake, 1,200 FE/t, enough for the whole plant
A concrete house reaching four blocks over the water; the **two intake pipes** reach four blocks down and must **stand in the water** at the bottom. The water is not used up
Two **large pipe connections** at the back (2×2 fields each), terminal, power and data port on the east wall
## Large pipe
Straight water pipe, 2×2 blocks thick, octagonal, **no corners**. Right-click the connection to place four blocks in the direction of the face, 640 mB/t per quarter. It links the pump to the large pipe connection of the **water treatment**
## Good to know
If an intake pipe is not in the water the pump stands still and the terminal says so
Small pipes do not dock at large pipe connections
compendium.plant_intake.title: Intake Pump
compendium.plant_purifier.text:
## Large Steam Purifier (3×5×3)
In the pressurized water reactor the steam is clean. The purifier sits between dryer and turbine as **protection against a tube leak**
**Clean steam** passes without power and without residue
**1,280 mB/t** contaminated steam → clean steam, 960 FE/t
Every **512,000 mB** one **filter residue** drops into the lead container. At **16** it stops and the terminal shows **RESIDUE FULL**
Radiates while running, stored residue adds to it
**Steam in**: right, cell 2 from the front, level 3
**Steam out**: top, cell 2 from the left, cell 2 from the front
**Residue out**: left, cell 2 from the front, level 1 (hopper or chest next to it, it hands out once a second)
**Energy in**: left, cell 3 from the front, level 2
## Good to know
Without power or with a full output they stand still and use nothing
Outputs go to all pipes and tanks at the port, not straight into other machine ports
compendium.plant_purifier.title: Large Steam Purifier

compendium.plate_mill.text:
The **plate mill** (**3×2×3**) has two counter-rotating rollers that turn while it works. Ingots go into the hopper on top, the plates leave the machine at the lower left.
## Recipes
**Iron plate**: 1 iron ingot
**Copper plate**: 1 copper ingot
**Gold plate**: 1 gold ingot
**Zircaloy sheet**: 4 zirconium ingots + 8 tin (second input) make 2 sheets
**Steel sheet**: 7 steel make 1 sheet (the same in the Small Parts Assembler)
## Setup
Kit from the **Small Parts Assembler**, placed like any machine. Power on the right (seen from the front), ingots on top, plates at the lower left, data cables at the data port.
compendium.plate_mill.tip: The plate mill takes ingots, not ores: grind ore in the ore mill first and smelt it in a furnace. The plate mill kit itself needs steel sheets, so the Small Parts Assembler makes the first steel sheets (7 steel).
compendium.plate_mill.title: Plate Mill

compendium.prot_airlock.text:
An airlock is **two doors** with a **chamber** between them. The **airlock controller** makes sure only one door is ever open. So the reactor hall stays tight even while you pass through.
## Building
1. Build two doors and **build each with sneak + left-click** (or put a **door controller** on each), ideally **airlock doors**, the chamber between them
2. Place the **airlock controller** nearby, at most **12 blocks** from both door controllers
3. It couples by itself the two nearest door controllers that do not belong to an airlock yet. The terminal shows door 1 and door 2
## Operation
• As long as one door is not fully closed, the other stays **locked**, whether by hand, redstone or data cable
• **Cycling**: sneak + right-click, a **redstone pulse** or the buttons in the terminal. The open door closes, the chamber is **purged for 2 seconds**, then the other opens
• The **Close** button closes both doors
• On a **data cable**: a button with the action Cycle airlock, or the value Open door (0, 1, 2) for console and computers
Note: put a decontamination shower and a contamination monitor into the chamber.
compendium.prot_airlock.tip: The airlock controller belongs in the chamber, then you can only reach it from either side through a door.
compendium.prot_airlock.title: Airlock
compendium.prot_basics.text:
Radiation comes from **sources** and drops off quickly with distance.
## Distance
Double the distance = only **a quarter** of the radiation
A few steps away from a source already help a lot
## Shielding
Every block between you and the source holds radiation back
Best: **lead**, then **steel/iron**, **concrete**, **stone**, **soil**, **water**
Glass, wood and leaves barely help
Radiation flows like water through **holes** and around corners: one open block in a lead wall lets a lot through, around the corner behind it a bit less
Under a roof fallout only reaches you at a fifth
## Sources
**Running reactor**: the more power, the more radiation around the pressure vessel
**Spent fuel rods**: radiate very strongly, fresh ones barely
Leaks, turbine, purifier, residue, fallout
## Values
Background: **0.27 µSv/h**
Elevated from **1 µSv/h**, dangerous from **1 mSv/h**
Exposure is sped up: 1 second counts like 40 minutes
## Shielding blocks
**Lead block** (34 lead ingots): strongest shielding
**Radiation concrete** (30 gray concrete + 4 iron ingots + 4 calcite): five times as good as normal concrete
**Lead glass** (30 glass + 4 lead ingots make 8): see-through, shields like steel, for windows
compendium.prot_basics.tip: Build a concrete or lead wall around the reactor before you power it up.
compendium.prot_basics.title: Understanding radiation
compendium.prot_doors.text:
You build doors in any size up to **15×15** blocks: place a **rectangle of panels** and build it with sneak + left-click. It becomes **one door in one piece**, you do not need a control block.
## Building
1. Place panels of **one kind** as a full rectangle in **one plane**. A panel placed on another takes over its orientation
2. **Sneak + left-click** a panel: the plates turn into the finished, closed door. A plain right-click does not build it
3. If a panel is missing in the rectangle, they stay plates and you get a message
## Kinds
• **Roller door**: roller box on top, guide rails left and right, slatted curtain with warning bar. Quickly rolls up and needs no room beside it
• **Sectional door**: bright, wide sections with a window band, runs up on rails
• **Roller grille**: see-through grille with roller box. You can see through it, but closed nobody gets through
• **Folding door**: yellow vertical slats that fold up like bellows to both sides
• **Airlock door**: pressure-tight door with frame, handwheel and porthole. The leaf slides aside in one piece and needs one door width of wall beside it
• **Vault door**: blast-proof door with a thick frame, hinge straps, handwheel and bolts. The handwheel turns, the bolts retract, then the leaf swings open to the front. From **4 cells wide** it has two leaves. It needs one door width of room in front of it
• **Lab door**, **glass door**, **cold room door**, **cage door** and **radiation door**: swing open to the front on their hinges, with two leaves from **2 blocks wide**. Lab, glass and cage doors are thin, cold room and radiation doors are thick. They need room in front to swing open
• **Sliding glass door**: two glass leaves slide into the wall on both sides. It needs half a door width of wall beside it
• **Industrial roller door** with light band, **perforated roller door** and **high-speed door** with red curtain: roll up like the roller door
• **Lift gate**: a heavy steel plate rises in one piece. It needs as much free room above the door as the door is tall
• Built lying flat it becomes a **floor hatch** or silo cover
## Operation
• **Right-click the door** opens and closes it. When it is open, click the roller box on top (roller door) or the frame at the side (airlock door, vault door)
• A **redstone signal** at a panel opens the door, without a signal it closes. Redstone wire connects directly to every panel, no control block needed. A lever or button on the block next to the door works too
• Closed and while moving the door is solid, open you walk through. It will not close while someone stands in it
## Door controller (accessory)
• Placed directly against a panel it takes over the door: right-click opens the **terminal** with state, kind and size, sneak + right-click drives the door
• On a **data cable** the controller is a plant: levers, console and computers set the value door open
• If you remove the controller, the single panels are back for a moment until you build the door again with sneak + left-click
compendium.prot_doors.tip: Put the lever on the wall block next to the door, then you can reach it from both sides.
compendium.prot_doors.title: Roller doors, airlock doors and vault doors
compendium.prot_dosimeter.text:
The **dosimeter** counts how much radiation you have taken today.
## Display
In hand: panel at the top left with **daily dose**, a bar up to the **250 mSv** limit, local dose rate, **body dose** (what you have just received, it slowly fades) and **contamination** (dust on your body, only from contaminated floors, leaks or food)
**Right-click** in hand **pins** the display: it stays open while you hold something else (marked PIN)
Pinning ends with another right-click or when the dosimeter is no longer in your hotbar
Hold **Alt** and drag to move the panel
The daily dose restarts every game day
## Warning
Anywhere in your inventory it beeps at **half** and at the **limit**
Past the limit the display blinks red
## Values
**At body** shows what reaches you **after** the suit and goes into your dose; with a suit, the line below shows how much it blocks and what is **outside** (that is what the Geiger counter measures)
Active remedies are listed below with time left: iodine (uptake −70 %), medicine (dose gain −50 %)
From about **1 Sv** (1,000 mSv) you get radiation sickness
In creative mode the values count, but you do not get sick
compendium.prot_dosimeter.tip: The dosimeter counts your dose. Find contaminated spots with the Geiger counter's needle.
compendium.prot_dosimeter.title: Dosimeter
compendium.prot_geiger.text:
The **Geiger counter** measures the radiation where you stand, from all sources.
## Measuring
**Right-click**: dose rate with a rating (normal, elevated, dangerous)
In hand or in the **hotbar** it shows the value small above the hotbar
It **clicks** like a real counter tube: about every other second at background, denser with more radiation until it crackles
Quieter in the hotbar than in hand
It includes what you carry yourself (fuel, residue, body contamination)
## Compass
In your **hand** the needle points to the **strongest source** within **64 blocks**: contamination, fallout, machines and reactor remains
**Yellow** = weak, **orange** = elevated (from 1 µSv/h), **red** = dangerous (from 1 mSv/h), each as the source would reach you, so without shielding
Above the hotbar you also get an arrow, the distance in blocks and ▲ or ▼ when the source is clearly higher or lower
Standing right on the source, the needle **spins**
With no source in range there is no needle; in the hotbar there is no needle, only the clicking and the value
Contaminated spots are **invisible**: only the Geiger counter finds them. The reading stays shielded, the needle also sees sources behind walls
## Moving the display
Hold **Alt** and drag the box with the left mouse button, right-click resets it
## Anti-radiation medicine
Reactor assembler: 4 glass bottles, 8 dried kelp, 4 gold nuggets
Drinking it lowers the absorbed dose by **3 Sv**
It does **not** protect against new radiation
compendium.prot_geiger.tip: Hold the Geiger counter in your hand and follow the needle: it points to the strongest radiation source.
compendium.prot_geiger.title: Geiger Counter and Medicine
compendium.prot_mask.text:
The **respirator mask** protects against what you **breathe in**: dust from contaminated ground and fallout and steam at leaks. It hardly stops radiation from outside.
## Effect
With a filter inserted: **60 %** less intake from dust on the ground and in fallout
At leaks (steam, aerosols): **95 %** less intake
Works on top of the hazmat suit and iodine tablets, the values multiply
Without a filter or with a used-up filter it does not protect against intake
## Filter
A **respirator filter** lasts **10 minutes** of polluted air
It only runs down when the air is polluted: contamination under your feet, fallout, radiation from 100 µSv/h or a leak. In clean air it keeps
In strong radiation it runs down up to **5 times** as fast, a leak costs 2 s per second
At **60 s** left you get a warning, at 0 a signal tone
Inserting: drag the filter onto the mask in your inventory, or right-click with the filter in hand while wearing the mask. The old filter has to be used up
## Iodine combo filter
Filters like the respirator filter and, as long as it lasts, also cuts the uptake of contamination and its inner radiation by **70 %**, like an iodine tablet
Recipe: reactor assembler from a respirator filter, 4 iodine tablets and enriched carbon
The dosimeter shows the filter time left and the dust protection, in red at 60 s
## Mask and suit
The mask sits in the **helmet slot** and replaces the hazmat suit helmet
Against outside radiation it counts as **half a helmet** (12.5 % of the suit)
Recipe: equipment assembler from 15 leather, 8 glass panes, HDPE seal, 4 rubber seals and steel sheet; filter from enriched carbon, HDPE sheet and steel sheet
compendium.prot_mask.tip: Check the filter before entering contaminated zones: the bar on the mask icon shows how much is left.
compendium.prot_mask.title: Respirator Mask
compendium.prot_robot.text:
The **decon robot** is a remote controlled tracked robot. It drives over contaminated ground and sucks up **contamination** and **fallout** in front of its scoop, so you do not have to walk into the radiation yourself.
## Controlling
1. Place the robot on the ground (right click)
2. Right click the robot with the **robot remote**: bound
3. Right click into the air starts the control. You see through its camera, **arrow keys** drive and turn like walking, **right-click** lowers and raises the arm, **Shift** ends it
Radio range **48 blocks**; in strong radiation the picture gets noisy
## Sucking up
Radius 1, every half second
What is sucked up ends as **rubble** in the tank (**200 points**)
Right click with an empty hand empties the tank as **contaminated rubble**, which radiates itself: take it straight to a waste barrel or the crusher
**Shift + right click** picks the robot up (only with an empty tank)
## Battery and damage
**Battery** 50,000 FE; it charges when you place it next to a power source (battery port, generator)
In radiation it takes **damage**. Right click with a **lead block** gives it a **lead plate** (only a tenth of the damage)
When broken it stays where it is. **Steel sheet** repairs it
## Crafting
Robot and remote are made in the **Equipment Assembler**
compendium.prot_robot.tip: The decontamination shower cleans you, the robot cleans the ground. They belong together.
compendium.prot_robot.title: Decon Robot
compendium.prot_shower.text:
The **shower** washes contamination off your body.
## Setup
Hang it from the ceiling, with up to **3 blocks** of room below
Water: connect a **pipe**, fill with a **water bucket**, or put a **water source directly above**
Tank: 4,000 mB, right-click shows the level
## Use
Stand below: the **mist nozzle** wraps you in spray, every second only a fifth of the contamination remains
Uses **20 mB per second**
It does **not** lower the absorbed dose. That is what the medicine is for
## Contamination monitor
Place it on the wall of the **airlock**, display facing the corridor
Checks everyone up to **2 blocks** in front of it every second: body **and** inventory
From **10 µSv/h**: red lamp, beeping, a hint and **redstone signal 15** (e.g. for a door that stays shut)
Clean: green lamp and a short low tone when you step in
Order: monitor alarms → **shower** → back in front of the monitor
compendium.prot_shower.tip: Put the shower at the exit of your reactor hall.
compendium.prot_shower.title: Decontamination Shower
compendium.prot_sickness.keywords: radiation sickness, radiation poisoning, iodine, iodine tablets
compendium.prot_sickness.text:
The absorbed **dose** makes you sick, and too much is **lethal**.
## Stages
From **0.25 Sv**: first signs, no symptoms yet
From **1 Sv**: nausea, now and then you stop and **throw up**
From **2 Sv**: weakness, slower mining, frequent vomiting
From **3 Sv**: damage that bypasses armor
From **5 Sv**: life-threatening, damage every second
From **8 Sv**: lethal within a short time
## Warning signs
On-screen messages, green to red screen edge, blue heart borders
Vomiting is the sign: get out of the radiation now
## Treatment
The dose slowly wears off (half in about 23 minutes)
**Anti-radiation medicine** lowers the dose by **3 Sv**, then for **2 minutes** it rises only **half as fast** (green shield icon)
Death resets dose and contamination
## Iodine tablets
Reactor assembler: 8 dried kelp, 4 bone meal, 4 paper → 4
Work for **5 minutes**: lower the pickup of contamination (ground, air, food) and its radiation inside the body by **70 %** (orange tablet icon)
They do not help against radiation from outside
compendium.prot_sickness.tip: Always carry a dosimeter and pin its display with right-click.
compendium.prot_sickness.title: Radiation sickness
compendium.prot_suit.keywords: hazmat suit, radiation suit, protective suit
compendium.prot_suit.text:
The **hazmat suit** blocks radiation from outside and protects against contamination on the ground.
## Tiers
**Tier I** (yellow): equipment assembler from leather, yellow and black wool, glass pane. Full suit: **60 %**
**Tier II** (orange): tier I piece + 2 lead shielding + HDPE seal + 4 rubber seals. Full suit: **85 %**
**Tier III** (white): tier II piece + 2 lead shielding + obsidian composite plate. Full suit: **97 %**
## Pieces
Helmet 25 %, chest 35 %, leggings 25 %, boots 15 % of the shielding
Pieces of different tiers can be mixed
The suit wears out in radiation, faster the stronger it is
It does not block radiation you carry (fuel, residue in your inventory)
compendium.prot_suit.tip: After an explosion, only approach the crater in tier III.
compendium.prot_suit.title: Hazmat Suit
compendium.prot_zones.text:
Radiation **sticks**: radioactive dust stays as **contamination** on floors, walls and bodies.
## Where from
Expired fallout leaves part of it behind as residue
**Leaks** at the reactor (red zone) settle in the area around, anyone standing next to them breathes it in
Strong sources (spent fuel rods, a running reactor) slowly contaminate the floor next to them
Whoever is contaminated **spreads** it where they walk
## What it does
It keeps radiating and does **not disappear on its own** on the ground
Walking over it or through fallout picks up **body contamination**
The suit lowers the pickup
## Spotting it
Contaminated spots are **invisible**, no particles and no film
The **Geiger counter** in your hand has a compass needle: it points to the strongest source within 64 blocks (yellow, orange, red by strength)
Debug frames (operators only, /nuclearsq debug radiation): **blue** = contamination (can be sprayed off), **orange** = fixed source, **yellow** = fallout
## Cleaning
**Decontamination sprayer**: right-click the ground to wash **5×5**, one spray cleans the spots completely
Right-click a player or **sneak and click the air**: wash off a body
It does not work on **fuel rods** and running machines, the material itself is radioactive there
It washes fallout blocks away completely
The tank holds **32 sprays**, right-click water to refill
## Items
What you pick up on contaminated ground or hold in hand becomes **contaminated** itself (tooltip shows the value)
Drops from heavily irradiated animals and harvest from contaminated ground are contaminated
Contaminated food contaminates you from inside
Shower and sprayer also wash your inventory
## Spot radiation sensor
Place it on a wall, ceiling or floor, measures the **local dose rate** every second
Right-click: current value, peak and threshold; sneaking: reset the peak
Above the threshold (default **10 µSv/h**): red lamp and **redstone signal 15**
On the network via **data cable**: values **dose_rate_usv**, **peak_usv**, **alarm**, threshold adjustable with **threshold_usv**
Put it on a display in the control room to see a leak before anyone walks into it
## Area radiation sensor
Measures a **radius** (default **8 blocks**, adjustable **1-16** with **radius**) instead of only its own spot
Reports the **maximum** and **average** in range and the **hottest spot** (hottest_x/y/z)
Lamp, redstone, threshold and peak like the spot sensor, the alarm follows the maximum
Good for whole rooms: one sensor on the ceiling covers a hall
compendium.prot_zones.tip: Spray fallout away before it expires. Then no residue remains.
compendium.prot_zones.title: Contaminated Zones
compendium.quantum_computer.text:
The **quantum computer** (**5×4×5**) is a component assembler without limits: it builds for the digital storage what you order at the **storage terminal**, but at **1,024 parts per second**.
## Setup
Kit from the heavy assembler, controller from the reactor assembler (with **quantum modules** from the small parts assembler)
Power on the right (west, seen from the front), **855,000 FE/t** when all lanes work
**Data cable** to the controller or a port, on the same network as racks and terminal
## Computing power
It only runs with **full computing power**: **320 CPU** and **5,120 GB RAM** free in the data network (about 10 computing clusters)
If anything is missing it stands still until there is enough
## Performance
