8 lanes, each run 20 ticks and up to 128 pieces: together 1,024 per second
No tempo modules, the lanes already bring everything
Pattern cards, orders and safety like the component assembler
The racks have to supply the ingredients, otherwise it waits with “Waiting for ingredients”
compendium.quantum_computer.tip: The computing power has to be fully there: if even one core or GB is missing, it stops. Terminals and consoles on the network take their share first.
compendium.quantum_computer.title: Quantum Computer
compendium.reactor_assembler.text:
The reactor assembler is the **second machine** after the small parts assembler: a small production cell (**3×3×3**) with a work table, press and robot arm for every recipe in the **3×3 grid**.
## Setting up
1. Kit from the **small parts assembler**: 6 iron ingots, 4 redstone, 4 copper ingots, crafting table, blast furnace
2. Hold the kit: a **hologram** shows the spot, **blue** = free, **red** = something in the way
3. **Right-click** places it. Dismantle it with the wrench: the kit comes back
## What it builds
Plates, seals, boards, zircaloy and fuel rod parts
The first kits: turbine and heavy assembler
## Power and operation
**1,350 FE/t** while building (as much as 2 coal generators), reactor parts **3,840 FE/t** (6 coal generators), power buffer **600,000 FE**
One part takes **20 seconds** (400 ticks)
**Power** on the right (seen from the front)
**Items in on top** (yellow port on the press beam): a hopper on it fills the grid
**Result out** on the left at the bottom (copper orange): hands it to a chest, hopper or pipe next to it once a second
## Terminal
Right-click the tube monitor on the front desk
**State**: building, recipe incomplete, grid empty, output full, no power or off
**Progress**, **power** and the **Off/On** switch
Hover the progress bar to see what is being made
compendium.reactor_assembler.tip: A coal generator makes 720 FE/t: the reactor assembler needs 2 of them, reactor parts 6. A battery buffers the peaks.
compendium.reactor_assembler.title: Reactor Assembler
compendium.reactor_core.text:
The heart of the reactor is the **fuel rod drive**. The inserted rods heat its **core**, the deeper and fuller, the more. Nine full, fully inserted rods add **0.7 heat per tick**.
## Cooling
**Passive**: 0.2 per tick, always
**Primary water**: every mB flowing through the vessel cools 0.001 (640 mB/t = 0.64)
The **main coolant pump** sets the flow: without it nothing flows
The **pressurizer** holds the **pressure**: below 20 % the drive shows **LOW PRESSURE** and the emergency cooling starts
## Limits
From **80 %** heat: alarm, steam escapes at the sides, the core **radiates**
At **100 %** it is **overheated**: no power until heat drops below **60 %**
If it stays at 100 % for **12.5 seconds**, it **explodes**. Below 90 % the countdown is canceled
**No flow**: if cold primary water runs out or the hot tank is full, the rods heat with no cooling, plus extra heat per missing mB. The core reaches 100 % within seconds
## Attached to the core
**Containment**, **pressurizer**, **emergency cooling**, **high-pressure injection**, **main coolant pumps** and the **detonator** look for the nearest fuel rod drive
The **thermal power** (up to 200) shows on the flux signal at the cabinet and in the control room
compendium.reactor_core.tip: Nine full rods fully inserted: full primary flow (640 mB/t) and passive cooling handle 0.84 of 0.7. If the flow stops, the core heats up at once.
compendium.reactor_core.title: The Reactor Core
compendium.reactor_fluids.keywords: fluids, ports, pipes, primary water, feedwater, wet steam, exhaust steam, condensate, coolant
compendium.reactor_fluids.text: Pick a fluid on the left. On the right, every port that puts it out shows which ports its pipe may lead into. Hover a machine to see all its ports, click to open its page.
compendium.reactor_fluids.tip: The port names are the same as when you right-click the port with an empty hand.
compendium.reactor_fluids.title: Reactor fluids
compendium.reactor_pwr.keywords: PWR, DWR, pressurized water reactor, nuclear power plant, NPP, power plant
compendium.reactor_pwr.text:
Your power plant is a **pressurized water reactor**. It has two separate water loops, so nothing radioactive reaches the turbine.
## Primary loop (radiates)
The **fuel rod drive** moves the rods into the reactor pressure vessel, they heat the **primary water**
Hot primary water flows to the **steam generator**, gives off its heat there and comes back cold
The **main coolant pump** drives the loop. Without flow the core heats up
The **pressurizer** holds the pressure at 155 bar and vents into the **relief tank** on overpressure
Primary water has no bucket. The **emergency cooling** fills the loop the first time and tops it up
## Secondary loop (clean)
Feedwater → **steam generator** → wet steam → separator and dryer → **turbine**
Exhaust steam → condenser → water treatment → feedwater pump → back to the steam generator
## Safety
If the pressure drops below **20 %**, the **emergency cooling** and the **high-pressure injection** start on their own
If a **heating tube** in the steam generator breaks, the steam becomes contaminated. A **steam purifier** in front of the turbine protects against that
The **containment** encloses the whole primary loop
## Build order
1. Set up and pipe the fuel rod drive, steam generator, main coolant pump and pressurizer
2. Fill the loop with the emergency cooling, power the pressurizer
3. Connect the secondary loop and the turbine, only then insert the rods
compendium.reactor_pwr.tip: The next three pages show the primary loop, the extended primary loop and the whole plant as pictures. Click a machine to open its page.
compendium.reactor_pwr.title: The Pressurized Water Reactor
compendium.reactor_pwr_extended.keywords: pressurizer, relief tank, high-pressure injection, cooling tower, safety, extended loop
compendium.reactor_pwr_extended.text: The primary loop with pressurizer, relief tank, high-pressure injection and cooling tower. Hover a machine for a hint, click to open its page.
compendium.reactor_pwr_extended.title: Extended Primary Loop
compendium.reactor_pwr_full.keywords: whole plant, power plant, condenser, cooling tower, feedwater pump, closed loop
compendium.reactor_pwr_full.text: The whole plant with turbine, condenser, cooling tower XL and feedwater pump. Hover a machine for a hint, click to open its page.
compendium.reactor_pwr_full.title: Full Loop
compendium.reactor_pwr_loop.keywords: primary loop, primary circuit, primary water, PWR, DWR
compendium.reactor_pwr_loop.text: The primary loop of the pressurized water reactor. Hover a machine for a hint, click to open its page.
compendium.reactor_pwr_loop.title: Primary Loop
compendium.reactor_terminal.text:
Right-click the terminal port of the fuel rod drive to open the terminal.
## Reactor core
**HEAT** in percent, red from 80 %, below it Normal, Red zone, OVERHEATED or the countdown
**COOLING** per tick: passive, primary water and pumps together
**POWER**: thermal power out of 200, 0 while overheated
## Controls (whole group)
**Slider** for the target 0-15, plus All out, −, +, All in
**SCRAM**: target 0 for the whole group, all rods move out
Source **terminal** or **redstone** (signal at the control port)
**Channel**: drives on the same channel move together
## Shafts
One card per shaft with position, **Lock Rod** and **Release**
## Vessel
Cold and hot primary water, flow in mB/t and temperature, red warning without flow
compendium.reactor_terminal.tip: ComputerCraft can do the same: the sqc_reactor peripheral on the controller, the terminal port or the signal port.
compendium.reactor_terminal.title: The Reactor Terminal
compendium.reactor_water.text:
## Boron and deposits
**Boron** (in ppm) absorbs neutrons: every 100 ppm lowers the power by 5%, 1,000 ppm by half. That works without moving rods and lowers the heat too
Boron enters the water as **boric acid** by right-clicking the control rod drive controller (100 ppm per piece, 1,000 at most)
**Deposits** (in percent) grow with power, at full load to 100% in about an hour. They worsen the heat transfer: at 100% flow, pumps and cooler cool 15% worse
The **ion exchanger** takes 35% deposits and 200 ppm boron out per run and needs 1 ion resin and 1,000 mB of primary water for it
During xenon poisoning less boron helps: take the boron out first so the power does not suffer twice
Both values show in the data network at the control rod drive (boron, deposits)
compendium.reactor_water.tip: Half a stack of boric acid in the reactor room is a cheap emergency brake when the cooling fails. Spent resin belongs in the repository.
compendium.reactor_water.title: Water chemistry in the primary loop
compendium.reactor_xenon.text:
**Xenon-135** builds up while burning and eats neutrons. Its level in percent shows in the fuel rod drive terminal (XENON) and on the data network (xenon poisoning).
## Effect
Up to **30 %** you notice nothing
Above that the power drops, by **40 %** at 100 %
From **80 %** the drive warns, at **100 %** the reactor stops until the xenon has fallen below **60 %**
By itself xenon decays only slowly; MOX rods poison 50 % faster
Less boron helps: take the boron out first, otherwise the power suffers twice
## Xenon filter
A block with an activated carbon delay line and a heater. Reactor assembler: 6 steel sheets, 4 osmium heat plates, 4 glass seals, copper coil, control board I
Stands anywhere within **24 blocks** of the reactor core and needs **600 FE/t**
Insert **carbon filters** (right-click or hopper): up to **4** slots, each lasts **20 minutes** of operation, they are used one after another
Two filters remove xenon twice as fast
Right-click with an empty hand shows filters, time left and power; the data network shows at the fuel rod drive whether a filter is working
## Carbon filter
Reactor assembler: 8 enriched carbon, 2 steel sheets, 1 glass seal
compendium.reactor_xenon.tip: Build the xenon filter before you insert MOX rods: they poison the core 50 % faster.
compendium.reactor_xenon.title: Xenon Filter
compendium.recipe_tree.title: How to build it: %s
compendium.reprocessing_plant.text:
## Reprocessing plant (5×4×5)
Reprocessing in one multiblock: filter residue and cooled spent fuel
**1 input, 4 results**, the residue in the input radiates
Power on the right (seen from the front), residue **in on top** (yellow port at the feed chute), **results out** on the left at the bottom (copper orange)
In the model: hot cell with viewing window and manipulators, feed belt, dissolver with agitator, two **pulse columns** with pulsator and the centrifuge. While running the manipulators swing, a crate rides over the belt, agitator, piston and drum run
Right-click the tube monitor in the cabinet to open the terminal (CRT or modern, with tooltips)
## Results
1 cooled spent fuel → 6 uranium oxide dust (the leftover uranium) + 2 ash, 30 % enriched uranium, 40 % **plutonium oxide** (4 oxide make a plutonium core, fits the fast breeder)
1 enriched uranium → **1 uranium core**
4 ash → 2 lead dust, 50 % zirconium dust, 50 % neptunium oxide
1 bred element → 1 plutonium oxide + 2 depleted uranium + 1 ash
4 plutonium oxide → **1 plutonium core**
8 filter residue → 4 ash and a 50 % chance of **1 uranium core**
1 bred neptunium element → 1 plutonium-238 oxide + 1 ash, with a 25 % chance of 1 neptunium oxide
Plutonium cores come **only from here**, uranium cores also from the pellet factory
compendium.reprocessing_plant.tip: Automation: a hopper on top of the yellow input refills it, a hopper under the copper orange output collects the result. Pipes and Create funnels work the same way.
compendium.reprocessing_plant.title: Reprocessing plant
compendium.robo_pets.text:
Two small **companions** in an industrial look: metal plates, yellow warning stripes and a glowing eye. They follow you, do not fight and are **immune to radiation**. They walk, trot and gallop like real animals; after standing still for 10 seconds they scratch, groom, stretch, yawn or pant.
## Controls
**Right-click** with an empty hand: **pet** it (eyes close, the dog wags, the cat purrs and rubs its head)
**Shift + right-click** with an empty hand: **sit/stay** or **follow** again
**Shift + right-click with the wrench**: back into the **kit**, the charge is kept
## Robo Dog
The **sniffer** searches like the Geiger counter for the strongest source within 64 blocks; at **dangerous** radiation it warns you with **direction** and **distance**
**Toy ball**: throw it, the dog runs after it and brings it back
## Robo Cat
It collects **items** within **5 blocks** and brings them to you
**Feather wand**: wave it, the cat stalks and pounces at the feather
## Collar modules
One module per pet, **right-click** the pet with the module to put it on (an old one drops out)
**Sniffer** (dog): runs to the strongest source and barks there
**Tidy** (cat): brings finds to a chest you clicked with the module before
**Lamp** (both): the pet glows
## Battery
**200,000 FE**; only walking uses power
When the battery is empty the animal **lies down**; it never dies or disappears
Charging: right-click with a **battery item**, or put it next to a **power source** or the **Exo Station**
## Crafting
Kits and toys are made in the **Equipment Assembler**
compendium.robo_pets.tip: The dog notices dangerous radiation before you do: let it walk ahead before you enter a contaminated hall.
compendium.robo_pets.title: Robo Dog and Robo Cat
compendium.robot_arm.text:
The **robot arm** moves items from a **source** to a **target**. Chests, machines with an item port and conveyor belts from other mods (Create) work. In chip production it carries the parts from machine to machine so you never touch them.
## Two sizes
**Robot arm**: range **3**, one move per second, **600 FE** per move
**Heavy robot arm**: range **5**, one move every **0.5 s**, **2,400 FE** per move
The **amount per move** (1, 4, 16, 32, 64) is set with up to four **robot arm upgrades** in the arm's window
## Setting up
1. Place the arm and connect a cable to power (any side)
2. Click the arm with the **link tool**
3. **Right click** the source, **Shift + right click** the target
4. **Filter** (five slots) in the window if only certain items should move. A redstone signal pauses the arm
## Docked to a machine
If the **arm's target is inside a machine** (clean room), the arm counts as **docked**; it may stand at most 7 blocks away
The **clean room** only runs with a docked arm
Without an arm it stops and waits
Step by step: **Robot Arm Docking**
## Crafting
Robot arm and heavy robot arm are made in the **Reactor Assembler**, upgrade and link tool in the **Small Parts Assembler**
compendium.robot_arm.tip: Chain your machines: the source is the output of the previous machine, the target a block of the next. Then production runs by itself.
compendium.robot_arm.title: Robot Arm
compendium.robot_arm_dock.keywords: dock, docked, docking, no robot arm, NO RECIPE, chip II, chip III, clean room, small parts assembler, link tool
compendium.robot_arm_dock.text:
The **clean room** only works when a **robot arm** is docked to it. Without the arm the machine window shows **NO ROBOT ARM** and nothing is made.
## Which parts need the arm
**Clean room**: everything, so chip III, CPU modules with 32, 64 and 128 cores, RAM modules with 32, 64 and 128 GB
The **Soldering Machine** needs no arm
## How to dock
1. Place a **robot arm** next to the machine, at most **3 blocks** from a machine block (heavy robot arm: 5)
2. Hold the **link tool** and **right-click** the arm. It is now selected
3. **Shift + right-click** a block of the machine. This makes the machine the arm's **target**, small flames rise
4. Done: within 2 seconds the machine starts
## Good to know
For docking the arm needs **no power**, no cable and no data port. All that counts is that its **target** is inside the machine
A **source** is not needed. If the arm should also bring ingredients, set its target on the machine's item input and give it a source (right-click without Shift, for example on a chest). Then it needs power
The arm may stand at most **7 blocks** to the side and **3 blocks** above or below the controller
One arm is enough for one machine
## Common mistakes
**Just placed**: an arm without a target does not count. Only the link tool sets the target
**Clicked without Shift**: right-click without Shift sets the **source**. The machine must be the **target**, so Shift + right-click
**Shift + right-click on the arm**: only opens its window. Select the arm without Shift
**Too far away**: the tool says "Out of the arm's reach". Move the arm closer to the machine
**Target gone again**: a second Shift + right-click on the same target removes it. The arm's window shows whether a target is set
compendium.robot_arm_dock.tip: If the window shows NO ROBOT ARM: take the link tool, right-click the arm, then Shift + right-click the machine.
compendium.robot_arm_dock.title: Robot Arm Docking
compendium.rod_acid.text:
## Acid plant (5×3×4)
Rotary kiln, contact tower and Teflon reactor in one plant, three recipes
**Roasting**: 4 raw ore (iron, copper or lead) → 3 **sulfur dust** and 2 metal dust, 2,400 FE/t (lead 2,700 FE/t), 10 seconds
**Contact process**: 1 sulfur dust + 400 mB water → 500 mB **sulfuric acid**, 1,800 FE/t, 5 seconds
**Hydrofluoric acid**: 1 fluorite + 250 mB sulfuric acid from its own tank → 500 mB **hydrofluoric acid**, 2,100 FE/t, 6 seconds
Ore, sulfur or fluorite **in on top** at the input, dust **out** at the copper orange output, **water in**, acids **out** at the two acid ports (names in the hologram)
The sulfuric acid goes by pipe to the leaching plant, the hydrofluoric acid to the UF6 conversion
When an acid tank is full the plant stands still; the menu shows all three tanks
compendium.rod_acid.tip: Hydrofluoric acid has no bucket, it only moves by pipe. Sulfuric acid needs no assembler recipe any more once the acid plant runs.
compendium.rod_acid.title: Acid plant
compendium.rod_advanced.text:
Above the reinforced casing there are two more tiers. They are stacked like the normal casing, but need a **docker of the same tier** on top.
## Hardened (tier 3)
Lead-gray casing with wide rust-gray grids, docker with shielding collar and bail handle
Reactor assembler: 1 full reinforced casing, 8 lead shielding, 4 HDPE seals
Docker: 1 reinforced docker, 4 control boards II, 4 lead shielding
**7.5 times the steam** from the same charge
## Experimental (tier 4)
Ceramic casing with four narrow grids, docker with instrumentation lance
Reactor assembler: 1 full hardened casing, 8 atomic hull plates, 15 plutonium cores
Docker: 1 hardened docker, 4 control boards III
**12.5 times the steam** from the same charge
## Which docker fits
Normal and reinforced docker: tier 1 and 2 casings
Hardened docker: up to tier 3, experimental docker: every tier
If a casing is too strong, a message says which tier the docker needs
## Good to know
All tiers burn down equally fast, a mined casing keeps its charge
Mixed rods work: every block counts with its own factor
Upgrading needs a full casing, the new casing comes out unloaded; it is loaded like any empty casing (page Fuel rod)
compendium.rod_advanced.tip: Double the heat means double the flow: cooling, feedwater and turbine have to grow with it.
compendium.rod_advanced.title: Hardened and Experimental Fuel Rods
compendium.rod_boric.text:
## Boric acid plant (3×3×3)
Dissolving vessel with a stirrer: 1 **borax** + 250 mB sulfuric acid + 200 mB water → 4 **boric acid**, 1,500 FE/t, 8 seconds
Borax comes from **borax ore** (between Y -16 and 48, needs a stone pickaxe)
Borax **in on top** at the input, boric acid **out** at the copper orange output, **water** and **sulfuric acid** each at their port (names in the hologram)
The sulfuric acid comes from the acid plant
Boric acid goes into the control rod drive by right-click, see water chemistry
compendium.rod_boric.tip: Boric acid is light and cheap, 4 pieces per borax. One stack lasts for very many reactor starts.
compendium.rod_boric.title: Boric acid plant
compendium.rod_build.text:
A fuel rod is made of **4 cladding blocks** and a **docker** on top. The cladding holds the fuel, the docker holds the rod in the drive.
## Building
1. Stack 4 cladding blocks
2. Put the docker on top. If cladding is missing, a message tells you how many
3. Put the finished rod onto the clamp frame of a **fuel rod drive** (section Reactor)
## Fuel rod assembly
Reactor assembler: 16 reactor plates, 15 uranium cores, 8 zircaloy sheets
Gives the normal amount of steam
The **reinforced cladding** gives more steam, see the next page
## Good to know
The normal docker carries tier 1 and 2 casings, tiers 3 and 4 need the matching docker
Full rods glow violet-blue and radiate according to their remaining charge
## Reloading
Reactor assembler: 1 partly burned, empty or unloaded casing + **15 uranium cores** or **9 fuel rods** → the same casing, full
Upgrading to the next tier only works with a **full** casing. The new casing comes out **unloaded**: it does not radiate, gives no steam and is loaded afterwards
compendium.rod_build.tip: Build cooling and water supply first, then insert the rods: a full rod heats up right away.
compendium.rod_build.title: Building the Fuel Rod
compendium.rod_castor.keywords: Castor, cask, transport cask, spent fuel cask, interim storage
compendium.rod_castor.text:
## Castor cask
**Large** (2×3×2 blocks) from the heavy assembler: 36 × 16 places, contents do not radiate and stay inside when mined
Placed starting at the block you aim at, extending east, south and up; needs free space there
With any part next to an item port: feeds rods in, picks cooled fuel up
Mining any part drops the whole cask with its contents
Right-click with a rod inserts it, empty hand shows the contents
**Shift + right-click** with an empty hand picks up the whole cask with its contents, no pickaxe needed
compendium.rod_castor.title: Castor cask
compendium.rod_centrifuge.keywords: enrichment, gas centrifuge, centrifuge, UF6, U-235
compendium.rod_centrifuge.text:
## Enrichment centrifuge (3×4×3)
Four gas centrifuges: 2 yellowcake → 1 enriched uranium and 1 depleted uranium (25 % uranium oxide as well), 240 FE/t, 10 seconds
**UF6 cylinders** from the UF6 conversion plant give more: 1 cylinder → 2 enriched and 1 depleted uranium
Power on the right, yellowcake or UF6 **in on top**, uranium **out** on the left at the bottom
compendium.rod_centrifuge.title: Enrichment centrifuge
compendium.rod_chemlab.text:
## Chemical lab (3×3×3)
Stirred kettle with a heating jacket, the stirrer turns while it works, five recipes
**Lye**: 6 dried kelp + 400 mB water → 500 mB **lye**, 2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds
**Nitric acid**: 4 gunpowder + 300 mB sulfuric acid → 400 mB **nitric acid**, 3,000 FE/t, 12 seconds
**Resin regeneration**: 2 spent resin + 200 mB lye from its own tank → 2 **ion resin**, 2,100 FE/t, 8 seconds
**Etch silicon**: 3 raw silicon + 150 mB hydrofluoric acid + 100 mB water → 3 **pure silicon** (instead of 2 with sulfuric acid), 2,700 FE/t, 12 seconds
**Grease**: 1 lithium ingot + 500 mB **diesel** → 4 **grease**, 2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds
Raw material **in on top**, water, sulfuric acid and hydrofluoric acid (upper row) on the right (seen from the front), lye and nitric acid out on the left, diesel in on the left, top, resin and grease **out** at the chute
## What for
**Lye**: turns spent resin back into fresh resin instead of sending it to the repository
**Nitric acid**: pipe it into the "nitric acid" input of the vitrification plant, which then makes 800 instead of 500 mB of liquid waste per batch
**Grease**: kits of the main coolant pump, high pressure pump and feedwater pump
compendium.rod_chemlab.tip: It only makes what is used: no ammonia as long as nothing needs it.
compendium.rod_chemlab.title: Chemical lab
compendium.rod_drive.keywords: FRD, CRD, fuel rod drive, control rod drive, rod drive, drive, SCRAM, reactor
compendium.rod_drive.text:
The fuel rod drive is the **heart of the reactor**, a large machine (**5×10×5**, machine kit from the heavy assembler): a slim tower, on top nine shaft inlets (3×3) in a collar, below it the **reactor pressure vessel**. All connections sit in the wall. It moves up to nine fuel rods into the vessel, their heat goes into the **core** (page The Reactor Core).
## Inserting a rod
1. Place a fuel rod (cladding + docker) on top of a shaft's **clamp frame**. With the drive inside the **containment**, it sits right under its hatch, and you place the rods in the hatch on top
2. Press **Lock Rod** for that shaft in the terminal: the frame grips the rod
3. Choose a target 0-15: only locked rods move in
4. **Release** raises the rod fully and opens the frame, then you can take it out
## Lamps below the monitor
**green**: all rods locked and clamped
**yellow**: a rod is moving or still free
**red**: no power, no hydraulic water, no rod inserted or no primary water flows through the vessel
## Supply and control
**Power** 60 FE/t (buffer 60,000 FE): without power the rods stay put, the core keeps heating
**Hydraulic water** (back, level 5): every step costs water
**Control signal** in the front wall: redstone 0-15 instead of the terminal
The same **channel** in the terminal links several drives
**Cherenkov glow**: hold right-click with an empty hand, move the mouse left/right, release (0 = off to 15). A short click still opens the menu.
compendium.rod_drive.tip: Right-click the terminal port (front, above the controller) to open the terminal. Hover a card to see insertion and clamp frame opening.
compendium.rod_drive.title: Fuel rod drive
compendium.rod_exchanger.text:
## Ion exchanger (3×3×3)
Two resin columns in a side stream of the primary loop: 1 **ion resin** + 1,000 mB primary water → 1 **spent resin** + 1,000 mB cleaned primary water, 900 FE/t, 20 seconds
Each run takes 35% deposits and 200 ppm boron out of the next **reactor in range**
Resin **in on top** at the input, spent resin **out** at the copper orange output; **primary water** comes from a branch of the primary line and goes back into it
Ion resin comes from the polymer plant (2 rubber + water)
Spent resin is weak waste: the **chemical lab** turns it back into fresh resin with lye, otherwise it belongs in the repository
compendium.rod_exchanger.tip: The side stream is its own line next to the main loop. With the exchanger off the reactor runs on unchanged.
compendium.rod_exchanger.title: Ion exchanger
compendium.rod_foundry.text:
## Foundry (5×3×4)
Furnace with a large casting channel for silicon
4 sand + 1 coal in the extra slot → 2 **raw silicon** (10 s, 3,000 FE/t)
2 pure silicon → 4 **wafers** (10 s, 3,300 FE/t), see page Silicon and Chips
Lead blocks, atomic hull plates, refined glowstone ingots and steel are made in the **blast furnace**, zirconium ingots in the **kiln**
Sand or pure silicon **in on top**, the addition in the **extra slot**, results **out** at the copper orange output below; 3,000 to 3,300 FE/t
compendium.rod_foundry.tip: The foundry makes the silicon for the chips.
compendium.rod_foundry.title: Foundry
compendium.rod_fuel.keywords: MOX, mixed oxide, fuel assembly, uranium core, uranium fuel
compendium.rod_fuel.text:
Fuel is made in several steps:
1. Ore becomes yellowcake in the ore mill
2. Yellowcake becomes enriched uranium in the centrifuge, more efficiently via leaching and UF6
3. Enriched uranium becomes a uranium core in the reprocessing plant or the pellet factory
4. 15 uranium cores and further parts make the fuel rod casing in the reactor assembler
The furnace only turns uranium ore into a uranium fragment, which the ore mill also grinds into yellowcake, but less than the ore
The individual plants are on the next pages
compendium.rod_fuel.tip: The fuel rod assemblies come from the reactor assembler, the uranium cores from the reprocessing plant or the pellet factory.
compendium.rod_fuel.title: Fuel
compendium.rod_gripper.text:
The **Rod Gripper** is a **crane for fuel rods**. It stands **above** a free, vertical column (shaft of the control rod drive, cooling rack) and lowers a **hook** into it. It is controlled by **redstone** only.
## Inputs
Sides are seen from the **window side** (the side with the display faces you when you place it)
**Back**: **Grip**, the hook holds the rod as long as the signal is on
**Left**: **Lift**, one block per step (5 ticks)
**Right**: **Lower**, one block per step
**Top**: **Pull**, the hook runs down to the rod, grips it and pulls it all the way up
## How it works
It grips an **assembled fuel rod** (docker and four blocks) exactly **below the hook**
The rod stays a real stack of blocks, the gripper moves it block by block including its charge
Without a signal on the grip input the hook lets the rod go where it stands
It does not touch rods that are **locked** (clamped) in the drive or cooling rack
On a **Create contraption** it also works while moving, without power; it reads the inputs as redstone at its current place in the world
If the next cell is occupied, the window shows **hook blocked**
One step costs **300 FE**, the buffer holds **30,000 FE**
## Window and data
Right-click shows power, depth, gripper, rod at the hook and the four inputs, plus an on/off button
The block has a data port: depth, gripper and power can be read on the data network, **enable** switches it
## Crafting
In the **Reactor Assembler** from a robot arm, steel sheets, control board II, copper coils, rubber and iron bars
compendium.rod_gripper.tip: Pull finds the rod by itself: the hook runs down to the rod, grips it and pulls it all the way up.
compendium.rod_gripper.title: Rod Gripper
compendium.rod_heavywater.keywords: D2O, heavy water, deuterium oxide, Girdler
compendium.rod_heavywater.text:
## Heavy water plant (3×3×3)
Two exchange towers using the Girdler process, two recipes
**Heavy water**: 1 sulfur + 8,000 mB water → 100 mB **heavy water**, 3,600 FE/t, 20 seconds
**Heavy water cell**: 2 glass seals + 16,000 mB water → 1 **heavy water cell**, 4,500 FE/t, 30 seconds
Sulfur or glass seal **in on top**, cell **out** at the copper orange output, **water in**, heavy water **out** (names in the hologram)
**Fusion**: heavy water at the input of the deuterium separator gives 20 times more deuterium per mB than water
**Moderator**: 30 cells, a fluorite moderator and 4 hull plates make the heavy water moderator in the Reactor Assembler (tier 5, power ×4, heat ×4.2)
Heavy water has no bucket, it only moves by pipe
compendium.rod_heavywater.tip: The plant needs a lot of water and power but little sulfur. One moderator needs 30 cells.
compendium.rod_heavywater.title: Heavy water plant
compendium.rod_leaching.text:
## Leaching plant (5×3×4)
Item plant with a **water and an acid tank**: 2 yellowcake + 250 mB acid + 500 mB water → 2 uranium oxide and with 50 % chance 1 uranium sludge, 1,200 FE/t, 10 seconds
The **sludge** goes through once more: 3 sludge + 100 mB acid + 200 mB water → 1 uranium oxide
Yellowcake **in on top** at the input, results **out** at the copper orange output below; the build preview hologram shows power, water and acid
**Sulfuric acid** comes by pipe from the acid plant or as a bucket from the reactor assembler: right-click the bucket on the acid port
The menu shows both tanks with their level, red when less is in than one run needs
compendium.rod_leaching.tip: Uranium oxide is also the raw material of UF6 conversion. Never throw the sludge away: 2 yellowcake give a little over 2 oxide, and after UF6 conversion and the centrifuge more than twice the enriched uranium of the direct route.
compendium.rod_leaching.title: Leaching plant
compendium.rod_ore_mill.text:
## Ore mill (3×3×4)
Ball mill: 1 ore → 2 yellowcake (25 % a third one), 120 FE/t, 10 seconds
Also grinds **iron, gold and copper ore** (and raw metal) into dust: 1 → 2 dust, 5 % a third; dust smelts into ingots in a furnace
Also **tin, lead and osmium** into NuclearSQ dust
And every other ore except uranium: coal, lapis, redstone, diamond, emerald, quartz, ancient debris, zircon, fluorite, borax, lithium. Same yield as mining, 5 % one more (10 % with one, 20 % with two working overclock modules)
Power on the right (seen from the front), ore **in on top** at the feed hopper, yellowcake **out** on the left at the bottom
compendium.rod_ore_mill.title: Ore mill
compendium.rod_pellets.text:
## Fuel pellet factory (5×3×4)
Rotary table with a press ram and a sintering furnace, two recipes
**Press**: 2 uranium oxide dust + 1 enriched uranium in the extra slot → 3 **uranium pellets**, 1,800 FE/t, 8 seconds
**Sintering furnace**: 2 pellets → 1 **uranium core**, 2,700 FE/t, 12 seconds
That gives **1.5 cores** per enriched uranium, the reprocessing plant gives only one
Dust or pellets **in on top** at the input, enriched uranium in the **extra slot** beside it, results **out** at the copper orange output below
Loading and fuel rod run time stay the same: 15 cores still fill one casing
compendium.rod_pellets.tip: Uranium oxide dust is made in the reactor assembler from 4 uranium oxide and comes out of the reprocessing of cooled spent fuel. The press pays off mostly with the dust from reprocessing.
compendium.rod_pellets.title: Fuel pellet factory
compendium.rod_polymer.text:
## Polymer plant (3×3×3)
Horizontal vulcanizing kettle with a roller at the left end (seen from the front), nine recipes
**Rubber from slime**: 4 slime balls + 1 sulfur in the extra slot + 500 mB water → 4 **rubber**, 2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds
**Rubber from kelp**: 8 dried kelp + 1 sulfur + 500 mB water → 2 **rubber**, 12 seconds
**Rubber seal**: 3 rubber + 1 glass seal in the extra slot → 2 **rubber seals**, 1,800 FE/t, 6 seconds
**Ion resin**: 2 rubber + 500 mB water → 4 **ion resin**, 2,100 FE/t, 8 seconds
**Rubber from tar**: 2 sulfur + 400 mB **tar** from the distillation column → 6 **rubber**, 2,400 FE/t, 10 seconds, no water
**Coke**: 1 coal + 200 mB **tar** → 2 **coke**, 1,800 FE/t, 8 seconds
**Sealing compound**: 2 rubber + 200 mB **tar** → 4 **rubber seals**, 1,800 FE/t, 6 seconds, no glass seal needed
**Photoresist**: 1 sulfur + 250 mB **naphtha** → 4 **photoresist**, 1,800 FE/t, 6 seconds
**HDPE from ethylene**: 1 iron nugget + 1,000 mB **ethylene** from the cracker → 2 **HDPE sheets**, 2,100 FE/t, 12 seconds
Raw material **in on top**, result **out** at the chute on the left, water comes in on the right, **tar** at the back left, bottom, **naphtha** at the front right, bottom, **ethylene** at the front left, bottom (gas port)
## What rubber is for
**Rubber seal**: hazmat suit tier II and respirator mask
**Rubber**: insulation of the hardened power cables
Ion resin for the ion exchanger
**Photoresist** for chip II, **HDPE sheet** for chip III
compendium.rod_polymer.tip: Rubber only exists here, no other mod supplies it.
compendium.rod_polymer.title: Polymer plant
compendium.rod_reinforced.text:
The **reinforced fuel rod assembly** (tier 2) has two extra blue steel bands. It is stacked like the normal one, with the same **docker** on top. The reinforced docker with hold-down springs carries the same casings.
## Making it
Reactor assembler: 1 full fuel rod casing, 8 steel sheets, 4 osmium heat plates
## What it gives
**3.75 times the steam** from the same charge, it burns down just as fast as the normal cladding
More steam means more power, but also more primary water flow, more feedwater and more cooling
## Good to know
Every cladding block counts on its own: normal and reinforced cladding can be mixed in one rod
You can upgrade later, the old cladding is the main ingredient
compendium.rod_reinforced.tip: Reinforced cladding pays off once cooling and water supply have some reserve: same charge, 3.75 times the steam.
compendium.rod_reinforced.title: Reinforced Fuel Rods
compendium.rod_repository.text:
Where does the nuclear waste go? Into the **waste repository** (5×9×5): the cage takes it deep down the shaft, and nothing comes back.
## What goes in
**Spent fuel rods** and **cooled spent fuel**
**Filter residue** from the cooling loop
**Radioactive fallout**
**Glass canisters** from the vitrification plant, **spent resin** and **activated wall tiles**
The intake refuses everything else.
## Operation
1. **Power** into the power port on the side of the base (600 FE/t, only while there is waste)
2. Waste into the **intake** opposite it by hopper or pipe, or click intake or controller with the waste in hand
3. Up to **4 items** go down the shaft every second
Right-click the controller to see how much is stored
Nothing can be taken out: storage is final
compendium.rod_repository.tip: Spent rods do not have to cool in the spent fuel rack first. On the way to the repository, though, carry them in a Castor.
compendium.rod_repository.title: Waste Repository
compendium.rod_slag.text:
## Waste crusher (3×3×3)
Two counter-rotating rollers grind waste into dust and complement the reprocessing plant
3 **nuclear ash** → 2 lead dust, with 75 % chance 1 zirconium dust and with 30 % chance 1 neptunium oxide, 1,200 FE/t, 8 seconds
2 **filter residue** → 1 lead dust and with 50 % chance 1 zirconium dust, 900 FE/t, 6 seconds
Waste **in on top**, dust **out** at the copper orange output
compendium.rod_slag.tip: The dust goes back to the foundry and the assembler recipes: that closes the loop.
compendium.rod_slag.title: Waste crusher
compendium.rod_spent.text:
An empty fuel rod is **spent**: it radiates strongly, even in your inventory.
## Spent fuel rack (3×6×3)
You **build the pool yourself**: a watertight hole, at least 3×3 wide and 11 blocks deep, filled with water.
1. Place the rack (9 shafts, one assembled fuel rod each) at the bottom of the pool
2. Water must keep **flowing** into the **water port** at the bottom (pipe or pump, 10 mB/t while rods are cooling)
3. At least **5 blocks of water** must stand above **each of the 9 shafts**
4. Put a fuel rod on top of a shaft and assemble it, or set it down finished with a crane: the **clamp** grabs it right away and it drives all the way in. After about 5 minutes it has cooled, drives back up and gives **cooled spent fuel** when broken. Loose rod items are not accepted
Without feed or water column: **no cooling**, and the rods radiate strongly
Right-click shows "Feed: ok/missing" and "Water column: n/5", so does the menu
**Cherenkov glow**: hold right-click with an empty hand, move the mouse left/right, release (0 = off to 15). A short click still opens the menu.
compendium.rod_spent.tip: Don't carry spent rods around for long: they are safe inside a castor.
compendium.rod_spent.title: Spent rods
compendium.rod_uf6.keywords: UF6, uranium hexafluoride, conversion, fluorite, hydrofluoric acid
compendium.rod_uf6.text:
## UF6 conversion plant (5×4×4)
Reaction chamber with a carousel: 2 uranium oxide + 1 fluorite → 1 **UF6 cylinder**, 2,400 FE/t, 15 seconds
With **hydrofluoric acid** from the acid plant it works without fluorite: 2 uranium oxide + 300 mB hydrofluoric acid → 1 UF6 cylinder; the acid arrives by pipe at the hydrofluoric acid port
Yellowcake works too: 3 yellowcake + 1 fluorite → 1 UF6 cylinder, without leaching, but dearer
Uranium oxide **in on top** in the input, **fluorite in the extra slot** beside it, cylinders **out** at the copper orange output below, power as in the hologram
In the **centrifuge** 1 UF6 cylinder gives 2 enriched and 1 depleted uranium (and sometimes uranium oxide)
The centrifuge also accepts yellowcake directly (2 yellowcake make 1 enriched uranium), but that yields less
compendium.rod_uf6.tip: Fluorite comes as ore. With hydrofluoric acid from the acid plant the fluorite extra is not needed, the plant takes the recipe whose ingredients are there.
compendium.rod_uf6.title: UF6 conversion plant
compendium.rod_uranium.text:
## Own route
1. **Uranium ore** (also raw uranium or uranium fragment) into the **ore mill**: becomes **yellowcake**
2. 2 yellowcake each into the **enrichment centrifuge**: 1 **enriched uranium**, sometimes uranium oxide as well
3. Each enriched uranium in the **reprocessing plant**: 1 **uranium core**
4. 15 cores load one fuel rod casing: **12 minutes** at full power, a whole rod is made of 4 casings
## More yield
**Leaching plant**: yellowcake with water and acid into uranium oxide, then in the **UF6 conversion plant** with fluorite into UF6 cylinders: the centrifuge gets more uranium out of them
## Building
All of them come as a **machine kit** from the heavy assembler (chapter Machine basics)
Right-click the monitor for input and output, hoppers go on top of the yellow input, chests, hoppers or pipes on the copper orange output
compendium.rod_uranium.tip: NuclearSQ generates its own uranium ore (and lead, tin, osmium, fluorite). Zircon ore generates as well. In areas already explored the particle assembler provides the raw materials.
compendium.rod_uranium.title: Uranium processing
compendium.rod_vessel.keywords: RPV, RDB, reactor vessel, pressure vessel
compendium.rod_vessel.text:
The vessel below the drive is the **reactor pressure vessel** of a pressurized water reactor: the inserted rods heat it and **primary water** flows through it. No steam is made here any more, the steam generator does that later.
**Cold in**: left (seen from the front, east side at rotation 0) in the wall, level 3. Primary water only, tank 32,000 mB
**Hot out**: right (west side) in the wall, level 3. Hot primary water, tank 32,000 mB
**Flux signal** in the back wall: redstone 0-15 by power
## How much flow?
All nine rods together up to **640 mB/t** (a ninth per rod), times insertion depth and remaining charge. Nine full, fully inserted rods: 640 mB/t
1 mB of cold primary water becomes 1 mB of hot, every mB cools the core
Fuel is **only used while primary water flows**: fully inserted 1 charge per tick and rod
Hot primary water is **slightly radioactive**, in pipes too
Primary water has no bucket, it stays in the closed loop
## No flow
If cold primary water runs out or the hot tank is full while rods are heating: no burn-up, red lamp and a warning in the terminal. The core **heats up fast** and can **explode**. SCRAM at once and get the loop running again.
compendium.rod_vessel.tip: The terminal shows the vessel with cold and hot primary water, flow and temperature. The core heat is at the top of the terminal.
compendium.rod_vessel.title: Reactor pressure vessel
compendium.rod_vitrify.keywords: HLW, vitrified waste, glass canister, nuclear waste
compendium.rod_vitrify.text:
## Vitrification plant (3×3×3)
Upright melting furnace with a turntable, four recipes in three steps
**Dissolve**: 8 filter residue + 400 mB sulfuric acid → 500 mB **high-level liquid waste** (HLW), 4,500 FE/t, 15 seconds
**Dissolve**: 4 spent resin + 200 mB sulfuric acid → 200 mB HLW, 3,000 FE/t, 10 seconds
**Vitrify**: 4 sand + 500 mB HLW from its own tank → 1 **glass canister**, 7,500 FE/t, 30 seconds
**Dissolve with nitric acid** (from the chemical lab, input at the front right, seen from the front): 8 filter residue + 200 mB nitric acid → 800 mB HLW, 4,500 FE/t, 10 seconds
**Separate**: 2 ion resin + 200 mB nitric acid + 300 mB HLW from its own tank → 1 **strontium-cesium concentrate** and 2 spent resin, 6,000 FE/t, 20 seconds
Waste and sand **in on top**, sulfuric acid at the back right, canister **out** at the chute on the left
The HLW port on the left also hands the liquid waste out by pipe
## Where it goes
The canister belongs in the **waste repository**
It is strongly radioactive in your inventory: work with a hazmat suit and short ways
compendium.rod_vitrify.tip: Spent resin from the ion exchanger and filter residue from the loop end up here instead of just vanishing down the shaft.
compendium.rod_vitrify.title: Vitrification plant
compendium.rod_water.keywords: Cherenkov, Tscherenkow, spent fuel pool, water
compendium.rod_water.text:
The drive and its vessel can be built and run **fully underwater**
**Fuel rods** glow violet-blue, brighter the fuller they are
With water at most 2 blocks away the blue **Cherenkov glow** joins in, fading out up to 6 blocks
Every rod block **radiates** according to its remaining charge, the Geiger counter shows it
Empty rods no longer radiate, full ones the most
compendium.rod_water.tip: The water around the drive is only looks and building space: the vessel is fed by its primary port alone.
compendium.rod_water.title: Underwater: Cherenkov and radiation
compendium.safety_boom.text:
The big explosion comes two ways: with the detonator or through overheating. If the core of the fuel rod drive stays at 100 % heat for 12.5 seconds, it ignites by itself.
## Overheating
Alarm from 80 %, warning with countdown in the action bar from 100 %
Canceled if heat falls below 90 %
## The explosion
A reactor does not explode like a nuclear bomb: steam and hydrogen blow away the lid, roof and walls of the hall, like in Chernobyl
Destruction **12 blocks** around the spot above the core (default, adjustable with reactorYield in serverconfig/nuclearsq-server.toml), damage up to 30 blocks, fire and debris all around
Water nearby boils away, a steam column rises
The real danger is the **radiation**: the core radiates strongly, radioactive fallout lands far around
compendium.safety_boom.tip: Keep your distance beforehand and save the world. Overheating sets off the same explosion as the button.
compendium.safety_boom.title: The Explosion
compendium.safety_detonator.text:
The button blows up the nearest **fuel rod drive** within **50 blocks** (sphere). It is only in the **creative tab** and works only in **creative mode** or for **operators**.
1. Right-click, then click again within **5 seconds**
2. A **3 second** countdown runs in the action bar (shown to all players nearby)
3. Then the reactor explodes
Also works with Shift + right-click, whatever you hold
Hold **Ctrl** to see whether a fuel rod drive is in range
compendium.safety_detonator.tip: The fuel rod drive must be loaded and assembled. If it is farther away, nothing happens on click.
compendium.safety_detonator.title: The Detonator
compendium.safety_tips.text:
Build the reactor far away from your base
Always leave cooling some reserve: primary water in the loop, feedwater at the steam generator and a powered main coolant pump
Watch the heat in the terminal, not only the steam
Red from 80 %: cool at once or SCRAM
SCRAM pulls all rods of the group
If the flow stops (no cold primary water, no pump, no feedwater, full steam tank), the core heats up
Test new builds in a copy of your world
Collect materials beforehand, the assembler only works with all ingredients
compendium.safety_tips.tip: The progression tree shows what you still need for the next tier.
compendium.safety_tips.title: Tips
compendium.small_parts_assembler.text:
The Small Parts Assembler is a precision workbench (**3×2×3**) with soldering iron and placement arm. It is the **first machine**: it builds the **reactor assembler kit**, the plate mill and the hammer mill with steel, plates, casings and ports and makes the electronics for the storage system, for example **Hard Drive I**.
## Building
1. **Kit** at the **crafting table**: 4 iron blocks, gold, 2 redstone blocks, crafting table and comparator
2. Place it like any kit (hologram, right-click)
## Operation
**960 FE/t** while working (the reactor assembler kit only 480 FE/t, one coal generator is enough), one part takes **5 seconds**, energy storage **300,000 FE**
**Power** and **items in** on the right (seen from the front), **result out** on the left
Right-click the screen at the front to open the terminal with the **3×3 grid**
The position in the grid does not matter, only the amounts
Some parts take longer or need more power
## Chips and precision
**Chain**: foundry (sand and coal make raw silicon), chemical lab (raw silicon and sulfuric acid make pure silicon), foundry (wafers), then chips
**Chip I** and the first RAM and CPU tiers (up to 2 cores and 2 GB) are made by the **micro assembler** (2×2×2). Its kit comes from this assembler
**Chip II**, CPUs with 4 to 16 cores, RAM from 4 to 16 GB and hard drives II to NVMe are made by the **Soldering Machine** (2×2×3, kit from this assembler).
**Chip III**, CPUs from 32 cores and RAM from 32 GB are made only by the **clean room** (3×3×3, with a robot arm, kit from the heavy assembler)
Machines up to the foundry and chemical lab (in achievement order) are built without a chip, including the reactor assembler kit from this assembler. Only later controllers need a **chip**: waste repository (chip I), component, compute and particle assembler, clean room, deuterium separator, electrolyzer, fuel cell and decon dock (chip II), fast breeder, fusion reactor, quantum computer and weapons processing plant (chip III)
compendium.small_parts_assembler.tip: A hopper or pipe at the result port collects the finished parts. If the window shows NO ROBOT ARM, no robot arm is docked: see the page Robot Arm Docking.
compendium.small_parts_assembler.title: Small Parts Assembler
compendium.solder_machine.text:
The **Soldering Machine** (**2×2×3**) is a wave soldering line: boards run through the solder tunnel, the soldering head places the parts, fans and the fume extractor cool and filter the vapour. It takes over the middle tiers from the Small Parts Assembler with the same recipes.
## Only here
Chip II, CPU modules with 4, 8 and 16 cores, RAM modules with 4, 8 and 16 GB
Hard drive II, hard drive III, SSD and NVMe
## Setup
1. Make the **kit** in the **Small Parts Assembler**: 4 advanced reactor casings, 2 control boards I, 2 chips I, one power and one data port, 2 item ports, 4 copper coils and 6 gold
2. Place it like any kit (hologram, right-click)
## Operation
**960 FE/t** while soldering, one part takes **5 seconds**, energy buffer **300,000 FE**
**Power** low on the back of the supply block, **parts in** on top of the feeder, **result out** on the left of the supply block, data cable high on the back of the supply block.
compendium.solder_machine.tip: The Soldering Machine comes after the CNC mill, because its kit needs advanced reactor casings. Without it there is no chip II and no hard drive II.
compendium.solder_machine.title: Soldering Machine
compendium.storage_cluster.text:
The **computing cluster** is a rack machine with built-in compute modules. It gives the data network lots of CPU cores and memory, for example for the **component assembler**: more cores mean more lanes, more RAM means bigger jobs.
## Performance
**32 CPU cores** and **512 GB RAM**, fixed, no upgrades
Consumption: **780 FE/t**
The terminal and the machine monitor show how many cores and how much RAM are being delivered
## Connections
**Data cable** to the cyan data port: then every device on the network sees the performance
**Power** to the red port, without power it delivers nothing
**Cooling water** to the blue port (tank 8,000 mB)
## Heat
Power turns into heat, water carries it away
From heat 500 the CPU performance drops down to 25 %, memory stays full
At 1,000 the machine switches off and only comes back below 700
Without water it does not last long
## Crafting
The **machine kit** is made in the **Reactor Assembler** (CPU and RAM modules, casing, boards, ports)
Right click with the kit shows the hologram, another click builds the machine
compendium.storage_cluster.tip: The values are in cluster_values.json and can be changed with a data pack.
compendium.storage_cluster.title: Computing Cluster
compendium.storage_compute.text:
Consoles and terminals need **computing power**: CPU cores and memory (RAM). Two separate parts provide it, the **CPU module** and the **RAM module**. Both go into a bay of a **server rack** like a hard drive and work while the rack has power. A device only works if CPU **and** RAM are enough.
## The modules
**CPU modules**: eight tiers with 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 cores, 3 to 150 FE/t in the rack
**RAM sticks**: eight tiers with 1 GB, 2 GB, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 GB, 3 to 12 FE/t in the rack
Several modules on the network add up, even in different racks
## And the storage?
RAM is **not storage space** for items, the drives keep their size
But each module takes a **bay** that is then missing for a drive
Its power counts for the rack, without power the rack goes offline with all its drives
The **storage terminal** needs 1 CPU and 16 GB RAM, otherwise it does not open
## Needs
**Data terminal**: 1 CPU, 8 GB
**Command console**: 1 CPU, 16 GB
**Storage terminal**: 1 CPU, 16 GB
**Control wall** (whole wall): 2 CPU, 32 GB
**Control desk**: 2 CPU, 32 GB
**Crafting terminal**: 2 CPU, 32 GB
**Wi-Fi adapter**: 1 CPU, 16 GB
Instruments, controls and computers need nothing
## Not enough
If the power does not cover everything, the devices get their share one after another, the rest stand still
Control wall and control desk then show a red tile with CPU and RAM, the **emergency stop** still works
In the console, **compute** shows what is there and what is missing
## Crafting
In the **Small Parts Assembler**
Each tier is made from the tier below plus extra parts: CPU with gold, quartz, redstone, control boards (diamond from tier 7), RAM with quartz, redstone, copper (gold from 128 GB)
compendium.storage_compute.tip: The values are in storage_values.json. To play without computing power, switch off data.computeRequired in the server config.
compendium.storage_compute.title: CPU and RAM Module
compendium.storage_crafting.text:
The crafting terminal is a **storage terminal with a workbench**: the items of all racks on the left, a 3×3 grid with a result slot on the right.
## Connecting
Like the storage terminal, with **data cable** to the racks or right next to them
**Reactor assembler**: storage terminal, crafting table, steel sheets, control board II, data cable
Needs no power itself, but **2 CPU and 32 GB RAM** on the network (CPU and RAM module in a rack)
## Use
Put items into the grid like at a workbench and take the result
When a grid slot runs empty while crafting, the terminal refills **one piece** of that kind from the racks
**Shift-click the result** crafts as often as ingredients, space and power allow (at most 1,024 times per click). The result goes into the network, what does not fit into your inventory
**Shift-click** a grid slot sends the stack back into the network
**Clear** puts the whole grid back
## Safety
When you close it, everything in the grid goes back: first into the network, then into your inventory, last onto the ground. Even if the terminal loses the connection nothing is lost
compendium.storage_crafting.tip: Without computing power on the network (CPU and RAM) the terminal cannot be opened.
compendium.storage_crafting.title: Crafting Terminal
compendium.storage_crate.text:
The **storage crate** is a crate that grows with you and controls its own sides.
## Size
• **2 blocks wide**, 1 high, 1 deep. It needs a free block to the right of where you place it
• **27 slots** without an upgrade
• **Capacity upgrade I**: 54 slots
• **Capacity upgrade II**: 108 slots
• Only one upgrade fits into the upgrade slot on the right of the window. The crate opens in its new size right away
• An upgrade only comes out if the contents fit into the smaller crate
## Sides
• On the right of the window is the side grid: top, left, front, right, bottom, back (left and right as seen standing in front of the crate)
• **Left-click** steps forward, **right-click** back: **off** (grey), **input** (blue), **output** (orange), **both** (green)
• Pipes, hoppers and robot arms follow the setting. A side that is off offers nothing at all
## Eject
• With the **Eject** switch the crate itself pushes up to 64 items per second through its output sides into the inventory next to it
## More notes
• **Contents and upgrade** stay in the crate when you break it
• Crates with contents (storage crate, quantum chest, shulker boxes) do not fit inside
• The crate shows up in the **data terminal** with used slots, types and the eject switch (enable)
• A comparator reads the fill level
• Needs **no power**
## Crafting
• Crate and both upgrades: **small parts assembler**. Upgrade II needs upgrade I
compendium.storage_crate.tip: For a store with a sorting system: top side on input, bottom on output, eject on.
compendium.storage_crate.title: Storage Crate
compendium.storage_drives.text:
Hard drives store the items. The contents stay on the drive even when you take it out or put it into another rack.
## Tiers
**Hard Drive I**: 4,096 items, 32 kinds, 3 FE/t
**Hard Drive II**: 16,384 items, 48 kinds, 6 FE/t
**Hard Drive III**: 65,536 items, 63 kinds, 12 FE/t
**SSD**: 262,144 items, 63 kinds, 24 FE/t
**NVMe**: 1,048,576 items, 63 kinds, 48 FE/t
## Making them
I in the **Small Parts Assembler**, II to NVMe in the **Soldering Machine**
I: iron, copper, redstone, control board I
II: iron, gold, redstone, quartz, control board I, 2 LCP module casings
III: gold, diamond, redstone block, quartz, control board II, 2 PBT module casings
SSD: diamonds, glowstone, quartz, gold, control board III, 2 HDPE module casings
NVMe: diamonds, glowstone, quartz, gold, control board III, 2 polycarbonate module casings
The module casings come from the **CNC Mill**
Note: The drive's tooltip shows used space and kinds.
compendium.storage_drives.tip: The drive values are in storage_values.json.
compendium.storage_drives.title: Hard Drives
compendium.storage_itemport.text:
The **item port** connects a chest (or any other inventory) to the storage network.
## Setup
Put the plate right against the side of the inventory: chest, barrel, furnace, machine or any block with an inventory
Connect it with a **data cable** to the network that holds the racks (or place it directly at a rack)
The port needs **no power**, the racks on the network do
## Window (right-click without an item)
Button for the **mode**, switch **On/Off**, button **Clear** for the filter and the current status
**5 filter slots**: click with an item to set it, click without an item to clear the slot, you keep the item
## Modes
**Import**: items from the inventory move into the racks. Everything without a filter, only the chosen ones with a filter
**Export**: items come out of the racks into the inventory as long as there is room. Everything without a filter, only the chosen ones with a filter
## Filter without the window
**Right-click with an item** adds it to the filter or removes it again
**Sneak + right-click** without an item clears the filter
## More notes
Up to 64 items per second. A redstone signal pauses the port
**Robot arms, hoppers and pipes** can use the port itself: what they put in is stored, filter items can be pulled out
The port shows up in the **data terminal** with switches for on/off and mode
The port never loads chunks: if the inventory or the network is not loaded it waits
## Crafting
**Reactor assembler**
compendium.storage_itemport.tip: Right-click opens the window: mode, on/off and filter in one place.
compendium.storage_itemport.title: Item Port
compendium.storage_monitor.text:
The Storage Monitor is a wall screen for the storage network: it shows every server rack on the data cable with its storage, and the whole storage at the top.
## Connecting
By **data cable** to the racks' network, or right next to it
Reactor Assembler: steel sheets, glass panes, data cable, control board I, glowstone dust and a chest
## Display
Per rack: drive usage, empty slots as “no drive”
Top: **Racks** with power out of all, and **Total** used of possible
If not all racks fit on screen, it turns the page, every 5 seconds by default
Several monitors side by side (up to **4×4**) form one large screen
A **comparator** reads the fill level of the whole storage
## Window
**Right-click** the screen to open the window
Tab **Racks**: every rack with position, power, priority, usage and drives, plus total storage and kinds
Tab **Display**: sorting (priority, fill level, distance), page turn (5, 10 or 30 s), hide racks without power and the fill level at which the bar turns red
The settings stay saved in the monitor
compendium.storage_monitor.tip: Racks without power or in unloaded chunks are missing from the display.
compendium.storage_monitor.title: Storage Monitor
compendium.storage_pipe_adapter.text:
The **network pipe adapter** connects the storage network to **item pipes**. Ingredients go from the racks straight into the machines and results come back.
## Setup
• At the back sits the blue **data socket**: the data cable from the storage network goes in here
• Opposite at the front sits the yellow **pipe flange**: the item pipe to the machine leaves here, or you put the adapter right against an item port of the machine
• The **panel** on the side shows the mode and the state: green supplies, yellow waits, red network missing
• When placed, the flange points at the block you clicked. Turn it with the **wrench**
• Needs **no power**, the racks on the network do
## Modes (right-click opens the window)
• **Demand**: reads the **recipe pattern** set on the machine at the end of the pipe and sends exactly the missing ingredients in recipe ratio until the slots are full. Items already travelling in the pipe are counted. Without a pattern the adapter waits
• **Store**: accepts everything a pipe pushes in and puts it into the network. This is the way back for results, for example with a pipe set to pull at the machine output
• **Export**: sends up to 5 filter items from the network into the pipe, as fast as the pipe allows. Without a filter the adapter waits. Pipes from other mods can also pick these items up at the pipe side
## More notes
• No buffer, no waiting: items pass in the pipe's rhythm (tier I/II/III: 16, 64 or 256 per second), directly at a machine 64 per second
• Whatever a pipe pushes into the adapter goes into the network in every mode. If an ingredient gets stuck in the pipe it flows back this way
• Pipes from other mods can store through the pipe side. Demand only works with our own item pipes or directly at the machine
• A redstone signal pauses the adapter. It shows up in the **data terminal** with switches for on/off and mode
## Crafting
• **Reactor assembler**
compendium.storage_pipe_adapter.tip: Set a pattern on the machine, then switch the adapter to Demand.
compendium.storage_pipe_adapter.title: Network Pipe Adapter
compendium.storage_racks.text:
Server racks are the heart of the digital storage. There is no controller like in other mods: every rack with power on the data cable is part of the storage network.
## Sizes
**Small** (1×3×2): 6 drive bays
**Normal** (2×4×2): 12 drive bays, made from two small kits
**Large** (4×5×3): 40 drive bays, made from two normal kits
The small kit already comes from the **Small Parts Assembler**, the larger ones from the **Heavy Assembler**
## Connecting
At the back: **power** (red) and **data port** (cyan, like on the control desk)
Base use **24 FE/t**, plus the power of every hard drive
Without power or switched off the rack is **offline**: the items stay on the drives but cannot be reached
## Use
Right-click the front or the data port to open the **bays**
**Priority** 0 to 9: new items go to racks with higher priority first
The model shows every drive with its tier, the **green** LED (ready), **red** (full) and the **yellow** access LED. The fans only spin with power
compendium.storage_racks.tip: When the rack is broken, the hard drives drop out with their contents.
compendium.storage_racks.title: Server Racks
compendium.storage_terminal.text:
The storage terminal shows every server rack on the network as **one** storage. It needs no power itself.
## Connecting
Connect it with **data cable** to the data port or controller of the racks, or place it right next to one
Reactor assembler: steel sheets, glass pane, data cable, control board I and a chest
## Use
**Left-click** takes a stack, **right-click** half
**Shift-click** in the grid puts the stack into your inventory
**Shift-click** in the inventory stores the stack
With an item in hand: **left-click** the grid stores all, **right-click** one
**Search** at the top: part of the name, or **@mod** for all items of a mod
**Sorting** by amount or name
The bottom line shows used space and how many racks have power
compendium.storage_terminal.tip: If the bottom says "racks without power", the racks lack power or are switched off.
compendium.storage_terminal.title: Storage Terminal
compendium.storage_wifi.text:
With the **Wi-Fi adapter** and the **wireless crafting terminal** you reach the storage network without cables.
## Wi-Fi adapter
Block on the **data cable** (or right next to a rack), with the storage network behind it
Needs **power** (12 FE/t, connection on any side) and **1 CPU, 16 GB RAM** on the network. Without power the Wi-Fi is off
**Range 48 blocks**. Antenna modules (right-click the adapter) upgrade it stage by stage, in this order:
**2 antenna modules**: 128 and 320 blocks
**Sector antenna module**: 1,024 blocks
**Directional dish module**: 4,096 blocks
**Quantum antenna module**: **unlimited**, even from other dimensions
Every stage shows on the adapter (mast, sector antennas, dish, quantum core), the lights on the front count the stages
Without the quantum antenna the Wi-Fi works in the **same dimension** only. Adapter and racks must be loaded
**Mesh**: adapters within mutual range (the smaller one counts) connect and pass the Wi-Fi on. An adapter without racks acts as a **relay** at a remote spot and only needs power. The racks stay on the adapter the terminal is linked to
**Charging field**: wireless terminals in the inventory of players up to 4 blocks away charge with up to 200 FE/t
Right-click without an item shows range, stage and buffer. Breaking it drops all modules again
## Wireless crafting terminal
**Right-click the adapter** to link the terminal (sneak + right-click in the air removes the link)
After that **right-click** opens the crafting terminal of the network anywhere in range
**Battery** 40,000 FE: opening costs 100 FE, every crafted recipe 20 FE. Charge in the field or with any charger
If you leave the range, the adapter loses power or is broken, the window closes. Items in the grid go back into the network
## Making them
Adapter: **reactor assembler**
All antenna modules and wireless terminal: **small parts assembler**
compendium.storage_wifi.tip: The values are in wifi_values.json and can be changed with a data pack.
compendium.storage_wifi.title: Wi-Fi Adapter and Wireless Terminal
compendium.survey_drone.text:
The **survey drone** finds spread radiation without you walking into it. It flies over a zone in a snake pattern and measures the dose rate every **2 blocks**, **1 block above the ground**.
## Use
**Right-click** a block with the drone: put it down (this is its start spot)
**Right-click** the drone with the **survey tablet**: bind
**Shift + right-click** two blocks with the tablet: mark the zone (up to **64 x 64**)
**Shift + right-click** the air or the drone: send it off, a second time calls it back
**Right-click** the air: view the **radiation map**
## Fly it yourself
Click **Fly yourself** in the tablet's map window: you see through the drone.
**W A S D** fly, **space** up, **shift** down, the **mouse** turns
Radioactive blocks up to **16 blocks** around the drone are **outlined** in the map colours
The **live map** at the top right grows with you, every cell you fly over is measured
**Right-click** ends the flight, the drone flies back to its start spot by itself and the map goes into the tablet
Radio range **48 blocks**. Without a marked zone it measures **64 x 64** around the start point.
## Map
North is up, the white cross is you. **Green** is background, then **yellow**, **orange**, **red** and from 1 Sv/h **violet**. Point at a cell to see the reading. Black means: not measured yet.
## Battery
**40,000 FE**, flying costs 4 FE per tick. When the battery runs low it comes back early. At its start spot it charges from a power source next to it.
**Shift + right-click** with both hands empty picks it up, the charge stays.
## Crafting
Drone and tablet in the **Equipment Assembler**
compendium.survey_drone.tip: Send the drone first, then go in with the hazmat suit: the map shows where you need the decon tools.
compendium.survey_drone.title: Survey Drone
compendium.the_mod_all.text: Every part of the mod, sorted by the chapters of this book. Drag to move, scroll to zoom, click keeps the links of a part lit, right click opens its page.
compendium.the_mod_all.title: All Items
compendium.tools_nanobots.text:
The **Nano Swarm Canister** sends out one nano bot (the config swarmSize allows up to ten) that takes work off your hands. There is no machine to set up: the bot follows you.
## Controls
**Right-click**: opens the **radial menu**: start and recall, the tasks, gadget (its own ring) and settings (window with radius, status and four upgrade slots). Pick with a left-click, or hold the right mouse button and release it over the field
**Sneak + right-click**: change the task (also while the swarm is running)
The bot also walks on **walls and ceilings** when its target is there: its feet stand on the surface and it visibly turns around edges
Everything is controlled from the canister: task, start and recall, radius and the four upgrade slots; under the slots the menu shows what the upgrades do (speed, bots, largest radius)
One swarm per player. It delivers its cargo when you log out or die
The bot really works: it walks to the block, stands against the face and hacks with its front legs. The block only breaks after the normal breaking time (hardness, best tool from your inventory, at least about 1.5 seconds for stone), the crack progress grows visibly
{drop=Gadget (like the Building Gadget)}
Tab **GADGET** in the menu (or **sneak + right-click** cycles the modes): **break area**, **build / fill**, **replace**
**Right-click a block** sets point 1, a second right-click point 2; a third (or the START button) confirms. A hologram shows the area first: red = break, blue = build, amber = replace
Shapes: cuboid, hull (outer layer only), plane, line and the round **sphere**, **circle** (flat, choose the axis) and **cylinder** (axis and height), solid or hollow. The round shapes need just **one** click (the center); set radius and height in the menu or with **Shift + mouse wheel** (Alt for the height). Building sets the points next to the clicked block
**Copy and paste:** the **COPY** mode selects an area like any shape (round ones too) and remembers all its blocks as a **template** (instant, no bots; the anchor is the lower corner, or the center for round shapes; chest contents are not copied; the template lasts until the server stops). **PASTE** mode: a right-click sets the **anchor**, and a green hologram shows the template at the aimed block beforehand. **R** (Shift + R the other way, or Shift + mouse wheel) rotates in 90° steps, **M** mirrors; the menu has rotation, mirror, **offset** (X/Y/Z: click +1, Shift +4, right-click subtracts, middle-click resets) and the mode **AIR ONLY** (fills free cells only) or **REPLACE** (breaks what is there). Each block uses the block's item from your inventory or the port (stairs, doors and pillars rotate along); UNDO and REDO work here too
Build and replace take the block in your **off hand** as the template; the material comes from your inventory or (switch PORT) from the coupled **Drone Item Port**, i.e. the digital storage of the data network. Creative players need neither material nor power
The bots work the order visibly block by block, bottom to top and near to far. **UNDO** (key Z) takes back the last order: built blocks vanish and the material is refunded, **broken blocks are restored** (the drops are taken out of your inventory again as far as they are still there). **REDO** (key Y) runs the undone order again. The history remembers the last orders (config gadgetHistory, default 10) until the server stops; contents of chests and other block entities do not come back
**Order of work:** breaking always goes from **top to bottom** (top layer first, near before far), building, filling and pasting always from **bottom to top**. If the bots cannot reach the top layer (rock or walls all around), they first dig a **vertical tunnel** (config tunnelDigging, at most tunnelMaxBlocks blocks); the tunnel blocks do not count towards the order, are not refilled (undo restores them) and deliver their drops like everything else. If that is impossible (protected, unbreakable, too long), the order reports **No way up**
Limits: at most 4,096 blocks (config gadgetMaxBlocks), inside the canister radius (reach upgrade), loaded chunks only, spawn protection, game mode and protection mods apply
{/drop}
{drop=Upgrades (reactor assembler)}
**Speed I to V**: walking speed, swarm flight, approach and work time x2 / x3 / x4 / x5 / x7 (the minimum work time of hard blocks and the per-tick break budget stay)
**Count I to V**: 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 bots; each works alone on its own target (more bots = more parallel targets, never two on the same block, surplus bots accompany the swarm)
**Reach I to V**: the radius in the menu may grow by 8 / 24 / 40 / 60 / 80 blocks (at most 128, near tasks half of it)
They go into the four slots of the menu, the highest level of each type counts
{/drop}
{drop=Tasks}
**Fell tree**: the nearest tree in range, it first clears the leaves right against the trunk, bottom to top (so it can climb the trunk, config leavesClear), then the trunk falls from top to bottom. Wooden buildings without natural leaves are left alone. The other leaves decay on their own (can be broken too in the config)
**Collect items**: items lying around in range, but not right next to you
**Mine ore vein**: the whole vein. You need a suitable pickaxe in your inventory (it is not worn down, its enchantments count)
**Plant saplings**: takes saplings from your inventory and plants them spaced apart on dirt
**Harvest**: ripe crops nearby (12 blocks), the seed is sown again right away
**Till fields**: soil with water within 4 blocks becomes farmland. You need a hoe in your inventory (it is not worn down)
**Mine stone**: the nearest exposed stone within 12 blocks (walls, mountains, ceilings, also the ground layer, but never the platform under you), then the connected mass. You need a pickaxe in your inventory
**Decontaminate**: sucks up contamination within 12 blocks of you, spot by spot like one puff of the decon sprayer. Good for corners, stairs and rooms the decon robot cannot reach. Active sources (fuel rods, running machines) stay
{/drop}
## Power and cargo
The **Exo Core** must be somewhere in your inventory. Without it the bots return (20 FE per work step from the core; pocket batteries recharge it)
The bots work from target to target and keep the cargo on board; it is delivered when it is full (8 stacks, config cargoLimit), there is nothing left to do, or you recall them. Nothing is lost. If your inventory is full, the rest drops at your feet
Blocks are broken in your name: protection and claim mods apply to the bots as well
compendium.tools_nanobots.tip: A swarm of nano bots fells trees, mines ore, collects items, plants saplings, harvests, tills fields and mines stone. It needs an Exo Core in your inventory.
compendium.tools_nanobots.title: Nano Swarm
compendium.transport_battery.text:
Batteries buffer power, e.g. to start the pumps or to keep solar power for the night. They come as machine kits and are placed like the big plants.
## Sizes
**Small** (2×2×2): 4M FE, 4,000 FE/t per connection
**Medium** (2×4×2): 16M FE, 16,000 FE/t per connection
**Large** (3×5×3): 64M FE, 131,072 FE/t per connection
## Connections
From the factory **power in** on one side and **power out** on the other; the large battery has a second pair at the back
In the **terminal** (right-click the monitor at the bottom right) you switch each connection off (click) or turn it into an input or output (right-click)
The **data port** for data cables and computers sits on the roof
**Redstone mode** for the outputs: always, only with signal or only without signal
The charge display at the front fills in eighths, the fans spin while charging and draining
## Regulator
The **terminal** has four thresholds in percent, each with hysteresis (click left/right, mouse wheel, Shift = 1 %):
• **Charge until**: above it the battery takes nothing more, the power flows on to other batteries and consumers
• **Charge below**: only below it does it charge again
• **Lock below**: below it the outputs give nothing, this is your reserve
• **Release from**: only above it does it give power again after a lock
From the factory 100/100 and 0/0, so the battery behaves as before. Tip: batteries near the source on **Charge until 50 %** so distant consumers get the rest; batteries at the consumer with **Lock below 0 %**
## Dismantling
With the wrench: the kit comes back and **keeps the charge**
compendium.transport_battery.tip: Chain batteries: output of one into the input of the next.
compendium.transport_battery.title: Batteries
compendium.transport_cables.text:
Cables carry **power (FE)** from generators to consumers and batteries.
## Tiers
**Basic**: 4,096 FE/t
**Reinforced**: 32,768 FE/t
**Hardened**: 524,288 FE/t
**Superconducting**: 33,554,432 FE/t, power cable only, for the fusion reactor
## Behavior
Cables connect automatically to cables and to anything that stores power
At machines a **terminal box** marks the connection; horizontal cables rest on a cable tray
Power goes **to all devices at the same time**, machines and batteries fill evenly
With the wrench you disconnect a side (right-click) or dismantle (shift)
## Mounting
Cables stick to **floors, walls or ceilings**, whichever face you click
Clicking an existing cable continues the run in the same orientation
Wall and floor cables (or wall and ceiling) run around an **inner edge** with tray and clamps
Where two runs in other orientations meet, a **terminal box** joins them
## Grid isolator
The **grid isolator** sits between two cables and separates the network behind it from the one in front: power enters at the **back (blue)** and leaves at the **front (green)**, never backwards
In the **terminal** (right-click) you set the **throughput limit** and four thresholds with hysteresis: charge below, charge until, lock below, release from
So important consumers get their own network with their own reserve; the wrench turns the direction
compendium.transport_cables.tip: Cables and pipes never connect to each other. You can lay them side by side.
compendium.transport_cables.title: Power cables
compendium.transport_frame.text:
The **conduit frame** runs a conduit through walls and ceilings without a visible hole.
## Insert a conduit
**Right-click the frame with a cable, pipe, item pipe or data cable** to insert it. It connects to neighbours and machines as usual
Or the other way round: **right-click a laid conduit with the conduit frame** to build the frame around it
Each frame holds **one** conduit
## Choose the look
**Right-click with a full block** (stone, bricks, concrete, wood …) to give the frame its look. The block is not used up
Where the conduit comes out, a small coloured **port** sits on the face: blue pipe, yellow item pipe. Power and data cables in front of it attach their usual junction box to the wall
**Sneak with an empty hand** and right-click to remove the look again
The wrench switches the sides like on any conduit
## Breaking
The frame gives back the conduit and the conduit frame
compendium.transport_frame.tip: The look is free: the block in your hand is not used up.
compendium.transport_frame.title: Conduit Frame
compendium.transport_grid.text:
Power over long distances without laying cable.
## Setup
